title: Duplicate mod archive breaks --all-features
notify_insert missing on HnswStrategy (ann)
batch-ingest opens existing DB read-only then attempts writes — always fails
description: When `--create` is not passed, `run()` calls `open_engine(db)` (line 305), which sets `config.read_only = true` (db.rs:39). The engine is then used to call `engine.add_facts_batch()` (lines 232, 250) which routes through `write_conn() -> pool.try_write()` and returns `MemoryError::ReadOnly` for every batch. Each batch is counted as a failed batch, `total_skipped` accumulates all records, and `anyhow::bail!` fires at line 270 with "no facts ingested". The non-`--create` path — the primary use-case for ingesting into an existing database — is completely non-functional.
_verified: VERIFIED: else-branch open_engine(read_only=true) then add_facts_batch writes; open_engine_writable exists

title: remove_node leaves node_map with a stale NodeIndex for the displaced node after petgraph's swap-remove
description:
petgraph::DiGraph::remove_node uses swap-remove semantics (documented in petgraph 0.7.1 src/graph_impl/mod.rs:639 and 668): removing the node at NodeIndex(k) moves the last node (at NodeIndex(N-1)) into position k. MemoryGraph::remove_node correctly removes fact_id from node_map, but never updates the map entry for the displaced fact whose NodeIndex just changed from N-1 to k.

Every subsequent operation that calls node_map.get(&displaced_fact_id) → stale_idx → self.graph[stale_idx] is broken:
- has_node(displaced_fact) returns true (node_map still has the key) — false sense of safety
- degree(displaced_fact) and neighbors(displaced_fact) call neighbors_directed(stale_idx, …) and return data for whatever fact now occupies stale_idx, or return 0/empty if stale_idx is out-of-range
- connected_component(displaced_fact) starts BFS from the wrong node and may silently corrupt importance scores and query results
- ensure_node(displaced_fact) returns the stale NodeIndex; any add_edge call wires the new edge to the wrong graph node, producing invisible write-side data corruption
- remove_edges_by_fact(displaced_fact) removes edges from the wrong node

The call site in engine/archive.rs:84-87 loops over fact_ids (≥100 facts, the ArchivePolicy default) calling remove_edges_by_fact then remove_node for each. Every iteration after the first operates on a corrupted node_map. The archive feature makes this reachable in production.
references: src/engine/archive.rs:84-87 (primary call site — loop over ≥100 fact_ids)
_verified: VERIFIED real by source; DORMANT — only caller engine/archive.rs:86 is #[cfg(feature=archive)] (blocked by #1), so cannot fire until archive compiles

title: Orphan .pak.tmp file on serialization or encoder-flush failure
description: In `write_pak_and_hash`, if `serde_json::to_writer` or `encoder.finish()` returns an error, the function early-returns via `?` but the temp file (`path.with_extension("pak.tmp")`) already exists on disk and is never deleted. Repeated failures accumulate stale `.pak.tmp` files in the archive directory. The atomic write guarantee (tmp+rename) only protects against a half-written final file, not against cleanup of the temp file itself on the failure path.

title: Orphan .pak file on commit_archive failure leaves unregistered pak on disk
description: The archive orchestration sequence is: (1) `write_pak_to_disk` (writes and renames `.pak`), then (2) `commit_archive` (SQLite manifest insert + hard-delete in one transaction). If `commit_archive` fails after step 1, the `.pak` file exists on disk but has no manifest row and the facts are still in the live DB. On the next `archive()` call with the same policy, the same candidates are selected again and a second `.pak` is written with a different timestamp filename — the first pak is never registered and accumulates as an orphan. Over time, disk space is silently leaked. There is no recovery or orphan-detection mechanism.
suggested_fix: Add a pre-commit cleanup step: before writing the new pak, scan the archive directory for `*.pak` files not referenced in the manifest table, log and optionally delete them. Alternatively, register a provisional manifest row (with a `status='pending'` column) before writing the pak file, then upgrade it to `status='committed'` inside the SQLite transaction that also hard-deletes the facts; abandoned rows with `status='pending'` can be cleaned up on engine open.

title: Stale in-memory importance_score causes incorrect inheritance in multi-duplicate chains
description: After `fact_store.update_importance_score(survivor.id, loser.importance_score)` (line 102), the survivor's `importance_score` field in the in-memory `active_facts` Vec is NOT updated. Subsequent comparisons in the outer `new_facts` loop that involve the same survivor as a candidate use its stale in-memory value. Concrete scenario with three near-duplicates A (score=0.3), B (score=0.8), C (score=0.5), all equal base importance, ids A < B < C: (1) new_fact=A vs candidate=B → expire B, B.score(0.8) > A.score(0.3) → DB update A to 0.8, but A.score in memory stays 0.3. (2) new_fact=A vs candidate=C → expire C, C.score(0.5) > A.score(0.3 stale) → DB update A to 0.5, overwriting the correct 0.8. Final DB importance_score for A is 0.5, but the correct max-of-all is 0.8. The existing test `survivor_inherits_max_importance` only exercises the two-fact case and does not catch this.
suggested_fix: Maintain a `HashMap<i64, f64>` (indexed by fact id) alongside `expired_ids` to track the running maximum importance_score for each survivor within the loop. Replace the in-memory read `survivor.importance_score` with a lookup in that map before deciding whether to issue the DB update. Alternatively, use a mutable Vec of (id, importance_score) tuples that is updated in place when a survivor gains a higher score. The same stale-read concern applies to `importance` (via `update_importance` at line 99), though in that case the condition is structurally unreachable given that `expire_id` is always the lower-importance fact — verify and document this invariant, or guard symmetrically.

title: embed_batch() does not handle the direct `embedding` response format that embed() supports
description: The struct-level doc (line 7) claims the provider auto-detects three response formats: OpenAI (`data[].embedding`), Ollama (`embeddings[]`), and direct (`embedding`). `embed()` (lines 145-158) handles all three. `embed_batch()` (lines 216-230) only handles the first two; a server that responds with `{"embedding": [...]}` to a batch call is silently rejected with "cannot extract embeddings from batch response" even though the same server works fine with single calls. This produces a confusing, latent runtime failure whenever a caller upgrades from single to batch ingestion against such a server.

title: Byte-indexed String slice `&body_str[..1000]` panics on multi-byte UTF-8 characters at the boundary
description: At line 222-224, `body_str[..1000]` performs a byte-indexed slice on a `String`. If the response body contains a multi-byte UTF-8 character whose first byte falls before byte 1000 and whose continuation bytes fall at or after byte 1000, Rust panics with "byte index is not a char boundary". OpenAI and Ollama response bodies can contain Unicode content (e.g. model names, embedded text excerpts, error messages) in any field that appears near the 1000-byte mark. This is a runtime panic in an error-reporting path, meaning the caller gets an unhandled panic instead of a structured `MemoryError`. `floor_char_boundary` (the idiomatic fix) is only stable from Rust 1.91, but the workspace MSRV is 1.85.
references: CWE-119 (improper restriction of operations within bounds)

title: Orphaned .pak file on commit_archive failure
description: In archive(), write_pak_to_disk() writes the .pak file to disk (line 65), then commit_archive() is called with ? (line 72). If commit_archive fails (DB error, disk-full, etc.), the .pak file is left permanently on disk with no manifest entry and no cleanup. This is a latent disk-leak: subsequent verify_archives() calls will fail to reconcile the orphan. The restore.rs module handles the same pattern correctly via let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&config.path) in its error paths (restore.rs:127).
suggested_fix: Capture the pak path before calling commit_archive, then add an on-error cleanup: let pak_path = config.path.clone(); self.commit_archive(...).inspect_err(|_| { let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&pak_path); })?;

title: Promotion failure silently swallowed, caller sees Recorded status
description: The Err(_) arm at line 131 swallows all errors from add_fact during activity promotion (DB errors, embedding dimension mismatches, read-only violations, etc.) and returns ActivityStatus::Recorded. The caller's RecordActivityResult has promoted_fact_id: None and status: Recorded with no signal that a promotion was attempted and failed. Even in a best-effort design, zero observability means silent data loss goes undetected in production. The bound variable is _ so the error is not even inspectable.
suggested_fix: Bind the error and emit a tracing span: Err(e) => { tracing::warn!(error = %e, tool = %req.tool_name, "activity promotion to fact failed"); ActivityStatus::Recorded }

title: flush_insights accepts unbounded insights array from untrusted MCP caller
description: The `handle_flush_insights` handler reads the `insights` array directly from client JSON with no `maxItems` cap — neither in the JSON schema definition (`all_tool_definitions`) nor in the handler logic. An untrusted MCP client can send an arbitrarily large array; the handler iterates every element, allocates `AddFactRequest` objects, embeds each via the HTTP provider, and inserts them all within a single `spawn_blocking` call. This creates a CPU/memory/network DoS vector bounded only by the tokio blocking thread pool timeout and available RAM. The JSON Schema for `memory_flush_insights` has no `maxItems` constraint.
suggested_fix: Add a server-side cap (e.g., 1000 items) at the start of `handle_flush_insights`: `if insights.len() > MAX_FLUSH_BATCH { return Err(ErrorData::invalid_params("insights exceeds maximum batch size", None)); }`. Also add `"maxItems": 1000` to the JSON schema property for `insights` in `all_tool_definitions`.

title: bootstrap_session accepts unbounded jsonl_data string from untrusted MCP caller
description: `handle_bootstrap_session` reads `jsonl_data` from client JSON (line 1225) with no length limit, then materializes it entirely into a `Cursor<Vec<u8>>` via `jsonl_data.into_bytes()` at line 1239. A multi-MB or multi-GB string allocates an equivalent byte buffer on the blocking thread pool before any processing begins. The JSON schema for `memory_bootstrap_session` has no `maxLength` constraint on `jsonl_data`. There is no streaming: the entire buffer is held in memory for the duration of the bootstrap operation.
suggested_fix: Add a maximum size check before `into_bytes()`: `if jsonl_data.len() > MAX_JSONL_BYTES { return Err(ErrorData::invalid_params("jsonl_data exceeds maximum size", None)); }`. Also add `"maxLength"` to the JSON schema property. For large-data use cases, consider accepting a filesystem path to the JSONL file rather than an inline string.

title: idx_activities_dedup index column count diverges between fresh install and migration path
description: TABLES_DDL (line 819) defines `idx_activities_dedup ON activities(session_id, tool_name, args_hash, outcome_class)` — 4 columns. migrate_v8_to_v9 (line 687) defines it as `ON activities(session_id, tool_name, args_hash, outcome_class, scope_id)` — 5 columns. A freshly-initialized database gets the narrower index; a migrated database gets the wider one. The indexes have different selectivity and serve different query shapes. Any deduplication query that relies on scope_id being part of the index will miss the optimization on fresh installs, and vice versa. Silent behavioral divergence between new and upgraded deployments.
suggested_fix: Decide the canonical index definition and apply it in both TABLES_DDL and migrate_v8_to_v9. If scope_id belongs in the index (wider), add it to TABLES_DDL line 819. If not, remove it from the migration. Then add a regression test that initializes via init_schema and a test-migrated DB and asserts both have the same index definition via `PRAGMA index_info(idx_activities_dedup)`.
_verified: VERIFIED: migrate line687=5cols(+scope_id) vs TABLES_DDL line819=4cols

title: `ArchivePak` has no constructor and `read_pak` does not validate `pak_version`
description: Current state: `ArchivePak` is a plain pub struct with all fields public. `read_pak` at pak.rs:58-67 deserializes any JSON without checking `pak_version`. A `.pak` file written by a future version with a different layout will silently deserialize as v1 with wrong data rather than returning an informative error. Additionally, callers can construct arbitrary `ArchivePak` values (including nonsensical `pak_version: 0`) without going through a validated path. Target state: (1) add version validation in `read_pak`: `if pak.pak_version != CURRENT_PAK_VERSION { return Err(MemoryError::Archive(format!("unsupported pak version: {}", pak.pak_version))); }`. (2) Consider sealing direct field construction behind a `ArchivePak::new(...)` constructor or making `pak_version` / `engine_schema_version` / `embed_dim` non-`pub`, exposed only via getters. Refactoring pattern: Validate on Deserialize + Constructor Encapsulation. Motivation: misuse-resistance — prevents silent data corruption on format evolution. Estimated scope: src/archive/types.rs, src/archive/pak.rs (2 files); also the 2 test helpers that construct `ArchivePak` directly. Prerequisites: finding #design-pak-version-magic-literal (the constant must exist first). Risk: medium — sealing fields is a public API break if the struct was re-exported and used externally; the struct is behind `pub(crate) mod archive` (lib.rs:36) so the API break is limited to crate-internal users.

title: Three parallel fact-type converters mapping `FactType` variants: two enums and one stringly-typed inline match
description: Current state: `FactTypeArg` (add_fact.rs:12-27) and `JsonlFactType` (batch_ingest.rs:63-78) are separate enums with identical structure and identical `From<_> for FactType` implementations. A third site (query.rs:89-98) uses an inline `match ft.to_lowercase().as_str()` with an `anyhow::bail!` fallback — a fully stringly-typed approach that re-implements the same three-way mapping without compile-time safety. `memory_engine::FactType` has no `FromStr` or `ValueEnum` impl (confirmed by grep of src/types.rs), so CLI-local wrappers are necessary — but three of them for the same three variants is avoidable duplication. Target state: one shared `#[derive(ValueEnum, Deserialize)] enum CliFactType` in `commands/mod.rs` (or a new `commands/types.rs`), with both a `From<CliFactType> for FactType` impl and `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` to satisfy both the clap and serde consumers. `query.rs` drops the stringly-typed inline match and uses `CliFactType::from_str` via clap. Refactoring pattern: Extract Superclass / Consolidate Duplicate Conditional Fragments. Motivation: DRY, single point of change when adding a new `FactType` variant, removes the last stringly-typed fact-type path. Scope: 3 files (add_fact.rs, batch_ingest.rs, query.rs) + 1 new/modified shared file. Prerequisites: none beyond the refactor. Risk: low — mechanical variant renaming; serde `rename_all` must match existing JSONL fixture format.

title: 11 of 12 source files lack any inline tests — critical paths entirely untested
description:
Only `batch_ingest.rs` has an `#[cfg(test)]` block (covering 11 cases). The remaining 11 files have no tests at all:
- `output.rs`: `truncate_str` has a multi-byte UTF-8 safety comment (line 16) but no test exercising characters wider than 1 byte (e.g. emoji, CJK) or the boundary at exactly `max_chars`.
- `db.rs`: `peek_embed_dim` has two branches (file-not-found path and missing-key path) that are untested.
- `embedding.rs`: `PassthroughEmbedder::embed_batch` error path (batch size != 1) is untested.
- `commands/query.rs`: the inline `match ft.to_lowercase().as_str()` fact-type parser has no test for the `anyhow::bail!` error path.
- `commands/add_fact.rs`: metadata JSON validation branches (array/string/number/bool rejection) are untested.
The integration test suite in `tests/` may cover some of these via CLI invocations (dev-deps include `assert_cmd`, `tempfile`), but the unit-level paths listed above are structurally untestable at the integration level without embedding a real SQLite database. Recommendation: add unit tests for `truncate_str` (UTF-8 boundary, exact max_chars, empty string), `PassthroughEmbedder::embed_batch` error path, and `validate_jsonl_fact` edge cases.

title: Magic usize::MAX sentinel encodes 'skipped' status in numeric return value
description: Current state: `local_dedup` returns `Ok((usize::MAX, vec![]))` when the corpus exceeds `MAX_DEDUP_FACTS`, using a sentinel numeric value to communicate 'skipped' status to the caller. The orchestrator (`mod.rs:55-57`) then checks `duplicates_removed == usize::MAX`, decodes the sentinel back to 0, and introduces a parallel `dedup_skipped: bool` to gate the watermark advance. This is a stringly-typed/magic-value anti-pattern: the semantics are invisible in the type, the sentinel is incompatible with any future count ≥ `usize::MAX - 1`, and the decoding logic is split across two files. Target state: replace `(usize, Vec<i64>)` with an enum `enum DedupOutcome { Ran { removed: usize, expired_ids: Vec<i64> }, Skipped { active_count: usize } }`. The orchestrator pattern-matches the result; the `Skipped` arm carries diagnostic context (`active_count`) and the watermark logic becomes an explicit match arm with no decoding arithmetic. Refactoring pattern: Replace Magic Number with Type. Motivation: correctness (magic value collides with legitimate count), readability (intent hidden from call site), testability (can assert `Skipped` variant without knowing the sentinel). Scope: 2 files (`dedup.rs`, `mod.rs`). Prerequisites: full test coverage of the dedup-skipped path (existing tests do not cover it). Risk: medium — touches the return signature of a `pub(crate)` function.

title: global_integration constructs fake Fact structs from Summary to satisfy SummaryGenerator trait
description: Current state: `global_integration` must feed cluster `Summary` objects to `SummaryGenerator::summarize(&[Fact])`. Because the trait only accepts `&[Fact]`, lines 35-57 synthesize an 18-field `Fact` per summary, hard-coding `content_hash: String::new()`, `importance: 1.0`, `importance_score: 0.5`, `access_count: 0`, `t_valid: None`, `t_invalid: None`, `is_pinned: false`, and `metadata: serde_json::json!({})`. This is a leaky abstraction: internal `Fact` fields that are semantically meaningless in this context (bi-temporal timestamps, pinning, hash) pollute the call. Worse, if `Fact` grows a new required field (it has no `#[non_exhaustive]`), this site silently breaks by compiling with a wrong value. Target state: either (a) add `fn summarize_summaries(&self, summaries: &[Summary]) -> Result<String>` to `SummaryGenerator` with a default impl delegating to `summarize` via the same pseudo-construction (keeps backward compat), or (b) refactor `summarize` to accept `&[SummarizableItem]` where `SummarizableItem` is a minimal data struct `{ content: String, embedding: Vec<f32> }` used by both callers. Option (b) is the right zero-compromise solution. Refactoring pattern: Introduce Intermediate Abstraction / Replace Implicit Convention with Type. Motivation: correctness (phantom field values), maintenance safety (struct growth breaks silently), coupling (global.rs imports the full `Fact` type to produce a dummy). Scope: 3 files (`global.rs`, `traits.rs`, `cluster.rs` secondary). Prerequisites: trait is `pub`; any change is a breaking API change for existing `SummaryGenerator` implementors. Risk: high — breaking trait change; requires deprecation strategy.

title: Glob re-export of error module creates implicit public API surface
description: Current state: `pub use error::*;` at lib.rs:52 re-exports the entire `error` module wholesale, including `MemoryError`, the `Result` alias, and any future items added to error.rs. Target state: explicit named re-exports `pub use error::{MemoryError, Result};`. Refactoring pattern: Replace glob re-export with explicit item list. Motivation: coupling — every new item added to error.rs becomes an implicit public API change with no compiler warning; glob re-exports also create two canonical paths to the same types (`crate::MemoryError` and `crate::error::MemoryError`), which confuses rustdoc, IDEs, and callers trying to `use` the type. Estimated scope: 1 file (lib.rs), plus updating any downstream imports that relied on the ambiguous double-path. Prerequisites: audit that no downstream code uses `crate::error::MemoryError` vs `crate::MemoryError` inconsistently. Risk: low — mechanical substitution, no behavior change.
suggested_fix: Replace `pub use error::*;` with `pub use error::{MemoryError, Result as MemoryResult};` (or keep `Result` alias if the shadowing of `std::result::Result` is intentional and documented).

title: Glob re-export of types module exposes ~30 types without an explicit contract
description: Current state: `pub use types::*;` at lib.rs:58 re-exports all ~30 public structs, enums, and type aliases from types.rs unconditionally. Target state: explicit named re-exports listing every consumer-facing type. Refactoring pattern: Replace glob re-export with named item list. Motivation: maintainability — adding any internal helper type to types.rs immediately becomes public API; reviewer diffing a PR cannot tell which additions are intentional API additions vs implementation details; semver reasoning is impossible. Estimated scope: 1 file (lib.rs) plus types.rs. Prerequisites: none — this is pure enumeration. Risk: low — no behavior change, but the list will be long (~30 items) and must be kept in sync when types are added.
suggested_fix: Replace `pub use types::*;` with an explicit list such as `pub use types::{Event, EventType, Fact, FactType, NewEvent, NewFact, Edge, NewEdge, Summary, NewSummary, ScopeNode, ScopeQuery, AddFactOptions, AddFactRequest, Insight, CycleReport, DreamCycleConfig, PromotionProvenance, LineageRecord, NewLineageRecord, LineageSnapshotEntry, FactId, LineageId, PromoteRequest, PromotionResult, OutcomeCounts, Outcome, ConsolidationLevel, Activity, NewActivity, RecordActivityRequest, RecordActivityResult, ActivityStatus, SessionCheckpoint, ProjectContext};`

title: `Fact` has two importance fields with near-identical names but different semantics
description: Current state: `Fact` (types.rs:133) has `pub importance: f64` (the caller-supplied base seed stored at insert time) and `pub importance_score: f64` (the materialized computed score updated by the forgetting pipeline). The distinction is confirmed by store/facts.rs:95 comment `// seed importance_score from base importance` and the existence of `update_importance_score` vs no `update_importance`. Target state: rename to make semantics self-documenting — `importance_seed: f64` or `base_importance: f64` for the caller hint, and retain `importance_score` for the computed materialized value. Refactoring pattern: Rename field for semantic clarity. Motivation: readability and coupling — callers reading the struct see two `f64` fields whose difference is not apparent without reading engine internals; the forgetting pipeline uses `importance_score` for decay comparisons (engine/query.rs:241) but `Fact.importance` is also read by engine tests (engine/tests.rs:400, 470), making it easy to confuse the two when writing new queries or forgetting logic. Estimated scope: types.rs, store/facts.rs, engine/ingest.rs, and all test sites (5-8 files). Prerequisites: decide on the canonical rename before touching call sites. Risk: medium — pure rename, no semantic change, but touches many files.
suggested_fix: Rename `Fact.importance` to `Fact.base_importance` (and `NewFact.importance` to `NewFact.base_importance`) everywhere in the workspace. Update the SQL column name in a schema migration if the DB column is also named `importance`.

title: HTTP request/response plumbing duplicated verbatim between `embed` and `embed_batch`
description: Current state: Both `embed()` (lines 117-165) and `embed_batch()` (lines 188-230) independently build the request (`client.post(&self.endpoint).json(...)`), attach auth (`bearer_auth`), call `.send()`, check HTTP status, parse the body as `serde_json::Value`, then branch on response format. These two blocks share ~35 lines of identical structure, differing only in the JSON payload and the extraction branch. Target state: Extract a private `fn send_request(&self, payload: serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, MemoryError>` method that handles client.post, auth, send, status check, and body parse. Both `embed` and `embed_batch` call this helper and then handle format detection on the returned `Value`. Refactoring pattern: Extract Method. Motivation: DRY — a bug fix (e.g. a new error class from reqwest, a retry, a header) must be applied in two places. Coupling: self-contained within `http.rs`. Testability: improved (the transport layer is separately testable/mockable). Risk: low. Estimated scope: 1 file.

title: Implementation submodules exposed as `pub` despite no external callers
description:
All five implementation submodules (`dump`, `explain`, `replay`, `restore`, `statistics`) are declared `pub mod` in `mod.rs`. Their free functions accept raw `&Connection` (dump.rs:113, restore.rs:200, explain.rs:28, statistics.rs:18, replay.rs:6) without any lock discipline. External callers invoking `memory_engine::inspect::dump::dump_json(conn, ...)` bypass the engine's `with_read`/`write_conn` pool protocol entirely, creating a lock-safety hazard. Verification of callers: every non-test consumer resides in `src/engine/inspect.rs` and `src/engine/restore.rs` (same crate, behind `with_read`). The integration test uses only `memory_engine::inspect::types::*`. No CLI or MCP crate reaches the submodule functions directly. The `pub` visibility is therefore over-broad and misleading.

Current state: `pub mod dump; pub mod explain; pub mod replay; pub mod restore; pub mod statistics;` — all `pub`.
Target state: `pub(crate) mod dump; pub(crate) mod explain; pub(crate) mod replay; pub(crate) mod restore; pub(crate) mod statistics;` — only `types` stays `pub`, re-exported as `pub use types::*`.
Refactoring pattern: Restrict Visibility.
Motivation: encapsulation, lock-safety misuse prevention, cleaner public API surface.
Estimated scope: 1 file (`src/inspect/mod.rs`). Verify no breakage in CLI/MCP crates before committing (confirmed clean by inspection).
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: low — mechanical change, no semantic change.

title: God module: 1386-line flat file mixing tool schema, dispatch, and all 22 handlers
description: Current state: `tools/mod.rs` contains three logically independent concerns in one file — (1) JSON schema blobs for all 22 tool definitions (~360 LOC), (2) the string-keyed dispatch table (~40 LOC), and (3) 22 handler functions plus all parsing helpers (~1000 LOC). Target state: split into `tools/definitions.rs` (schemas + `all_tool_definitions`), `tools/dispatch.rs` or a `mod.rs` dispatcher, and per-group handler modules (`tools/p0.rs`, `tools/p1.rs`, `tools/p2.rs`, `tools/session.rs`, `tools/outcome.rs`). Refactoring pattern: Extract Module. Motivation: coupling — a schema change forces a read of the same file as a handler bug-fix; readability — the handler for `handle_flush_insights` (102 LOC) is buried 800 lines in; testability — unit tests currently require scanning the whole file. Estimated scope: 1 file → 5-7 files, no logic change. Prerequisites: none (purely structural). Risk: LOW — mechanical split, handlers are already private functions.
suggested_fix: Create `tools/definitions.rs` exporting `all_tool_definitions` + `tool_def`, `tools/parse.rs` exporting the `get_*` / `parse_*` helpers, and per-phase handler files. `tools/mod.rs` becomes the dispatcher (`pub fn dispatch` + `pub fn all_tool_definitions` re-exports).

title: read() in in-memory mode acquires write_conn.lock(), creating a deadlock if write() is held on the same thread
description:
Current state: `read()` for in-memory pools calls `self.write_conn.lock()` (line 191). `parking_lot::Mutex` is non-reentrant. Any code path that holds a `MutexGuard` from `write()` and subsequently calls `pool.read()` on the same thread will deadlock (parking_lot may panic with the `deadlock_detection` feature; otherwise it spins forever).

The current callers are all sequential (write guard dropped before read is called), so the bug is dormant. However, the API contract of `read()` — "always available" — cannot be honoured in in-memory mode when the write lock is held. The doc comment (line 183-186) does not warn about this constraint.

Target state: either (a) document the invariant explicitly on `write()` — "must not call `read()` while holding this guard in in-memory mode" — and add a `debug_assert` that detects the violation at dev time, or (b) give in-memory `ReadConn` its own slot (e.g. a separate `Mutex<Connection>` clone) so `read()` never re-acquires `write_conn`.

Refactoring pattern: Contract documentation + defensive assertion, or structural decoupling.
Motivation: correctness, thread-safety documentation.
Estimated scope: `connection_pool.rs` only.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: option (a) is zero-risk; option (b) requires an additional in-memory connection.

title: ResumeConfig::Default captures wall-clock time — impure and stale-prone
description: Current state: `impl Default for ResumeConfig` calls `Utc::now()` at construction time (`now: Utc::now()`). This is an impure `Default` impl: the value of a field depends on when the struct is built, not on explicit intent. Two consequences: (1) any consumer that stores the struct and uses it later operates on a stale timestamp; (2) the codebase already exposes the flaw — every test that exercises `now`-sensitive behaviour overrides it explicitly (`ResumeConfig { now, ..ResumeConfig::default() }` at lines 191–194, 222–225, 253–257 in context.rs), which means the author already knew the trap and worked around it rather than fixing the API. Target state: remove `now` from `Default` entirely — either require callers to supply it (change `Default` to not set `now`, making it non-`Default` or defaulting to a sentinel like `DateTime::<Utc>::MIN_UTC` that callers must override), or change the field type to `Option<DateTime<Utc>>` and resolve it inside `resume_context` when `None`. Refactoring pattern: Eliminate Impure Default / Make-Invalid-State-Unrepresentable. Motivation: correctness (stale timestamp silently surfaces wrong due facts) and testability (tests currently fight the impl). Estimated scope: 2 files (`context.rs`, `engine/resume.rs`) plus all call-sites; `async_engine.rs` passes `ResumeConfig` by value, so its signature is unaffected. Prerequisites: confirm no external consumers rely on `Default` producing a wall-clock `now`. Risk: public API break — semver bump required.

title: schema.rs is a 2491-line god module mixing DDL, migrations, config, backup, pragmas, and test fixtures
description: Current state: single file contains (a) DDL constants for all tables/indexes, (b) 8 migration functions (v1→v9), (c) SQLite pragma configuration, (d) backup logic, (e) config key-value store operations, (f) epoch-gate checks, (g) frozen test-fixture DDL strings for every historical schema version. These concerns are completely orthogonal. Target state: split into sub-modules — schema/ddl.rs (DDL constants), schema/migrations.rs (migration chain), schema/config.rs (key-value pragma/config), schema/backup.rs (backup logic), schema/fixtures.rs (test-only frozen DDL, cfg(test) gated). Refactoring pattern: Extract Module. Motivation: readability, maintainability, reduced merge conflict surface. Estimated scope: schema.rs only, plus updating all `use crate::store::schema::*` call sites (~10 callers). Prerequisites: no behavioral changes, existing tests cover migrations. Risk: medium — import paths change across the workspace.
suggested_fix: Create src/store/schema/ directory, split into sub-modules as described, re-export public items from src/store/schema/mod.rs to preserve the existing public API surface. Test-fixture DDL should be gated with #[cfg(test)].

title: relation_type is a bare String throughout EdgeStore — no newtype or enum enforcement
description: Current state: `relation_type` field on `Edge` and `NewEdge` is `String`/`&str` everywhere (edges.rs:21,49). Any caller can insert an arbitrary string. Target state: introduce `RelationType` as either a closed enum (if the set of relation types is finite and known) or a newtype `struct RelationType(String)` with a validated constructor that enforces non-empty, lowercase-kebab constraints. Refactoring pattern: Replace Primitive with Object / Introduce Value Object. Motivation: type safety, prevents invalid relation type values being persisted, enables exhaustive match on consumers. Estimated scope: edges.rs + types.rs + all call sites of EdgeStore::insert and consumers of Edge. Prerequisites: audit all relation type strings in use across the codebase. Risk: medium — API-breaking change to NewEdge.

title: Fact struct: importance and importance_score are both undocumented with no explanation of their semantic difference
description: The public Fact struct (crate API surface) exposes two f64 importance fields with no doc comments on either: `importance` (line 133, the base/user-supplied value at ingest) and `importance_score` (line 139, the materialized value continuously updated by the forgetting pipeline). No field-level /// comment distinguishes them. Consumers reading the struct cannot determine which to filter on, which to supply, or why both exist. The schema comment in store/schema.rs confirms they are seeded identically (`seed importance_score from base importance`) and then diverge, but this is invisible at the public API level.

title: `EmbeddingProvider::embed` impl has no /// doc comment
description: The `embed` method on the `EmbeddingProvider` impl block (http.rs:116-181) carries zero documentation. The method has four distinct error conditions: (1) HTTP send failure → `MemoryError::Internal`; (2) non-2xx HTTP status → `MemoryError::Internal` with status+body; (3) JSON parse failure → `MemoryError::Internal`; (4) unknown response format → `MemoryError::Internal`; (5) dimension mismatch → `MemoryError::EmbeddingDimension`; (6) NaN/Inf in result → `MemoryError::Internal`. None of these are documented. Users relying only on generated docs have no way to know which errors to expect or match on.

title: `EmbeddingProvider::embed_batch` impl has no /// doc comment
description: The `embed_batch` method on the `EmbeddingProvider` impl block (http.rs:183-248) carries zero documentation. The trait's default implementation loops sequentially; this override makes a single round-trip batch call — a material performance difference undiscoverable from the generated docs. It also has the same multi-path error surface as `embed`, plus an additional `MemoryError::Internal` for count mismatch between the returned array length and `texts.len()`, and per-index dimension/NaN errors. None of these are documented.

title: remove_node doc omits NodeIndex invalidation side-effect; silent correctness hazard in archive loop
description:
MemoryGraph::remove_node (line 82) calls petgraph::DiGraph::remove_node, which uses swap_remove internally (petgraph 0.7.1 src/graph_impl/mod.rs:668): the last node in the internal Vec is moved into the vacated slot. The MemoryGraph::node_map (HashMap<i64, NodeIndex>) removes the entry for the deleted fact_id (line 83) but does NOT update the node_map entry for the node that was relocated by swap_remove. After the call, that node's map entry points to a stale (now out-of-bounds or aliased) NodeIndex. All subsequent operations that use node_map — neighbors(), degree(), connected_component(), remove_edges_by_fact() — will silently produce wrong results or access wrong nodes for the relocated node.

The only non-test caller is src/engine/archive.rs:83-88, which iterates a fact_ids Vec and calls remove_edges_by_fact + remove_node in a loop. Any archive batch with more than one fact reliably corrupts node_map for surviving nodes whose internal petgraph index was the 'last' before each swap_remove.

The doc comment (lines 78-81) is silent on this invariant break. It says 'Remove a node and all its edges from the graph. No-op if the fact id is not in the graph.' — both claims are locally true but together they imply the operation is safe to call iteratively, which it is not with the current DiGraph + node_map design.

No test covers sequential remove_node calls on a multi-node graph followed by queries on surviving nodes, so the bug is latent but not caught by the test suite.
references: src/engine/archive.rs:83-88 (only non-test caller; iterates fact_ids in a loop)

title: `QueryDiagnostics::results_returned` documented but never assigned
description: The field doc on line 77 promises "Total results returned after all filters and truncation", but `hybrid_search` constructs `QueryDiagnostics` at lines 247-252 using `..QueryDiagnostics::default()`, leaving `results_returned` at 0 regardless of how many results were collected. Any consumer reading `diagnostics.results_returned` receives 0, making the diagnostic field a silent lie.

title: `HnswStrategy::notify_insert` panics in production code with no `# Panics` section
description: The `HnswStrategy` impl of `notify_insert` contains an `assert_eq!` at line 334 that panics if the HNSW crate assigns a non-sequential ID. This is production code (not test, not `#[cfg(test)]`). Neither the trait method doc in `strategy.rs:40-42` nor the `HnswStrategy` impl has a `# Panics` section documenting this invariant. The trait's contract implicitly promises no panic (the default impl is a no-op), but the override can abort the process.

title: select_archive_candidates loads entire facts and edges tables into memory
description: `select_archive_candidates` calls `FactStore::list_all()` (no WHERE clause, fetches all facts including active, pinned, and non-expired ones with their full embedding BLOBs) and `EdgeStore::list_all()` (all edges), then filters in Rust. For a database with 100 000 facts and 1 536-dimension embeddings, this allocates roughly 600 MB in a single call just to discard most rows. The facts store already contains several targeted queries with `WHERE t_expired IS NOT NULL AND is_pinned = 0` patterns — a dedicated SQL query for archive candidates is missing.
suggested_fix:
Add a targeted query to `FactStore`:
```sql
SELECT ... FROM facts
WHERE t_expired IS NOT NULL
  AND t_expired < ?1
  AND is_pinned = 0
ORDER BY id ASC
```
This pushes filtering into SQLite (which already indexes `t_expired`), avoiding the full-table allocation. Similarly for edges: filter `WHERE source_fact_id IN (…)` rather than loading all edges and filtering in Rust.

title: N+1 SQLite round-trips in hybrid_search result collection
description: Inside the ranked-ID loop, `store.get(id)` issues one `SELECT` per candidate, for up to `effective_limit` (default 150 = 50 × 3 overfetch) round-trips on every hybrid search call. This is the hot path: every `engine.execute_query()` with text or embedding lands here. The fix is a single batched `WHERE id IN (?)` fetch before the loop.
suggested_fix: Collect the ordered IDs first, then batch-load: `let ids: Vec<i64> = ranked.iter().take(effective_limit).map(|(id,_)| *id).collect(); let facts = store.get_many(&ids)?;` — implement `FactStore::get_many` with `WHERE id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))` to preserve insertion order. Iterate the pre-fetched map in the existing loop for temporal post-filter and match-type tagging.

title: 2N SQLite round-trips per HNSW candidate in HnswStrategy::search
description: For each HNSW candidate (up to `limit × OVERFETCH_FACTOR × 2^attempt` = typically 9 × limit per attempt across MAX_WIDEN_ATTEMPTS=3), two separate queries are issued: `check_fact_filters` (EXISTS) and `load_embedding` (SELECT embedding). With a 50-result request and one widening attempt that's 2 × 150 = 300 round-trips before the brute-force fallback. A single `SELECT id, embedding FROM facts WHERE id IN (?) AND t_expired IS NULL AND ...` batches both checks into one query.

title: API stable-since-1.91 vs MSRV 1.85
clippy -D warnings gate fails (default)
cargo test --all-features broken via #1
Path-traversal guard is ineffective: lexical Path::starts_with does not resolve `..`
description: search_archives builds `pak_path = archive_dir.join(&entry.pak_path)` and guards with `if !pak_path.starts_with(archive_dir) { continue; }` (search.rs:47) before `read_pak(&pak_path)` (search.rs:54). `entry.pak_path` is a plain `String` read from the SQLite `archive_manifest` table (store/archive_manifest.rs `row.get(1)`), whose column `pak_path TEXT NOT NULL` has NO CHECK constraint restricting separators or `..` (store/schema.rs:632). `Path::starts_with` is a purely LEXICAL component comparison that does not canonicalize `..`. I verified this empirically with rustc: `/data/archives/../../etc/passwd`.starts_with(`/data/archives`) returns TRUE, and `sub/../../../etc/passwd` also returns TRUE; the guard only rejects an absolute component (e.g. `/etc/passwd` -> false). Consequently a manifest row containing `..` segments escapes archive_dir and read_pak will open, zstd-decompress, and serde-deserialize an arbitrary file on disk. The legitimate write path always inserts a generated separator-free filename (archive-<ts>-<nanos>.pak), so this is unreachable in normal operation, but the guard exists specifically as defense-in-depth against an untrusted/tampered/restored DB or any future code that inserts a manifest row from less-trusted input -- exactly the 'trust blobs/JSON read back from the DB as if validated' surface this audit enumerates. The control is present in intent but broken in implementation. The identical defective guard is duplicated at src/engine/archive.rs:124 (verify_archives, out of audit scope) -- fixing one should fix both.

title: Unbounded memory allocation parsing untrusted JSONL session logs
description: parse_session_file reads an attacker-controlled JSONL stream with no size cap. reader.lines() allocates one String per line with NO per-line length limit (a single multi-gigabyte line lacking a newline forces unbounded allocation before the JSON parser even runs), and every successfully parsed SessionEntry is pushed into an unbounded `entries: Vec`. Each entry carries `data: Option<serde_json::Value>` (parse.rs:44) and `message.content: Option<serde_json::Value>` (parse.rs:51), which accept arbitrary-WIDTH JSON (one huge array/string per line); serde_json's default recursion limit of 128 bounds nesting DEPTH but not width or total size. The only bound in the whole chain is config.max_turns, applied at mod.rs:162 AFTER parse + reconstruct_turns + classify_outcome have all run on the full unbounded set, and it defaults to 0 = no limit (metrics.rs:20). The public entry points engine/bootstrap.rs:23 (bootstrap_session, arbitrary BufRead) and :63 (bootstrap_directory, processes ANY top-level *.jsonl file in the supplied dir) expose this with no upstream cap. A single crafted .jsonl file exhausts process RAM (OOM kill of the embedding agent).

title: Decompression bomb: size cap applies to compressed file, not decompressed stream
description: read_snapshot enforces MAX_SNAPSHOT_SIZE = 4 GiB against metadata.len() (restore.rs:75), which is the ON-DISK / COMPRESSED size. For Gzip and Zstd snapshots, the decoder output is then handed to serde_json::from_reader (read_gzip at restore.rs:95, read_zstd at restore.rs:109) with NO cap on the decompressed byte count. A small crafted zstd/gzip file (a few MB) can expand 100x-1000x+, and serde_json builds unbounded Vec<Fact>/Vec<Event>/Vec<Edge>/Vec<Summary> in memory. An attacker who can supply a snapshot file to restore_json / restore_json_memory (engine/restore.rs:29,80) triggers OOM / process kill. The plain-JSON path IS bounded by the 4 GiB file cap; only the compressed paths are unbounded. CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data), CWE-400/CWE-770 (uncontrolled resource consumption).

title: Unbounded Vec<f32> allocation from untrusted client embedding array (alloc precedes dim check)
description: parse_embedding() does serde_json::from_value::<Vec<f32>>(v.clone()) on a client-supplied JSON array of arbitrary length. The whole array is materialized into a heap Vec BEFORE any size/dimension validation. For memory_add_fact the dimension check exists only AFTER allocation (line 598-606), and for memory_query there is NO mcp-layer dimension check at all — the handler hands the Vec straight to the engine (the engine's vector_search at src/search/vector.rs:48 does reject a wrong dimension, so the wrong-dim is caught, but the large allocation has already occurred on the blocking thread pool). A client sending {"embedding":[0,0,...]} with tens of millions of elements forces a multi-hundred-MB f32 allocation per request, repeatable, exhausting server memory (CWE-400/770). The rmcp stdio transport frames the message first but applies no inherent per-message size cap.

title: assert! in notify_insert panics with permanently-corrupt HNSW index
description: `index.insert(vec, &mut searcher)` at line 333 mutates the HNSW graph before the sequential-ID invariant is checked at line 334. If the assert fires: (1) the vector is already in the graph; (2) `index_to_fact` has NOT been pushed; (3) `fact_to_hnsw` has NOT been updated. `parking_lot::RwLock` does not poison on panic — the write lock is released, and subsequent lookups via `inner.index_to_fact[neighbor.index]` will index out-of-bounds for the orphaned entry, causing a subsequent panic or silent wrong answer. `build_from_db` handles the same invariant via `MemoryError::Internal` (line 119) — `notify_insert` must be consistent. Since `VectorSearchStrategy::notify_insert` has no return value, the fix requires changing the trait signature or storing a poisoned flag.
_verified: VERIFIED: index.insert mutates before assert_eq; parking_lot no-poison; ann-gated defensive assert

title: Dump path security check vulnerable to symlink in final filename component
description: The path security check in `handle_dump_state` canonicalizes only the *parent* directory of the client-supplied path. If the final filename component is itself a symlink pointing outside `/tmp` (e.g., `/tmp/escape -> /etc/passwd`), `p.parent()` resolves to `/tmp` (which canonicalizes correctly) while `p` itself still points outside the sandbox. The subsequent `engine.dump_state(&dump_format)` write follows the symlink, enabling arbitrary file overwrite. Additionally, `temp_dir()` is not canonicalized before the `starts_with` comparison: on platforms where `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp` are themselves symlinks (e.g., macOS `/tmp -> /private/tmp`), legitimate paths inside `/private/tmp` fail the check — a false rejection. Both bugs share the same root cause: only one side of the comparison is canonicalized.
suggested_fix: Canonicalize `p` itself (not just its parent) after creating it: `let canonical = std::fs::canonicalize(&p).map_err(|_| ValidationError::Other(...))?;`. Also canonicalize `temp_dir()` on the right-hand side: `let temp = std::fs::canonicalize(std::env::temp_dir()).unwrap_or_else(|_| std::env::temp_dir());`. This closes both the symlink-filename and the false-rejection bugs. Note that for a non-existent destination file, `canonicalize` will fail; the fix should canonicalize the parent and then reconstruct the full path from the canonicalized parent plus the file_name component.

title: ancestors and path_for_id loop forever on cyclic parent links
description: ancestors() (lines 61-68) and path_for_id() (lines 158-165) walk the parent_id chain with no visited-set or depth cap. The DB schema enforces a DAG for normally-inserted rows, but the from_snapshot() path (lines 178-190) reconstructs the tree from unvalidated snapshot bytes without any cycle check. Malformed or adversarially crafted snapshot data with a cycle (e.g. node A.parent_id = B, B.parent_id = A) causes both methods to spin forever, hanging the thread that holds the RwLock<ScopeTree> write guard. Because this is safe Rust, it is a liveness violation rather than memory unsafety, but it can permanently deadlock the engine. subtree() (lines 72-84) uses a VecDeque and visits each node once due to the tree structure, but a cycle in children map would cause it to loop forever and grow memory without bound.
_verified: VERIFIED: no visited-set guard; add cycle/depth guard regardless of reachability

title: explicit_counter_loop denied error
search.rs has zero inline tests — public search_archives is entirely untested at unit level
description: src/archive/search.rs exports the public function search_archives (line 34) that implements the brute-force archive fallback path. The file has 117 lines and no #[cfg(test)] mod block at all. The integration test in tests/archive_test.rs:189-263 exercises the happy path (text query, MatchType::Archive) but leaves the following code paths untested: (1) path traversal guard at search.rs:47 (pak_path.starts_with(archive_dir)); (2) fact-type filter branch at search.rs:59-63; (3) the vector/cosine-similarity branch at search.rs:77-85 (no test ever passes a query.embedding); (4) the 'match all' fallback at search.rs:88-91 (query with neither text nor embedding); (5) missing .pak file silently skipped at search.rs:50; (6) multi-pak iteration (all integration tests produce exactly one .pak).
suggested_fix: Add a #[cfg(test)] mod tests block in src/archive/search.rs. Use tempfile + write_pak to manufacture .pak fixtures. Parameterise tests over: text-only query, embedding-only query, text+embedding query, no-query (match-all), fact_type filter hit/miss, path-traversal entry (pak_path pointing to '../escape.pak'), missing pak file entry (entry present in manifest_entries but file absent on disk). Each test should call search_archives directly without going through the engine.

title: read_pak error paths and decompression-bomb cap are not tested
description: pak.rs inline tests (lines 103-160) cover only the success path: write then read back an empty pak. Missing error-path tests: (1) read_pak on a nonexistent path should return MemoryError::Archive; (2) read_pak on a file containing random bytes (not zstd) should return an error; (3) read_pak on valid zstd but invalid JSON inside should return MemoryError::Serde; (4) the decompression-bomb cap — MAX_PAK_DECOMPRESSED_SIZE = 4 GiB at pak.rs:9 is enforced by Read::take(decoder, MAX_PAK_DECOMPRESSED_SIZE) at pak.rs:64, but there is no test that feeds a payload exceeding the limit (or a micro-limit) to confirm the cap fires correctly. (5) write_pak_and_hash on a path whose parent directory does not exist should return MemoryError::Archive.

title: max_turns test asserts the pre-truncation turn count, proving nothing
description: `report.turns_reconstructed` is set at `src/bootstrap/mod.rs:153` — before the `max_turns` slice at line 162-166. The test assertion `turns_reconstructed <= 1` measures the number of reconstructable turns in the fixture (which happens to be 1), not whether the truncation actually fired. With `max_turns=1` in a 4-turn session the assertion would still pass because the field is pre-truncation. The downstream effects of truncation (reduced `candidates_found` and `facts_created`) are never checked, so the `max_turns` code path is effectively unguarded.
suggested_fix: Add a multi-turn fixture (or build the JSONL inline) that produces ≥3 reconstructed turns. Then assert that `candidates_found` or `facts_created` under `max_turns=1` is strictly less than the same run with `max_turns=0`. Alternatively, change `report.turns_reconstructed` to record the post-truncation count (and update the doc comment), then assert `report.turns_reconstructed <= config.max_turns`.

title: PersistenceClassifier path never exercised in integration tests
description: Every call to `bootstrap_session` / `bootstrap_directory` in the integration test passes `classifier: None`. The conditional pinning branch at `src/bootstrap/mod.rs:206-228` — which builds a temporary `Fact`, calls `c.should_pin()`, and sets `new_fact.is_pinned` — has zero integration coverage. A regression in the is_pinned propagation or in the temporary `Fact` construction would be invisible.
suggested_fix: Add a `struct AlwaysPinClassifier;` that implements `PersistenceClassifier` returning `true`, run a bootstrap with it, then query facts and assert `is_pinned == true` on every created fact. Also add a `NeverPinClassifier` baseline to confirm the flag is toggled, not always true.

title: Savepoint rollback on mid-pipeline failure is never tested
description: The error path in `bootstrap_within_savepoint` (mod.rs:101-114) issues `ROLLBACK TO bootstrap; RELEASE bootstrap` to keep the connection usable, but no test exercises this. An embedder that returns `Err` after the marker event is already inserted is the natural trigger. Without a test, a future change to the savepoint handling could leave the writer in an open transaction — precisely the scenario the comment warns about.
suggested_fix: Implement a `struct FailEmbedder;` that returns `Err(MemoryError::NotFound("inject embed failure".into()))`. Run `bootstrap_session` with it; assert it returns `Err`. Then run a second successful session on the same engine to confirm the connection is still usable (i.e., the savepoint was properly released).

title: Zero inline tests in output.rs, db.rs, and embedding.rs
description: None of these three modules have a #[cfg(test)] block. output.rs exports truncate_str (a UTF-8 string utility with documented guarantees), print_json, and OutputFormat. db.rs exports open_engine and open_engine_writable with non-trivial error paths (missing config table, wrong file type). embedding.rs exports PassthroughEmbedder whose embed_batch intentionally errors for n!=1 texts — no path through that error is tested anywhere.
suggested_fix: Add #[cfg(test)] mod tests to each file. For output.rs: test truncate_str with empty string, exact-boundary, over-boundary, multi-byte Unicode (e.g., '日本語' chars), and max_chars<3. For embedding.rs: test embed_batch with 0 texts (should error), 1 text (Ok), and 2 texts (should error). For db.rs: test open_engine on a path that is not a memory-engine DB (missing config table).

title: record-outcome and outcome-counts subcommands have zero integration test coverage
description: Neither record-outcome nor outcome-counts appear anywhere in the tests/ directory. These subcommands exercise write paths (record_outcome mutates the DB) and read paths (get_outcome_counts) across all three output formats. All three format branches (Table, Json, Plain) and the nonexistent-fact error path are untested.

title: The only export integration test is permanently #[ignore] due to a library bug; export command has zero running test coverage
description: The comment at line 324-326 of cli_integration.rs acknowledges a schema-version mismatch bug (CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION=5 vs runtime v6) blocks the roundtrip test. As a result, the export command (all four formats: json, sqlite, json-gz, json-zst) has no running integration test. export.rs:27-31 has four format branches, none exercised. The sqlite branch requires write access (open_engine_writable), which is also untested.

title: consolidate() orchestrator has no #[cfg(test)] module
description: The top-level `consolidate()` function (mod.rs:35) is responsible for: reading/writing the `last_consolidated_at` watermark, detecting the `usize::MAX` sentinel that suppresses watermark advancement when dedup is skipped, and committing a single atomic transaction across all three passes. None of these behaviors have unit tests. The sentinel detection (mod.rs:55-66) and the conditional `set_config` call (mod.rs:64-66) are completely untested at the unit level. Integration tests in `tests/eval/quality/consolidation.rs` exercise the happy path but do not test watermark suppression.
suggested_fix: Add a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block to mod.rs. At minimum: (1) a test that calls `consolidate()` on an empty DB and asserts `last_consolidated_at` is set; (2) a test that mocks or simulates the over-cap condition (by inserting via a stub or directly calling `local_dedup` with the sentinel return) and asserts `last_consolidated_at` is NOT advanced; (3) a test that uses a failing `SummaryGenerator` and asserts the DB is unchanged (transaction rolled back) after the call returns `Err`.

title: Transaction rollback on SummaryGenerator failure is untested
description: The doc-comment on `consolidate()` promises: 'On any failure (including SummaryGenerator errors), the entire consolidation is rolled back.' This invariant is never tested. No test in `src/consolidation/` or `tests/` supplies a failing `SummaryGenerator` to verify that facts expired in the dedup pass are un-expired (or that no facts are modified at all) when a later pass fails. The `unchecked_transaction` / `tx.commit()` pattern (mod.rs:50,68) means a panic or early-return `?` before `commit()` would implicitly roll back via `Drop`, but this is never asserted.
suggested_fix: Add a `FailingSummaryGenerator` test double that returns `Err(MemoryError::Internal(...))` from `summarize()`. Run `consolidate()` with near-duplicate facts (so dedup would expire something) and a `min_cluster_size` low enough for cluster_fusion to attempt summarization. Assert the call returns `Err`, then verify that `fact_store.list_active(None)` still returns the same count as before — proving the rollback actually occurred.

title: AsyncMemoryEngine has 6 tests covering ~25+ public methods
description: The `#[cfg(test)]` mod in async_engine.rs contains exactly 6 `#[tokio::test]` functions (async_add_fact_and_query, async_concurrent_queries, async_graph_methods, async_list_due, async_pin_unpin, async_config_roundtrip). The following public async methods have no test at all: `open` (file-backed), `from_arc`, `ingest`, `add_facts_batch`, `execute_query`, `consolidate`, `forget`, `resolve_conflict`, `list_active_facts`, `list_summaries`, `resume_context`, `link_session_facts`, `statistics`, `replay_events`, `explain_fact`, `fact_history`, `dump_state`, `sample_dormant`, `record_insight`, `run_dream_cycle`, `write_snapshot`, `restore_json`, `restore_json_memory`, `restore_sqlite`, `next_due_time`, `reranker_name`, `is_file_backed`, `embed_dim`, and the `#[cfg(feature = "archive")]` methods. The integration tests in tests/ exercise the sync MemoryEngine — they do not exercise the spawn_blocking shim, which is the only value-add of this file. A panic inside the closure after the join returns `JoinError`, tested nowhere.

title: Public API embed() and embed_batch() have no inline tests within this crate
description: All five inline unit tests in http.rs (lines 251-311) cover only the private helpers parse_openai_batch and parse_ollama_batch. The public EmbeddingProvider impl methods embed() (line 116) and embed_batch() (line 183) are exercised solely through memory-engine-mcp/tests/embedding_integration.rs — a consumer-crate test file. As a library crate, memory-engine-embed provides no direct evidence that its own public contract works; if extracted or versioned independently, its correctness is unverifiable without the consumer. The wiremock + tokio dev-deps declared in memory-engine-embed/Cargo.toml are currently unused within the crate.

title: `sample_dormant` has zero integration test coverage
description: `MemoryEngine::sample_dormant` is a public API method with its own module at `src/engine/dormant.rs`. No file in `tests/` exercises it via the external consumer API. The inline `#[cfg(test)]` block in `dormant.rs` (lines 67-148) only covers unit-level helpers, not the end-to-end path through the engine facade. A consumer that calls `sample_dormant` after a sequence of `add_fact` + `forget` calls has no test verifying the returned candidates satisfy the dormancy invariant.
suggested_fix: Add `tests/dormant_test.rs`: open an in-memory engine, ingest facts with varying `last_accessed` timestamps (use `add_fact` + manual SQL update via a test helper to back-date `last_accessed`), call `sample_dormant(limit, None)`, and assert all returned facts are older than the dormancy threshold and not already expired.

title: Lineage API (`record_lineage`, `get_provenance`, `get_full_lineage`, `delete_lineage`) has zero integration test coverage
description: All four public lineage methods are exercised only through the internal `promote_with_lineage` path in `cognitive.rs` tests. No test in `tests/` calls `engine.record_lineage(...)`, `engine.get_provenance(fact_id)`, `engine.get_full_lineage(fact_id, depth)`, or `engine.delete_lineage(fact_id)` as an external consumer. The delete path in particular has no coverage anywhere: there is no test verifying that deleted lineage records are removed and that `get_provenance` returns `None` afterward.
suggested_fix: Add `tests/lineage_test.rs` that: (1) promotes two facts and records lineage linking them; (2) calls `get_provenance` and `get_full_lineage` with depth 1 and 2, asserting structure; (3) calls `delete_lineage` and asserts `get_provenance` returns `None`. Use `MemoryEngine::open_memory` with a stub embedder.

title: `run_dream_cycle` and `record_insight` have zero integration test coverage
description: The `DreamCycle` trait and `run_dream_cycle` engine method are tested only for compile-path smoke in `cognitive.rs` unit tests (lines 234-352); the engine-level facade (`mod.rs` `run_dream_cycle`) is not covered. `record_insight` likewise appears nowhere in `tests/`. No integration test verifies that a `DreamCycle` implementation returning `InsightStream` items causes the correct facts to be promoted and that `record_insight` persists the insight to the store.
suggested_fix: Add `tests/dream_cycle_test.rs` with a `MockDreamCycle` that returns a fixed `InsightStream` of one `Insight`; call `engine.run_dream_cycle(&mock)`, assert `Ok(CycleReport { insights_recorded: 1, .. })`, then verify the resulting fact is retrievable via `get_fact`.

title: No fuzz target for `load_from_file` binary parser (untrusted file input)
description: `load_from_file` reads untrusted bytes from disk: it parses a u32 LE `header_len` field (line 227), indexes `data[4..header_end]` (line 228-231), then msgpack-deserializes two structs. The bounds check at line 231 (`if header_end > data.len() - 32`) prevents the obvious OOB, but msgpack deserialization of arbitrarily deep nested structures or large allocation requests is not covered. No `fuzz/` directory exists in the workspace. `cargo-fuzz` is not configured. A adversarially crafted `.snapshot` file on disk (e.g., from a compromised model cache) could trigger panics in the msgpack allocator paths.

title: Graph edge cascade on prune is never tested
description: The `prune` function performs two operations when a fact is expired: it calls `edge_store.expire_by_fact(fact_id, now)?` (SQL cascade) and `graph.remove_edges_by_fact(fact_id)` (in-memory graph). All existing inline tests (`prune_expires_low_importance_facts`, `prune_skips_pinned_facts`, `prune_materializes_importance_scores`) and all integration tests pass an empty `MemoryGraph::new()` with no edges added. The SQL edge-expiry and in-memory graph-removal branches are therefore never executed by the test suite. A regression in `EdgeStore::expire_by_fact` or `MemoryGraph::remove_edges_by_fact` would be invisible. Additionally, the `graph_degree_weight` signal (the 3rd of 4 scoring signals) is always zero in every test because `graph.degree(fact_id)` always returns 0 on an empty graph, meaning the graph-connectivity branch of `compute_importance` is never meaningfully exercised in an end-to-end scenario.
suggested_fix: Add an inline test that pre-populates both `facts` and `edges` tables (via `EdgeStore::insert`) and a `MemoryGraph` with edges, then calls `prune` and asserts: (1) the expired fact's edges are marked expired in SQLite, (2) `graph.degree(fact_id)` is 0 after prune, (3) adjacent non-expired facts retain their edges. Also add an integration test where a well-connected fact survives while an isolated one is pruned under equal importance, exercising the graph-degree signal.

title: remove_node is untested and its petgraph swap_remove semantics silently corrupt node_map
description: MemoryGraph::remove_node has zero unit tests. The function calls petgraph DiGraph::remove_node (petgraph-0.7.1/src/graph_impl/mod.rs:668), which uses swap_remove: the last node in the internal Vec is moved into the removed node's slot. MemoryGraph does NOT update node_map for the displaced node, so after any remove_node call every subsequent lookup on the swapped-in node resolves to a stale, now-invalid NodeIndex — yielding wrong neighbors/degree results or out-of-bounds panics. The production path in src/engine/archive.rs:84-87 calls remove_node in a loop over multiple fact_ids, making the corruption cumulative. A test with three nodes where the middle one is removed, then operations on the remaining two, would immediately fail under the current implementation.

title: FactState::Expired and FactState::Invalidated branches have zero test coverage
description: The `determine_state` function (explain.rs:85-109) handles five lifecycle states: Expired > Invalidated > Pinned > Due > Active. No inline test and no integration test ever produces a fact in the `Expired` or `Invalidated` state and then calls `explain_fact`. Grep for `FactState::Expired|FactState::Invalidated` across `src/` and `tests/` returns only the two production-code match arms. The `Expired` branch (line 87-90) is reachable by setting `t_expired` on a fact; the `Invalidated` branch (line 92-95) requires a `t_invalid` in the past. Both remain completely dark from a test perspective.
suggested_fix:
Add two unit tests in `explain.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`:
1. `explain_expired_fact`: create an engine, call `add_fact`, then directly set `t_expired` via raw SQL on the pool, then call `engine.explain_fact(id)` and assert `matches!(state, FactState::Expired { .. })`.
2. `explain_invalidated_fact`: add a fact with `AddFactOptions { t_invalid: Some(Utc::now() - Duration::minutes(1)), .. }` and assert `matches!(state, FactState::Invalidated { .. })`.

title: dump_sqlite live-database safety guard has no test
description: `dump_sqlite` (dump.rs:196-206) canonicalizes both the source DB path and the target path and returns `MemoryError::Conflict` if they resolve to the same file. This is a data-safety mechanism that prevents overwriting the live database. No test verifies it fires. A regression could silently corrupt the live database on a re-dump.
suggested_fix: Add `sqlite_dump_refuses_to_overwrite_live_db`: open a file-backed engine at path `source.db`, then call `engine.dump_state(&DumpFormat::Sqlite(source_path.clone()))` and assert `matches!(err, MemoryError::Conflict(_))`.

title: MANAGED_CONFIG_KEYS exclusion during restore has no test
description: `restore_snapshot_into` (restore.rs:351-355) iterates the snapshot's `config` map and skips keys in `MANAGED_CONFIG_KEYS` (`["schema_version", "storage_epoch"]`). No test verifies this exclusion. A hostile or hand-crafted snapshot containing `schema_version: "9999"` in its config map would currently be skipped silently — but a regression that drops the filter would allow a snapshot to corrupt the DB's schema_version config entry, causing future opens to fail migration checks.
suggested_fix: Add `restore_does_not_import_managed_config_keys`: build an `EngineSnapshot` with `config: HashMap::from([("schema_version".into(), "9999".into()), ("custom_key".into(), "value".into())])`, call `restore_snapshot_into`, then query `get_config(conn, "schema_version")` and assert it equals `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION.to_string()` (not `"9999"`), while `get_config(conn, "custom_key")` equals `"value"`.

title: 1387-line tools module has no #[cfg(test)] block — private parsing helpers are untested at unit level
description: tools/mod.rs is the largest file in the crate (1387 lines) and contains a large set of private helper functions: parse_event_type (line 488), parse_fact_type (line 498), parse_search_mode (line 476), parse_replay_order (line 1120), parse_outcome (line 1255), parse_embedding (line 467), get_datetime (line 445), and require_f64_if_present (line 509). None has a dedicated #[cfg(test)] mod. Integration tests exercise these transitively but only over the success/known-error paths. Fine-grained boundary cases — e.g., parse_embedding with a JSON array containing non-numeric values, get_datetime with malformed-but-not-empty strings, require_f64_if_present distinguishing absent vs wrong-type (the bug it was written to catch) — are exercised only incidentally or not at all.
suggested_fix: Add a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block at the bottom of tools/mod.rs. At a minimum: (1) one happy-path + one error path for each parse_* fn; (2) `require_f64_if_present` with `Value::String("1".into())` must return Err (that is the exact regression the fn guards); (3) `get_datetime` with an invalid ISO-8601 string must return Err; (4) `parse_embedding` with a JSON array containing a string element must return Err.

title: Six dispatch-level tools have zero integration test coverage
description: Inspecting all five test files (tests/tool_roundtrip.rs, tests/tools.rs, tests/depth_shaping.rs, tests/query_mode_inference.rs, tests/embedding_integration.rs): memory_replay_events, memory_fact_history, memory_bootstrap_session, memory_record_activity, memory_checkpoint_session, and memory_load_context are never called through tools::dispatch() in any test. These cover the P2 debugging tools and the entire activity-stream / session-lifecycle feature (#224 commit). In particular, memory_record_activity has server-side deduplication logic and memory_checkpoint_session is called by the Stop hook — both are high-value paths and neither has a dispatch-level regression guard.
suggested_fix: Add a new test file tests/session_lifecycle.rs (or extend tests/tools.rs) covering at minimum: (1) memory_record_activity happy path + dedup (two identical calls in same dedup window return was_deduplicated=true); (2) memory_checkpoint_session creates a fact retrievable by memory_load_context; (3) memory_replay_events with a populated engine returns events and honours limit=0 vs limit=5; (4) memory_fact_history for a known fact_id; (5) memory_bootstrap_session with a minimal JSONL stub and no embedder returns an error.

title: DoS-relevant unbounded-input code paths have no test coverage
description: Three handlers accept untrusted input with no cap and no test exercising the extreme: (1) handle_replay_events line 1174-1178: limit=0 maps to None, meaning an unbounded result set; no test sends limit=0 to verify the query succeeds and returns all events (or that a server-side cap is in place). (2) handle_bootstrap_session (line 1225): jsonl_data is accepted as a raw String with no size cap; a 100 MB JSONL payload will be materialised in RAM before any validation. (3) handle_flush_insights (line 842): insights array has no cap; a client can send 10 000 entries. All three paths sit behind the MCP trust boundary and take untrusted JSON-RPC input.
suggested_fix: For replay_events: add a test that sends limit=0 and verifies it succeeds (confirming intentional, not accidental, unbounded behaviour). Consider adding a server-side cap comment explaining the choice. For bootstrap_session and flush_insights: add a test that sends a payload above a chosen threshold to confirm it is rejected or completes without OOM; alternatively, document explicitly in code that these are trusted-caller-only tools. The missing-test issue is independently fixable regardless of whether a cap is added.

title: Security-critical path-traversal rejection in handle_dump_state is not tested
description: handle_dump_state validates that a client-supplied 'path' argument is within std::env::temp_dir() to prevent MCP clients from overwriting arbitrary files (the security comment on line 1059 is explicit). The test suite (tests/tools.rs:261-286, 288-311) only exercises the success case and the default-path case. There is no test that passes a path outside the temp directory (e.g. /etc/passwd, /home/user/.ssh/authorized_keys) and asserts the result is Err. This validation would silently regress without a test.
suggested_fix: Add a test: `let result = tools::dispatch("memory_dump_state", args(&[("format", json!("json")), ("path", json!("/etc/clobber.json"))]), ...); assert!(result.is_err(), "path outside temp dir must be rejected"); let err = result.unwrap_err(); assert!(err.message.contains("temp directory"), "error should name the constraint");`

title: No fuzz target exists for tools::dispatch — primary untrusted-input entry point
description: tools::dispatch (line 377) is the sole point where untrusted MCP JSON-RPC arguments cross into the engine. It deserialises free-form serde_json::Map<String, Value> and dispatches across 23 tools. There is no fuzz/ directory in the workspace and no cargo-fuzz harness. Functions with especially high fuzzing ROI: dispatch() itself with arbitrary tool name + args map; parse_embedding() (line 467) which calls serde_json::from_value on attacker-controlled JSON; get_datetime() (line 445) with arbitrary strings; handle_bootstrap_session's JSONL parsing (line 1239 Cursor::new). The crate-level audit rationale explicitly flags untrusted JSON-RPC input as a high-weight concern.
suggested_fix: Add a fuzz/ crate: `cargo fuzz init` then `cargo fuzz add dispatch`. Minimal harness: `fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| { if let Ok(s) = std::str::from_utf8(data) { if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(s) { if let Value::Object(map) = v { let engine = MemoryEngine::open_memory(8).unwrap(); let _ = tools::dispatch("memory_ingest", map, &engine, None, None, 8, &Default::default()); } } } });`. Add a second target for parse_embedding specifically (call it with arbitrary JSON values). Add a third for jsonl_data in handle_bootstrap_session.

title: ScopeQuery::Ancestors and ScopeQuery::Inherited have no integration test coverage
description: The integration conformance suite (tests/eval/conformance/scope_isolation.rs) covers only ScopeQuery::Exact and ScopeQuery::Subtree. No test exercises the end-to-end path from MemoryQuery::scope_ancestors / scope_inherited (src/search/query.rs:114, 121) through engine::execute_query to ScopeTree::resolve_query (src/scope/tree.rs:108-109) and back to SQL filter. The inline unit tests in src/scope/tree.rs also cover only Exact (line 266) and Subtree (line 275) via resolve_query_exact / resolve_query_subtree. If resolve_query incorrectly dispatches Ancestors or Inherited, no test catches it.

title: ScopeTree::to_snapshot / from_snapshot have no roundtrip test
description: to_snapshot (line 171) and from_snapshot (line 178) are pub(crate) and used in engine/mod.rs:465 and 339 for the crash-recovery path. The snapshot.rs test (engine/snapshot.rs:478-497) only tests file serialization of the raw ScopeTreeSnapshot struct — it never asserts that from_snapshot(tree.to_snapshot()) reproduces the same tree (same node set, same children map, same path-resolution behavior). A bug in either direction (e.g. a future field added to ScopeNode but not wired in from_snapshot) would silently lose scope hierarchy on restore.

title: `include_expired_probe` contract has no end-to-end test
description: The `include_expired_probe` flag is tested only as a builder-setter (`query.rs:381-383`). No test anywhere in `src/` or `tests/` asserts that `diagnostics.expired_matches` is actually populated with a non-None count when `include_expired_probe = true` and facts have been expired, or that it is `None` for a vector-only query (documented invariant at `query.rs:59`). The execution path through `engine/query.rs:253-262` that calls `fts_count_expired` and writes `diagnostics.expired_matches = Some(expired_count)` is never exercised by a test that inspects the returned value.
suggested_fix:
Add an integration test (in `tests/` or `src/engine/tests.rs`) that:
1. Adds two facts matching a keyword, expires one.
2. Calls `execute_query` with `MemoryQuery::new().text(keyword).include_expired_probe()`.
3. Asserts `response.diagnostics.expired_matches == Some(1)`.
4. Adds a second sub-test with embedding-only query and asserts `expired_matches == None`.

title: Bi-temporal post-filter in `hybrid_search` never exercised at unit level
description: The `valid_at`/`t_valid`/`t_invalid` post-filter block at `hybrid.rs:218-230` is the only part of `hybrid_search` that enforces bi-temporal semantics. Every unit test in `hybrid.rs` passes `valid_at: None` and constructs facts with `t_valid: None, t_invalid: None`. The three branches — (1) future-dated `t_valid > cutoff` filtering out a fact, (2) past-invalidated `t_invalid <= cutoff` filtering out a fact, (3) explicit `valid_at` time-travel revealing a future fact — are all absent from `hybrid.rs` inline tests. Coverage exists only indirectly via `tests/eval/conformance/temporal_consistency.rs` going through the full `execute_query` stack, not through `hybrid_search` directly.

title: FactStore::stamp_surfaced has zero test coverage
description: stamp_surfaced updates the surfaced_at column and is the sole mechanism for recording when a fact was last presented to the user. No test exercises it — not the happy path, not the NotFound path, not the idempotent re-stamp case. The surfaced_at field is used for dormancy tracking (list_dormant checks whether surfaced_at + decay_interval < now), so an undetected regression here silently breaks prospective-memory recall.
suggested_fix: Add inline tests in the facts.rs #[cfg(test)] block: (1) stamp an existing fact and verify surfaced_at is set; (2) re-stamp and verify it's updated; (3) attempt to stamp a nonexistent id and confirm MemoryError::NotFound is returned.

title: FactStore::list_dormant has no tests and captures Utc::now() internally
description: list_dormant is entirely untested. It calls Utc::now() on line 203 inside the function body — the cutoff time is not injectable, making it impossible to write a deterministic unit test without sleeping or mocking the clock. This pattern also shows up in list_due and next_due_time. The inability to inject time is both a testability defect and a potential source of flakiness: test setup that inserts facts with 'just past due' timestamps can race the clock.
suggested_fix: Refactor list_dormant (and list_due, next_due_time) to accept an explicit as_of: DateTime<Utc> parameter instead of calling Utc::now() internally. The public MemoryEngine facade can call Utc::now() once and pass it in. Then add deterministic inline tests using fixed timestamps.

title: FactStore::update_importance_score is untested and missing NotFound guard
description: update_importance_score has no tests at all.
