More critically, unlike update_importance (line 275-284 which checks rows_affected == 0 and returns MemoryError::NotFound), update_importance_score silently returns Ok(()) even when the target fact id does not exist. This is a behavioral inconsistency that allows callers to believe a write succeeded when it was a no-op.
suggested_fix: Add a rows_affected == 0 guard identical to update_importance's guard. Then add tests: (1) update score on existing fact and verify retrieval; (2) attempt update on nonexistent id and verify MemoryError::NotFound.

title: Five FactStore query methods have no inline tests
description: list_by_scope_importance (line 310), list_by_scopes_importance (line 334), for_each (line 543), list_by_importance_score (line 574), and list_by_scopes_recent (line 677) have zero test coverage. These are non-trivial SQL queries involving ORDER BY, multi-scope IN clauses, and callback iteration — categories where SQL typos, wrong column references, and off-by-one LIMIT clauses are common. list_all (line 519) is also untested.
suggested_fix: Add one test per method exercising at least: empty result, single result, multi-result ordering, and (for scope-filtered variants) a fact in a different scope is not returned.

title: EdgeStore::expire silently succeeds for nonexistent edge IDs
description: EdgeStore::expire executes an UPDATE and returns Ok(()) without checking rows_affected. Expiring a nonexistent edge id is an undetected no-op. This is inconsistent with FactStore::expire (which checks rows_affected and returns MemoryError::NotFound) and violates the caller's expectation that Ok(()) means something was actually expired. No test exercises the nonexistent-id case.
suggested_fix: After the execute call, retrieve conn.changes() and return Err(MemoryError::NotFound { id: edge_id }) if changes == 0, mirroring FactStore::expire. Add a test that expires a nonexistent edge and asserts NotFound.

title: row_to_activity and row_to_checkpoint silently discard JSON parse errors
description: Both row mapping functions use serde_json::from_str(...).unwrap_or_default() to deserialize the 'args' column (activities.rs:218) and 'metadata' column (checkpoints.rs:98). If the column contains syntactically invalid JSON — due to DB corruption, a migration bug, or a direct SQL INSERT — the field silently becomes serde_json::Value::Null / Value::Object({}) with no error surfaced. The constraint CHECK(json_valid(...)) on the column in DDL provides protection at write time, but does not help if a row was inserted before the constraint existed or via a path that bypasses it. Neither the happy path with malformed JSON nor the data-loss scenario has a test.
suggested_fix: Replace unwrap_or_default() with a proper match or ? operator that propagates a rusqlite::Error::FromSqlConversionFailure, then add tests that insert a row with deliberately malformed JSON in the args/metadata column (bypassing the CHECK constraint by using a raw PRAGMA-disabled connection) and assert the read returns an error rather than silently returning a default.
references: CWE-390: Detection of Error Condition Without Action

title: In-memory graph not updated when commit_archive succeeds but graph.write() is interrupted
description: After a successful `commit_archive` (facts hard-deleted from SQLite), the code acquires `self.graph.write()` and removes the corresponding nodes and edges. If the process panics or is killed between the SQLite commit and the graph removal loop, the in-memory graph retains stale nodes pointing to facts that no longer exist in the database. On the next engine load the graph is rebuilt from the DB (facts are gone), so persistence survives a restart — but within a single session, any graph query that hits the stale nodes will encounter dangling references. While `parking_lot::RwLock` does not poison, a panic inside the `graph.write()` lock block would drop the lock guard and leave the graph partially pruned.
suggested_fix: This is inherent to a two-phase commit (SQLite + in-memory). The safest mitigation is to make the graph update loop panic-safe by collecting the fact IDs into a local Vec before entering the lock and wrapping the loop in a catch_unwind guard, or by rebuilding the graph lazily on next access when a missing node is detected.

title: Decompression size limit produces opaque serde EOF error, not a clear limit-exceeded error
description: `read_pak` applies a 4 GiB cap via `Read::take(decoder, MAX_PAK_DECOMPRESSED_SIZE)`. When a compressed bomb reaches that limit, `take` stops reading and `serde_json::from_reader` receives an unexpected EOF — it returns a `serde_json::Error` with kind `io` ("unexpected end of JSON input"), which is then wrapped as `MemoryError::Serialization`. The caller cannot distinguish between a genuinely truncated/corrupt file and a size-limit trigger. In addition, the 4 GiB default is extremely large — a malicious pak in a test or adversarial restore path would OOM the process long before serde returns an error.
references: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)

title: EpisodeCategory serialised with Debug repr, producing capitalized strings inconsistent with outcome serialisation
description: Line 79 uses `format!("{:?}", episode.category)` to store the episode category in fact metadata. This emits Rust Debug output: "Bug", "Decision", "Convention", "Learning". The adjacent outcome serialisation at lines 84-85 uses lowercase literals ("failure", "success"). Consumers parsing `metadata["category"]` must handle mixed-case, and any rename of an EpisodeCategory variant silently changes the stored string without a compile error.
suggested_fix: Implement `std::fmt::Display` on `EpisodeCategory` (or add a `fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str`) returning lowercase kebab-case strings, and replace `format!("{:?}", episode.category)` with `episode.category.to_string()` (or `.as_str()`). This aligns with the "failure"/"success" convention used two lines below and makes the stored schema independent of Rust naming.

title: session_outcome key absent from metadata for Indeterminate sessions, producing inconsistent JSON schema
description: The match on `outcome` at lines 83-87 sets `metadata["session_outcome"]` for `Failure` and `Success` but does nothing for `Indeterminate`. The key is therefore absent (not "indeterminate") in one of the three cases. Consumers reading `metadata["session_outcome"]` get `serde_json::Value::Null` for Indeterminate rather than a sentinel string, making field presence unreliable as a discriminant.

title: Plain output omits scopes.max_depth present in Table output
description: The Table branch emits both `scopes.total` (line 69) and `scopes.max_depth` (lines 73-74), but the Plain branch (lines 94-105) only emits `scopes.total` and silently drops `max_depth`. Scripts that parse `--format plain` output to drive automation (the explicit purpose of the Plain format) will not see this field. The inconsistency is invisible at runtime since no error is raised.

title: Old fact is read outside the transaction before arbitration (TOCTOU window)
description: `let old_fact = fact_store.get(old_fact_id)?;` runs against the bare `&Connection` BEFORE `conn.unchecked_transaction()?` is opened in the Add/Update/Delete branches (lines 79, 116, 152). Any concurrent writer can mutate `old_fact_id` between the read and the BEGIN, so the arbiter decides on stale data. The Update/Delete branches partially self-heal via `expire_and_invalidate`'s `AND t_expired IS NULL` predicate (which surfaces as `NotFound` if already expired), but other mutations (importance, metadata, valid window) are silently accepted. The Add branch has no such guard and will happily create a `supplements` edge pointing at a fact whose state no longer matches what the arbiter saw.

title: Synthetic `Fact` passed to arbiter has hard-coded `importance_score: 0.5`, ignoring `new_fact.importance`
description: When building `new_as_fact` from `NewFact`, `importance_score` is hard-coded to `0.5` (line 65) regardless of `new_fact.importance`. An arbiter that compares `old.importance_score` vs `new.importance_score` will always see `0.5` for the candidate, biasing decisions silently. Compare to `FactStore::insert` (facts.rs:95) which correctly seeds `importance_score` from `fact.importance`. The `ConflictArbiter` doc (traits.rs:60-67) carries no caveat about which fields are synthetic, so consumers will reasonably assume `new_fact` is a faithful pre-insert view.
suggested_fix: Change line 65 from `importance_score: 0.5` to `importance_score: new_fact.importance`. This matches the seeding logic in `FactStore::insert`. Also add a `# Contract` section to `ConflictArbiter::arbitrate` documenting which fields are synthetic (`id == 0`, `importance_score == importance`, `surfaced_at == None`).

title: `conn.unchecked_transaction()` bypasses nested-transaction detection with no documented caller contract
description: All three mutation branches call `conn.unchecked_transaction()`. Per rusqlite, this bypasses the `&mut Connection` borrow check that normally prevents nested `BEGIN`s. If `resolve_conflict` is ever invoked from a caller that has already opened a `rusqlite::Transaction` on the same connection (e.g. a future engine-level batch op), SQLite returns `cannot start a transaction within a transaction` at runtime. The function doc says 'all mutations happen in a single transaction' but does not state 'caller must not hold a transaction'. For an embedded library, this is a latent footgun.
suggested_fix: Either (a) accept `tx: &rusqlite::Transaction<'_>` instead of `conn: &Connection` to make the caller's transaction discipline explicit at the type level, eliminating the need for `unchecked_transaction` entirely; or (b) add an explicit `# Errors` clause stating "the caller must not have an outer transaction open on `conn`; otherwise the inner BEGIN fails at SQLite level." Option (a) is preferred.

title: usize::MAX sentinel smuggled inside Result<(usize, Vec<i64>)> breaks the public API contract
description: `local_dedup` is a `pub` function (re-exported at `src/consolidation/mod.rs:10`). Its documented return type says "Returns count of duplicates removed", but when the safety cap is exceeded it returns `usize::MAX` as an out-of-band skip signal. The `#[doc]` comment on the function does not mention this sentinel. Any caller that does not know the convention — including future callers who read only the documented contract — will misinterpret `usize::MAX` as a huge duplicate count. This is a type-safety violation: a sentinel value is sharing the space of a valid integer count with no type-level distinction.
suggested_fix: Change the return type to `Result<(DedupResult, Vec<i64>)>` where `DedupResult` is an enum `{ Completed { removed: usize }, Skipped }`. This makes the skipped state structurally visible to the compiler and all callers. Alternatively, wrap the return in `Option<usize>` where `None` means skipped. Either approach eliminates the sentinel and lets the orchestrator in `mod.rs` use a pattern match instead of the `== usize::MAX` check.

title: Wildcard arm in by_level match silently drops unrecognised ConsolidationLevel rows
description: compute_statistics maps 'local'/'cluster'/'global' to enum variants and uses `_ => continue` for anything else (line 75). If a new ConsolidationLevel variant is added and this match is not updated, or if a DB row has corrupted text, the count is silently discarded. This produces a sum(by_level.values()) < summary_total invariant violation with no error signal. The 'total' count (line 60) still includes those rows, making the stats struct internally inconsistent.
suggested_fix: Either (a) parse via a dedicated str_to_consolidation_level() -> Result function so a new variant forces a compile-time update, or (b) replace `_ => continue` with `other => return Err(MemoryError::Internal(format!("unknown consolidation level in DB: {other}")))`. Option (a) is preferred — it eliminates the wildcard entirely.

title: tmp_path() silently degrades when path.file_name() is None
description: tmp_path uses `path.file_name().unwrap_or_default().to_os_string()` (line 21). For paths where file_name() returns None (e.g. '/', '..', a path ending with '/'), the default empty OsStr is used, name becomes ".tmp", and `path.with_file_name(".tmp")` produces a sibling at the parent directory rather than a temp file next to the intended target. dump_json/dump_json_gzip/dump_json_zstd then write to the wrong location; the subsequent fs::rename either overwrites an unintended file or fails with a misleading I/O error. The atomic-write-then-rename safety invariant is silently lost.
suggested_fix: Change tmp_path to return Result<PathBuf>: `fn tmp_path(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> { let name = path.file_name().ok_or_else(|| MemoryError::Internal(format!("dump path has no file name: {}", path.display())))?; let mut name = name.to_os_string(); name.push(".tmp"); Ok(path.with_file_name(name)) }` and propagate the error in each caller.

title: Wildcard arm silently maps invalid scope_mode to subtree
description: In `handle_query`, the scope_mode match uses a catch-all `_ =>` arm that silently applies `scope_subtree` for any unrecognised string (e.g., `"FOO"`, `"EXACT"` with wrong case). A caller sending a misspelled or unsupported mode receives no error and gets subtree semantics instead, hiding intent bugs and making call-site mistakes invisible. The four valid values are `"exact"`, `"ancestors"`, `"inherited"`, `"subtree"`.
suggested_fix: Replace the `_ =>` arm with an explicit `"subtree" =>` arm and a final arm that returns `Err(ErrorData::invalid_params(format!("unknown scope_mode: {scope_mode}"), None))`.

title: Negative integer sent as limit/usize parameter silently becomes None
description: `get_usize` calls `usize::try_from(v).ok()`, converting conversion failure (e.g. `-1_i64`) to `None`. Call sites such as `handle_query` use the result as `query.limit(get_usize(...))` — when the client sends `"limit": -1`, the limit parameter is silently dropped and the engine applies its own default, returning more results than the caller intended. The JSON schema for `memory_query` has no `minimum` constraint on `limit`, so this is reachable from untrusted input with no error returned.
suggested_fix: Change `get_usize` to return `Result<Option<usize>, ErrorData>` and return `Err(ErrorData::invalid_params("limit must be non-negative", None))` when `try_from` fails. Alternatively, add `"minimum": 0` to the JSON schema and add an explicit validation check in the handler.

title: read() dispatches on read_pool_size==0 instead of path.is_none(), conflating in-memory with zero-sized file-backed pool
description: read() at line 188 routes to WriteAsReadGuard (the write-connection fallback) whenever self.read_pool_size == 0. open_memory() always sets read_pool_size=0 (line 132), so the heuristic works for that case. However, open() and open_read_only() accept caller-supplied read_pool_size and do not validate it is non-zero. A caller passing read_pool_size=0 to open() receives a file-backed ConnectionPool where is_file_backed() returns true (path.is_some()) but every read() call still acquires the write lock via WriteAsReadGuard, serialising all readers and defeating WAL concurrency. The doc comment at line 185-186 reinforces the wrong mental model by calling this path 'In-memory mode'.

title: resolve_path hardcodes root id=1 instead of using self.root_id()
description: resolve_path initialises its cursor as `let mut current = 1i64;` (line 45) rather than `self.root_id()`. root_id() also returns 1 (line 39), but the two values are now silently decoupled. If root_id() is ever updated (e.g. schema-driven root seeding changes the autoincrement start), resolve_path will continue to walk from the old hardcoded value while all other traversal helpers (ancestors, subtree, path_for_id) use self.root_id() correctly, producing inconsistent results with no compiler warning.
suggested_fix:
Change line 45 to:
```rust
let mut current = self.root_id();
```

title: activities dedup index in TABLES_DDL omits `scope_id`, diverging from migration DDL
description: The `idx_activities_dedup` index in `TABLES_DDL` (fresh-schema path) is defined over `(session_id, tool_name, args_hash, outcome_class)` — four columns. The equivalent index in `migrate_v8_to_v9` (line 687) includes a fifth column `scope_id`. A database initialized fresh will have a weaker dedup index than one that went through migration, causing the `insert_or_dedup` query (which filters on `scope_id` in its WHERE clause) to miss index-assisted lookup on scope on fresh databases. The two code paths produce structurally different schemas for the same logical version.
suggested_fix:
In `TABLES_DDL` change:
```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_activities_dedup
    ON activities(session_id, tool_name, args_hash, outcome_class);
```
to:
```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_activities_dedup
    ON activities(session_id, tool_name, args_hash, outcome_class, scope_id);
```
This matches the migration DDL at schema.rs:687.

title: Silent `unwrap_or_default()` on JSON deserialization swallows data corruption
description: In `row_to_activity` (activities.rs:218): `serde_json::from_str(&args_str).unwrap_or_default()` silently replaces malformed `args` JSON with `Value::Null`. In `row_to_checkpoint` (checkpoints.rs:98): `serde_json::from_str(&metadata_str).unwrap_or_default()` silently replaces malformed `metadata` with `Value::Null`. Both columns are `NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(...))` in the schema, so malformed JSON should never appear — but when it does (e.g., from a schema bug, direct DB edit, or corruption), the caller gets no indication and operates on empty data. All other JSON deserialization in the store (facts.rs, summaries.rs, lineage.rs) propagates errors properly via `map_err`. These two sites are inconsistent with the rest of the codebase and hide bugs.

title: Arithmetic overflow if `from_revision == u16::MAX` in `UpcasterRegistry::register`
description: `let target = from_revision + 1;` at upcaster.rs:55 is plain `u16` addition. If a caller registers an upcaster with `from_revision = u16::MAX` (65535), this panics in debug builds and wraps to 0 in release builds, silently making the `latest` map store revision 0 for the event type. Subsequently, `latest_revision` returns 0, and any stored event at revision 1 would appear 'ahead' of the registry's latest (current_revision >= latest), so the upcasting chain would silently no-op on all events for that type. This is a safe-Rust panic path triggered by an out-of-range API call.

title: Magic literal `pak_version: 1` repeated with no named constant
description: Current state: the integer `1` is used as `pak_version` in three separate struct literals (types.rs:88 in a test, pak.rs:110 in the test helper, engine/archive.rs:177 in `build_pak`). There is no `CURRENT_PAK_VERSION` constant anywhere. Target state: define `pub(crate) const CURRENT_PAK_VERSION: u32 = 1;` in `src/archive/types.rs` (or `pak.rs`) and reference it in all construction sites. Refactoring pattern: Extract Constant. Motivation: readability and correctness — a future format bump will require a grep to find all sites instead of a single edit; the lack of a constant also makes it impossible to validate the version in `read_pak`. Estimated scope: 3 files, 3 substitutions. Prerequisites: none. Risk: none (purely additive). Note: a complementary finding (#design-archivepak-no-version-check) depends on this constant existing.

title: `search_archives` accumulates all matching facts across all paks before truncating
description: Current state: `search_archives` at search.rs:41-108 iterates every manifest entry, fully decompresses each `.pak` via `read_pak` (which materialises the entire decompressed JSON in memory per pak.rs:65), collects all matches into `all_results: Vec<SearchResult>`, sorts, and only then truncates to `limit`. For N paks with M facts each, peak memory is O(N×M) matching facts plus O(N×M) full `Fact` structs held simultaneously during the sort. This contradicts the design intent of a 'slow fallback path' — it can OOM on a large cold-storage tier. Target state: use a bounded max-heap (e.g. `std::collections::BinaryHeap` with capacity `limit`) so only `limit` facts are retained in memory at any time; paks can still be decompressed sequentially. Refactoring pattern: Replace Vec+Sort with Bounded Heap. Motivation: memory safety / correctness under load. Estimated scope: 1 file (search.rs). Prerequisites: none. Risk: medium — sorting semantics change from stable to heap-order among equal scores; add a test with >limit candidates to pin the truncation behaviour before refactoring.

title: All five submodules declared `pub mod` — internal implementation types leak into the public API surface
description: All five submodules (`extract`, `filter`, `metrics`, `outcome`, `parse`) are declared `pub mod` in `src/bootstrap/mod.rs`. Because `bootstrap` itself is `pub mod` in `lib.rs`, every internal type becomes reachable at a stable public path: `memory_engine::bootstrap::parse::SessionEntry`, `memory_engine::bootstrap::filter::reconstruct_turns`, etc. None of these paths are intended API: `SessionEntry`, `MessagePayload`, `ContentBlock`, `EntryType`, `ToolUseResult`, `reconstruct_turns`, and `keyword_prefilter` are implementation details of the JSONL-to-turn pipeline. The consumer-facing re-exports (`BootstrapConfig`, `BootstrapReport`, `KeywordExtractor`, `SessionExtractor`, `CandidateEpisode`, `ConversationTurn`, `EpisodeCategory`, `ToolCallRecord`, `OutcomeSignals`, `SessionOutcome`, `PrewarmMetrics`) are already flat-exported via `pub use` in `mod.rs` and `lib.rs:49`. The leak is confirmed: `tests/bootstrap_test.rs:5-6` access `bootstrap::extract::KeywordExtractor` and `bootstrap::metrics::BootstrapConfig` by module path rather than the re-exported symbols, creating a coupling to internal layout. Current state: `pub mod extract; pub mod filter; pub mod metrics; pub mod outcome; pub mod parse;`. Target state: all five changed to `pub(crate) mod`. The public re-exports already in place continue to serve consumers. Refactoring pattern: Visibility Reduction. Motivation: encapsulation, freedom to restructure submodules without semver break. Scope: 1 file (mod.rs) + update `tests/bootstrap_test.rs` imports to use re-exported paths. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — re-exported names are unchanged; only direct module-path imports break (only `tests/bootstrap_test.rs` is affected and it can use the re-exported symbols).

title: Three functions with 9–11 arguments suppressed by `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` — missing context struct
description: All three entry-point functions — `bootstrap_session_inner` (9 args), `bootstrap_within_savepoint` (11 args), and `bootstrap_directory_inner` (9 args) — carry the same five context fields (`conn`, `embed_dim`, `upcaster_registry`, `embedder`, `classifier`) plus session-specific fields. The pattern is repeated verbatim at every call site (`engine/bootstrap.rs:42-52` and `82-92`). Current state: three `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` suppressions, 9–11 positional parameters each. Target state: extract an `InnerBootstrapCtx<'_>` struct holding `conn`, `embed_dim`, `upcaster_registry`, `embedder`, `classifier` (all borrows), reducing each signature to 4–6 parameters and removing all three suppressions. Refactoring pattern: Introduce Parameter Object. Motivation: readability, prevents positional mis-ordering at call sites, makes it easy to add future fields (e.g., a progress callback) in one place. Scope: `src/bootstrap/mod.rs` + `src/engine/bootstrap.rs`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: MEDIUM — mechanical but touches all call sites; rename risk is low since these are `pub(crate)` internal functions.
suggested_fix:
```rust
// In src/bootstrap/mod.rs
struct InnerBootstrapCtx<'a> {
    conn: &'a Connection,
    embed_dim: usize,
    upcaster_registry: &'a UpcasterRegistry,
    embedder: &'a dyn EmbeddingProvider,
    classifier: Option<&'a dyn PersistenceClassifier>,
}

pub(crate) fn bootstrap_session_inner(
    ctx: &InnerBootstrapCtx<'_>,
    reader: impl BufRead,
    extractor: &dyn SessionExtractor,
    config: &BootstrapConfig,
    scope_id: i64,
) -> Result<BootstrapReport> { ... }
```

title: Full `Fact` struct constructed as scratch pad to call `PersistenceClassifier::should_pin` — redundant 20-field struct allocation repeated per fact
description: In `bootstrap_within_savepoint` (lines 207–228), a complete `crate::types::Fact` is constructed with placeholder values (`id=0`, `content_hash=String::new()`, etc.) solely to call `classifier.should_pin(&temp)`. This is the same pattern used in `engine/ingest.rs:56-79`, but in the bootstrap context the fields `t_valid`, `t_invalid`, `access_count`, `last_accessed` are all set to constants that differ from what `NewFact` will eventually store. The `PersistenceClassifier` trait docs (`traits.rs:87-92`) already document that classifiers should only use `content`, `fact_type`, `importance`, and `metadata`. The current API forces construction of an 11+ field struct when 4 fields matter. A follow-on improvement would be to define a `ClassifierInput<'a>` view type or change `should_pin` to accept `&NewFact` (which holds the same 4 meaningful fields and already exists). Current state: temporary `Fact` struct with ~20 fields, 15 of which are dummy values. Target state: classifier receives `&NewFact` (already exists and has all required fields) so the temp struct is replaced by the already-constructed `new_fact`. Refactoring pattern: Simplify by Reusing Existing Type. Motivation: eliminates allocations, removes confusion about which fields matter, removes the need to keep the temp in sync with `Fact` struct evolution. Scope: `src/bootstrap/mod.rs:206-228` + `src/traits.rs:95` (trait signature) + `src/engine/ingest.rs:56-79` (same pattern). Prerequisites: trait change is semver-breaking. Risk: HIGH — changes `PersistenceClassifier` public trait signature.

title: Stringly-typed `target` arg with `unreachable!()` guard instead of a `ValueEnum`
description: Current state: `DumpArgs.target` is a `String` constrained by `value_parser = ["facts", "events", "all"]` and matched via `args.target.as_str()` with a `_ => unreachable!()` arm (lines 12-14, 53-58). The clap value_parser list prevents invalid input at runtime but gives no compile-time exhaustiveness guarantee — a new variant requires two edits (parser list + match arm) with no compiler help if one is missed. Target state: replace with `#[derive(ValueEnum, Default)] enum DumpTarget { Facts, Events, All }` and change the field type accordingly. The match becomes an exhaustive enum match with no wildcard. Refactoring pattern: Replace Stringly Typed with Value Object / Enum. Motivation: readability, misuse-resistance, compiler-enforced exhaustiveness. Scope: 1 file (dump.rs). Prerequisites: none. Risk: none — behaviour-preserving.

title: Stringly-typed `export_format` arg with `unreachable!()` guard instead of a `ValueEnum`
description: Current state: `ExportArgs.export_format` is a `String` constrained by `value_parser = ["json", "sqlite", "json-gz", "json-zst"]` (line 14) and matched via `as_str()` with `_ => unreachable!()` (lines 26-31). The format is also matched again as a string to decide read-only vs writable engine (line 20). Adding a new export format requires editing the value_parser list, the engine-open branch, and the DumpFormat dispatch — three disconnected sites with no compiler guard. Target state: `#[derive(ValueEnum)] enum ExportFormat { Json, Sqlite, JsonGz, JsonZst }` field, with the `is_sqlite()` method or match consolidated into one enum match block. Refactoring pattern: Replace Stringly Typed with Value Object / Enum. Motivation: misuse-resistance, compiler-enforced exhaustiveness, single point of change. Scope: 1 file. Prerequisites: none. Risk: none.

title: Relation type constants are stringly-typed; a closed enum would enforce invariants
description: Current state: `RELATION_SUPPLEMENTS` and `RELATION_CONTRADICTS` are `&str` constants (lines 12-13). They are `.to_string()`-ed on every use: lines 88, 103, 132, 199—four heap allocations per conflict resolution call. The relation type is stored as `String` in `NewEdge` and `Edge`, which is correct for the open store schema, but at the construction site only two values are ever legal for conflict-derived edges. Target state: introduce `enum ConflictEdgeRelation { Supplements, Contradicts }` (or `pub(crate)` in `conflict/mod.rs`) with `impl From<ConflictEdgeRelation> for String`, and replace the four `RELATION_*` constant references with enum variants. Refactoring pattern: Replace Stringly-Typed Parameter with Enum. Motivation: the closed set of legal relation types is now compiler-enforced; the four `.to_string()` calls are consolidated to two; future contributors cannot accidentally introduce a typo'd relation type. Estimated scope: 1 file (`temporal.rs`), optionally adding the enum to `conflict/mod.rs`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: VERY LOW—no behavior change; the string values are identical. LIGHT: fully mechanical.

title: Cluster similarity threshold is a hardcoded constant while dedup threshold is configurable
description: Current state: `CLUSTER_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.85` is a private constant in `cluster.rs` (line 11), not reachable by consumers. `ConsolidationConfig` (traits.rs:185) exposes only `dedup_threshold` and `min_cluster_size`. Callers that tune dedup strictness have no way to adjust clustering without patching the crate. Target state: add `cluster_threshold: f32` to `ConsolidationConfig` with a default of 0.85 (either via `impl Default` or a constructor), pass it through `consolidate()` → `cluster_fusion()`. The constant in `cluster.rs` is then removed. Refactoring pattern: Replace Magic Constant with Parameter. Motivation: API symmetry (both passes are configurable or neither is), tuning ability for consumers with domain-specific embedding spaces, testability (current tests can only exercise 0.85). Scope: 3 files (`cluster.rs`, `mod.rs`, `traits.rs`). Prerequisites: `ConsolidationConfig` is non-public but in `traits.rs` which is `pub`; bumping the struct is a semver-compatible addition only if it already implements `Default` or a builder. Risk: low-medium — additive API change.

title: Safety cap constant duplicated in dedup and cluster with inconsistent enforcement policy
description: Current state: `MAX_DEDUP_FACTS: usize = 50_000` (dedup.rs:30) and `MAX_CLUSTER_FACTS: usize = 50_000` (cluster.rs:36) are identical values in two files. More importantly, they are enforced differently: the dedup cap returns a sentinel and blocks watermark advancement (skip-with-consequence); the cluster cap silently returns 0 (skip-with-no-consequences, existing summaries are deleted at line 53 after the cap check). A future developer changing one cap is unlikely to know about the other, and the two enforcement policies diverge silently. Target state: lift both constants to `consolidation/mod.rs` or a private `constants` submodule; name them `MAX_FACTS_FOR_PAIRWISE_OPS` or with distinct, clear names; document the policy difference explicitly. Refactoring pattern: Consolidate Duplicate Constants / Introduce Explaining Variable. Motivation: maintainability (single source of truth), readability (explicit policy difference). Scope: 2 files. Prerequisites: none. Risk: low.

title: `MemoryError` lacks `#[non_exhaustive]`, making variant additions a SemVer break
description: Current state: `pub enum MemoryError` at error.rs:3 has no `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute. Any downstream crate that matches on `MemoryError` with a wildcard arm will fail to compile if a new variant is added, making every new error variant a SemVer-breaking change. Target state: `#[non_exhaustive]` on `MemoryError`. Refactoring pattern: Attribute addition. Motivation: API surface — the enum already has 17 variants and is actively growing (Lineage, Archive were added recently); without `#[non_exhaustive]`, adding the next variant (e.g. for Phase 5 wisdom promotion failures) breaks all downstream matchers. Estimated scope: 1 line in error.rs; downstream exhaustive match arms must add `_ => ...` wildcards. Prerequisites: confirm no internal exhaustive matches exist that would silently miss new variants (grep for `match.*MemoryError` in non-test code). Risk: low for library; moderate for downstream.
suggested_fix: Add `#[non_exhaustive]` on the line before `pub enum MemoryError {` at error.rs:3.

title: Ten error variants carry only `String`, preventing structured matching
description: Current state: `NotFound(String)`, `Conflict(String)`, `Migration(String)`, `NotImplemented(String)`, `Pool(String)`, `Internal(String)`, `Bootstrap(String)`, `Reranker(String)`, `Archive(String)`, `Lineage(String)` — 10 of 17 variants are `Variant(String)`. Target state: high-traffic variants like `Lineage`, `Pool`, and `Internal` should carry structured payloads (e.g. `Lineage { wisdom_fact_id: i64 }`) so callers can branch on data without parsing strings. Refactoring pattern: Stringly-typed → structured variant. Motivation: testability and coupling — the test at error.rs:99 asserts on `err.to_string().contains("wisdom fact 42")` rather than matching a field, which is fragile; callers cannot distinguish `Internal("concurrent write")` from `Internal("schema mismatch")` without string parsing. `Internal(String)` is a particularly problematic catch-all that absorbs unrelated failure modes. Estimated scope: error.rs + all `?` propagation sites across the workspace. Prerequisites: decide which variants warrant structured payloads before refactoring; start with `Lineage` (Phase 5, small footprint). Risk: high — changing variant shapes is a breaking API change; must be done alongside a semver bump or before 1.0.
suggested_fix: For `Lineage`, change to `Lineage { wisdom_fact_id: i64, message: String }`. For `Internal`, consider splitting into `Internal(String)` (retained for unexpected errors) plus specific variants for known failure modes (e.g. `ConcurrentWrite`, `SchemaMismatch`).

title: `outcome_class` is `String` across three types where an enum would enforce the invariant
description: Current state: `Activity.outcome_class: String` (line 534), `NewActivity.outcome_class: String` (line 551), `RecordActivityRequest.outcome_class: Option<String>` (line 577). In practice only `"success"` and `"error"` appear in store code (store/activities.rs:264, 288, 320), with `"test_failure"` documented in a comment. Target state: a `pub enum OutcomeClass { Success, Error, TestFailure, Other(String) }` with `Default` returning `Success` (matching the DB default). Refactoring pattern: Stringly-typed → enum (open variant for extensibility). Motivation: misuse-resistance — a consumer can currently pass any string including `""`, which breaks the DB dedup index on `(session_id, tool_name, args_hash, outcome_class)`; an enum prevents that class of bug at compile time. Estimated scope: types.rs + store/activities.rs + engine/activity.rs + MCP/CLI crates. Prerequisites: check the DB schema constraint — there is none (schema.rs:674 shows only `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'success'`), so the migration is purely Rust-side. Risk: medium — API break for consumers calling `record_activity`.
suggested_fix: Add `pub enum OutcomeClass { Success, Error, TestFailure, Other(String) }` with `impl Default`, `Display`, and `FromStr`. Replace the three `String` fields. For the `Other(String)` arm, document that it bypasses compile-time checking.

title: Inconsistent `Send + Sync` super-trait bounds: only `Reranker` declares them; six other traits do not
description: Current state: `Reranker: Send + Sync` at traits.rs:124, but `EmbeddingProvider`, `SummaryGenerator`, `ConflictArbiter`, `PersistenceClassifier`, `InsightStream`, and `DreamCycle` carry no `Send + Sync` bounds. Yet async_engine.rs consumes all of them as `Arc<dyn T + Send + Sync>` (lines 102-103, 125-126, 163-164, 183-184, 524-525, 537-538), which compiles only because Rust applies the bounds at the `Arc<dyn ...>` usage site rather than the trait definition. Target state: either (a) add `: Send + Sync` super-trait bounds to all six traits (matching `Reranker` and the actual usage contract), or (b) define a `trait AsyncCompatible: Send + Sync {}` blanket-bound and document explicitly which traits must satisfy it. Refactoring pattern: Bound propagation / super-trait extraction. Motivation: coupling and readability — a consumer implementing `EmbeddingProvider` cannot know from the trait alone that their impl must also be `Send + Sync`; they discover this only when passing the impl to `async_engine`, which is a poor DX. Estimated scope: traits.rs (6 trait definitions). Prerequisites: none. Risk: low — adding super-traits is backward-compatible for existing impls that already satisfy them; breaks only impls that are not `Send + Sync`, which are not usable with `AsyncMemoryEngine` anyway.
suggested_fix: Add `: Send + Sync` to `EmbeddingProvider`, `SummaryGenerator`, `ConflictArbiter`, `PersistenceClassifier`, `InsightStream`, `DreamCycle` trait definitions to match `Reranker` and the actual usage contract in async_engine.rs.

title: Constructor returns `Result<Self, String>` instead of `Result<Self, MemoryError>`
description: Current state: `HttpEmbeddingProvider::new` has signature `fn new(...) -> Result<Self, String>`. Target state: `fn new(...) -> Result<Self, MemoryError>`. Refactoring pattern: Widen error type to crate error enum. Motivation: callers (e.g. CLI setup) must `map_err` from `String` to `MemoryError` at every callsite, and the string loses structured context. `MemoryError::Internal(String)` is already used everywhere else in this file for reqwest failures; the TLS-init failure on line 32 is categorically the same kind of internal error. Using `String` as a public error type is stringly-typed and creates a leaky abstraction — the constructor is the only public API of this crate. Coupling: tight (single file). Testability: unaffected. Readability: improved. Estimated scope: 1 file (http.rs) + any callsite that does `.map_err(|e| ...)`). Prerequisites: none. Risk: low — purely additive type change.

title: Response format detected via if-let chain on `serde_json::Value` instead of typed deserialization
description: Current state: Both `embed` and `embed_batch` use untyped `serde_json::Value` with `.get("data")` / `.get("embeddings")` / `.get("embedding")` chains to detect the response format at runtime. The same three-branch detection appears twice (single and batch paths). Target state: Define a `#[derive(Deserialize)] enum EmbeddingResponse { OpenAi { data: Vec<OpenAiItem> }, Ollama { embeddings: Vec<Vec<f32>> }, Direct { embedding: Vec<f32> } }` with `#[serde(untagged)]`, deserialize once with `serde_json::from_value`, then match on the enum variant. This eliminates manual field probing, provides compile-checked field names, centralises the format knowledge, and removes the need for the redundant `.clone()` calls on individual array elements. Refactoring pattern: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism / introduce typed deserialization. Motivation: readability, correctness (typos in string keys become compile errors), coupling (format knowledge in one place). Estimated scope: 1 file. Prerequisites: add `serde` derive to the crate (already available transitively via `memory-engine` dep). Risk: low–medium — `#[serde(untagged)]` disambiguation must be tested against all three server fixtures.

title: `reqwest::blocking` embeds a hidden tokio runtime, conflicting with async callers
description: Current state: `HttpEmbeddingProvider` uses `reqwest::blocking::Client`, which internally spins up a tokio single-threaded runtime. This is documented in the integration test as a constraint (test file lines 7-10: 'HttpEmbeddingProvider must be created AND dropped on the blocking thread pool'). The `EmbeddingProvider` trait is sync, so blocking is required — but the hidden runtime means that any async caller (MCP server on tokio) must use `spawn_blocking` to avoid the 'nested runtime' panic. This is an architectural seam where the crate's design (sync trait) conflicts with the deployment environment (async MCP server). Target state: Document this constraint explicitly in `HttpEmbeddingProvider`'s rustdoc with a `# Panics` section noting the nested-runtime hazard. Longer-term: if `EmbeddingProvider` gains an async variant, `memory-engine-embed` could expose `AsyncHttpEmbeddingProvider` using `reqwest` (non-blocking). Refactoring pattern: Surfacing a hidden constraint. Motivation: misuse-resistance, discoverability. Estimated scope: 1 doc comment. Risk: doc-only change is zero risk.

title: select_archive_candidates() materialises all facts and edges then filters in Rust — SQL filter is entirely expressible
description: Current state: `select_archive_candidates()` calls `FactStore::list_all()` (line 153), loading every fact into memory, then retains only `!f.is_pinned && f.t_expired.is_some_and(|te| te < policy.expired_before)` in Rust (lines 155-159). Same pattern for `EdgeStore::list_all()` (line 161). For a database with many facts, this is O(N) memory and I/O where a SQL WHERE clause would return only the qualifying rows. Target state: add `FactStore::list_archive_candidates(expired_before: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<Vec<Fact>>` that issues `SELECT ... FROM facts WHERE is_pinned=0 AND t_expired IS NOT NULL AND t_expired < ?1`. Refactoring pattern: Push Predicate to Store (filter pushdown). Motivation: performance + memory — full-table scan defeats SQLite's row-level I/O budget; also coupling, since the archive module now knows FactStore's internal schema for filtering. Estimated scope: archive.rs + store/facts.rs (2 files). Prerequisites: a test with a large fact set would demonstrate the regression. Risk: low — new store method, archive just calls it.

title: pub fn record_lineage() exposes non-atomic lineage insertion — callers can create orphaned lineage records
description: Current state: `record_lineage()` (lineage.rs:17) is `pub` on `MemoryEngine` and inserts a lineage row with a bare write connection, with no savepoint and no check that the referenced `wisdom_fact_id` exists. The atomic path is `DreamContext::promote()` → `promote_with_lineage()` (cognitive.rs:143), which wraps both the fact insert and the lineage insert in a savepoint. Exposing `record_lineage()` as a public API allows consumers to insert lineage referencing a non-existent or already-expired wisdom fact, or to perform the fact insert and lineage insert in separate transactions that can be interrupted between them. Target state: reduce to `pub(crate)` (tests in lineage.rs can access it; the test at line 142 uses it directly and works under pub(crate)). The only external use case for lineage manipulation is `DreamContext::promote()`. Refactoring pattern: Encapsulate Leaky API (restrict visibility). Motivation: correctness + leaky abstraction — the atomicity guarantee documented by DreamContext is undermined at the library boundary. Estimated scope: lineage.rs (1 file), check memory-engine-cli and memory-engine-mcp for external call sites. Prerequisites: confirm no MCP/CLI tools call record_lineage directly. Risk: breaking change if any consumer uses it; negligible if only internal.
suggested_fix:
Change `pub fn record_lineage` to `pub(crate) fn record_lineage` in lineage.rs:17.
If the MCP or CLI expose a 'record lineage' endpoint, route it through DreamContext::promote() instead.

title: ForgetPolicy and PruneStats are concrete structs housed in traits.rs
description:
Current state: `ForgetPolicy` (lines 221–293, a config struct with validation logic) and `PruneStats` (lines 200–203, a plain output struct) both live in `src/traits.rs` alongside trait definitions. Neither is a trait. The `memory-engine-mcp` consumer already imports them via `memory_engine::traits::ForgetPolicy` (tools/mod.rs:11), which makes the trait module a mixed bag of behaviour contracts and configuration types.

Target state: Move `ForgetPolicy` and `PruneStats` to `src/forgetting/mod.rs` or a new `src/forgetting/types.rs`, then re-export from `src/lib.rs` with explicit names alongside the other public types. Update the three internal call-sites (`engine/forgetting.rs:7`, `engine/cognitive.rs:6`, `async_engine.rs:17`) and the one external call-site (`memory-engine-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:11`) to use the new path.

Refactoring pattern: Extract Type / Move Module.

Motivation: Coupling — `traits.rs` currently conflates two distinct concerns (trait definitions and concrete forgetting configuration), making it harder to reason about the public trait API. Readability — a contributor looking for where `ForgetPolicy` is defined will not look in `traits.rs`.

Estimated scope: 3 files (traits.rs, forgetting/mod.rs or new forgetting/types.rs, lib.rs) + 4 use-site updates. Prerequisites: existing tests already cover both types extensively. Risk: LOW — mechanical path change, no behaviour change.

title: EdgeData.relation_type is stringly-typed; no shared enum enforces the set of valid relations
description: Current state: `EdgeData.relation_type: String` (graph/memory_graph.rs:17) is an open string. Call sites work around this by declaring local constants (`RELATION_SUPPLEMENTS`, `RELATION_CONTRADICTS` in `conflict/temporal.rs:12,14`; `CO_SESSION_RELATION` in `engine/graph.rs:15`), but those constants are not shared. `engine/snapshot.rs:474` bypasses them entirely with a bare literal `"supplements"`. A typo in any call site produces a silently valid but semantically wrong edge label that is stored in SQLite and may never be detected. Target state: introduce a `RelationKind` enum in `src/graph/` (e.g. `pub(crate) enum RelationKind { Supplements, Contradicts, CoSession, Custom(String) }`) and change `EdgeData.relation_type` to `RelationKind`. Refactoring pattern: Replace-stringly-typed-field / Introduce-Value-Object. Motivation: invariant-enforcement, readability, prevents silent mismatch between in-memory graph and SQLite edge labels. Estimated scope: 3–4 files (graph/memory_graph.rs, conflict/temporal.rs, engine/graph.rs, engine/snapshot.rs). Prerequisites: update SQLite serialization to convert enum ↔ string at boundary (only in store/edges.rs). Risk: MEDIUM — touches multiple modules; needs schema round-trip test.

title: Enum variants serialized to DB strings via `format!("{:?}", …).to_lowercase()` instead of canonical helpers
description:
Two lines in `restore_snapshot_into` convert enum values to their SQLite string representation by formatting through `Debug` and lowercasing:
- Line 265: `let ft = format!("{:?}", fact.fact_type).to_lowercase();`
- Line 327: `let level = format!("{:?}", summary.level).to_lowercase();`

This is fragile: a future variant named `MultiWord` serializes to `"multiword"` rather than the dash-separated or underscore form that the rest of the store layer might expect. It also couples restore.rs to the internal `Debug` representation of types. Canonical `const fn` helpers already exist in the store layer: `fact_type_to_str` at `src/store/facts.rs:16` (already `pub(crate)`) and `level_to_str` at `src/store/summaries.rs:7` (currently module-private). The event insertion at restore.rs:237 already imports and uses `event_type_to_str` correctly — the fact and summary paths are inconsistent by comparison.

Current state: `format!("{:?}", …).to_lowercase()` in two places.
Target state: use `crate::store::facts::fact_type_to_str(&fact.fact_type)` and `crate::store::summaries::level_to_str(&summary.level)` (widen to `pub(crate)`).
Refactoring pattern: Replace Magic String with Symbolic Constant / centralise serialization.
Motivation: consistency with the rest of the store layer, resilience against future variant additions.
Estimated scope: 2 files (`src/inspect/restore.rs`, `src/store/summaries.rs` to widen `level_to_str`).
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: negligible — replaces non-canonical path with the canonical one already used by insert paths.

title: JSON object header hand-assembled with raw `write!` instead of a structured serializer — schema contract held only by a test
description:
`stream_snapshot` at line 43 manually constructs the JSON object header:
```rust
write!(writer, r#"{{"schema_version":{schema_version},"storage_epoch":{storage_epoch},"embed_dim":{embed_dim}"#)?;
```
and then calls `stream_for_each` for each collection. The field names and order are duplicated relative to `EngineSnapshot`'s serde-derived representation. If `EngineSnapshot` fields are renamed or reordered (e.g., a new top-level scalar is added for Phase 5), the streaming path silently diverges. The only thing preventing a mismatch is the `streaming_output_matches_snapshot_schema` test at dump.rs:278 — a test, not a compile-time constraint.

A fully type-safe streaming approach would use `serde_json::Serializer` with `serialize_map` for the object root, serializing scalar fields normally and collections via `stream_for_each`. Alternatively, a `SnapshotHeader { schema_version, storage_epoch, embed_dim, config }` struct carrying only scalars could be fully serde-serialized, with collections streamed afterwards — but this requires changing the JSON structure.

Current state: raw `write!` macro assembles JSON field names.
Target state: use serde's `Serializer`/`serialize_map` API so field names track the struct definition.
Refactoring pattern: Replace Hand-Rolled Serialization with Library Serializer.
Motivation: correctness, schema evolution safety.
Estimated scope: `src/inspect/dump.rs` only; restore.rs and the snapshot format are unchanged.
Prerequisites: familiarity with `serde_json::ser::Serializer`.
Risk: medium — the streaming guarantee (O(1) peak memory) must be preserved; the serde map API supports this but requires care.

title: Hand-rolled string→enum parsers duplicate what serde already provides on EventType/FactType/Outcome
description: Current state: `parse_event_type`, `parse_fact_type`, and `parse_outcome` are manual `match s { ... => Ok(...), other => Err(...) }` functions. `EventType`, `FactType`, and `Outcome` already derive `serde::Deserialize`. Target state: replace each parser with `serde_json::from_value::<T>(Value::String(s.to_owned()))` or add a `FromStr` impl delegating to serde, then call `T::from_str(s).map_err(|_| ...)` at each call site. Refactoring pattern: Delete Dead Code / Delegate to Existing Abstraction. Motivation: maintainability — when a new variant is added to `EventType`, the MCP parser must be updated separately; the compiler won't warn about the mismatch. Estimated scope: ~45 LOC removed across `tools/mod.rs`. Prerequisites: verify serde variant names match the JSON strings sent by clients (they do — both use PascalCase without `rename`). Risk: LOW.

title: Unknown scope_mode silently falls back to subtree instead of returning an error
description: Current state: `match scope_mode.as_str() { "exact" => ..., "ancestors" => ..., "inherited" => ..., _ => query.scope_subtree(scope) }`. An MCP client sending `"scope_mode": "Exact"` (wrong case) or a typo gets silent subtree semantics — a wrong query result with no error. The JSON schema declares an `enum` constraint, but the server does not enforce it. Target state: the wildcard arm should return `Err(ErrorData::invalid_params(format!("unknown scope_mode: {scope_mode}"), None))`. Refactoring pattern: Convert Silent Fallback to Explicit Error. Motivation: misuse-resistance — the MCP boundary is an untrusted input surface; erroneous queries silently returning wrong data is a correctness and security concern. Estimated scope: 1 LOC change. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LIGHT.

title: All MemoryMcpServer fields are pub — breaks encapsulation for a type that is the main server object
description: Current state: `pub engine`, `pub embedder`, `pub summary_gen`, `pub embed_dim`, `pub filter_config` are all `pub`. The struct is constructed only in `main.rs` via `MemoryMcpServer::new()`, and accessed only via `ServerHandler` trait methods. No external code reads the fields directly. Target state: change all five fields to `pub(crate)` or private. The constructor already exists. Refactoring pattern: Restrict Visibility. Motivation: encapsulation — nothing outside the crate needs to name these fields; `pub` on a binary-linked library struct invites accidental coupling in integration tests. Estimated scope: 5 one-word changes in `server.rs`. Prerequisites: verify test code does not access these fields directly — grep confirms no external field access. Risk: LIGHT.
suggested_fix:
pub struct MemoryMcpServer {
    pub(crate) engine: Arc<MemoryEngine>,
    pub(crate) embedder: Option<Arc<HttpEmbeddingProvider>>,
    pub(crate) summary_gen: Option<Arc<dyn SummaryGenerator + Send + Sync>>,
    pub(crate) embed_dim: usize,
    pub(crate) filter_config: Arc<ActivityFilterConfig>,
}

title: handle_dump_state path restriction canonicalizes the parent but not the final path — symlink TOCTOU bypass
description: Current state: the security check in `handle_dump_state` calls `fs::canonicalize(parent)` on the *parent directory* of the client-supplied path, then checks `canonical.starts_with(&temp)`. If `parent` itself does not exist, `canonicalize` returns an error, the `.ok()` makes it `None`, and `unwrap_or_default()` substitutes `PathBuf::new()` (empty path). `PathBuf::new().starts_with(temp_dir)` is `false`, so the empty-parent case is caught. However, if a symlink in the temp dir points outside it, the canonical check on the *parent* will still pass if the parent itself resolves inside temp — the *final component* (the filename) is never canonicalized. More critically, the validated canonical path is `parent`, but the engine is later given the *original* `p` (which still contains the unresolved symlink). This creates a check-then-use race. Target state: after validating, call `fs::canonicalize(&p)` on the full resolved path before passing to the engine, or reject any path whose canonical parent is not a *direct* child of temp (no subdirectories). Refactoring pattern: Fix TOCTOU / Harden Path Restriction. Motivation: input validation — MCP input is untrusted; the path restriction is security-critical. Estimated scope: ~10 LOC in `handle_dump_state`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: MEDIUM — changes security behavior.

title: handle_bootstrap_session accepts unbounded jsonl_data string — potential memory DoS via MCP
description: Current state: `handle_bootstrap_session` reads the full `jsonl_data` string from the JSON args map (already fully deserialized in memory by serde_json), then wraps it in a `Cursor` and passes it to `engine.bootstrap_session`. There is no size cap on the input string. An MCP client can send a JSON-RPC request with `jsonl_data` containing hundreds of megabytes of text, causing the blocking thread to hold a large allocation for the duration of the import. Target state: add a pre-check `if jsonl_data.len() > MAX_BOOTSTRAP_BYTES { return Err(...) }` before constructing the Cursor. A reasonable cap is 10–50 MB. Refactoring pattern: Add Input Size Guard. Motivation: DoS hardening — the MCP boundary is an untrusted input surface per the audit mandate; blocking all worker threads with a multi-hundred-MB import would starve the server. Estimated scope: 3 LOC in `handle_bootstrap_session`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — purely additive guard.

title: read_pool_size == 0 is used as an implicit 'in-memory mode' sentinel, creating a file-backed footgun
description:
Current state: `read()` at line 188 branches on `self.read_pool_size == 0` to decide between the in-memory path (lock `write_conn`) and the file-backed path (pop from `Vec`). `open_memory()` hardcodes `read_pool_size: 0` at line 132. There is no type-level distinction between the two modes.

Footgun: a caller invoking `ConnectionPool::open(path, dim, 0, None)` gets a file-backed pool that silently routes all reads through the write connection (serialized, WAL-parallelism lost, write contention on every read). This is not rejected, warned, or documented.

Target state: introduce a `BackendMode` enum (`FileBacked { read_pool_size: usize } | InMemory`) as a private field, replacing the `read_pool_size == 0` sentinel. The `read()` method dispatches on the variant, and `open()` enforces `read_pool_size >= 1`.

Refactoring pattern: Replace implicit sentinel with discriminated enum.
Motivation: misuse-resistance, readability, correctness.
Estimated scope: `connection_pool.rs` only (~40 lines changed).
Prerequisites: existing test suite covers both paths.
Risk: low — mechanical substitution, no external API change (pool is pub(crate)).

title: WriteAsReadGuard name implies read-only but exposes a fully-writable Connection with no query_only PRAGMA
description:
Current state: `WriteAsReadGuard<'a>` (line 52-60) wraps the `write_conn` `MutexGuard` and implements `Deref<Target = Connection>`. The name suggests read-only semantics, but the underlying connection was opened with full read-write privileges and no `PRAGMA query_only = ON` is applied in the in-memory path. A caller receiving a `ReadConn::InMemory(guard)` via `pool.read()` can execute `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` statements through it without any Rust-level or SQLite-level prevention.

By contrast, the file-backed read connections in `open()` explicitly set `PRAGMA query_only = ON` (line 101-102), enforcing read-only at the SQLite level.

Target state: either (a) apply `PRAGMA query_only = ON` to in-memory connections used for read paths (not possible without a separate connection), or (b) rename `WriteAsReadGuard` to `SharedWriteGuard` or `SerializedReadGuard` to accurately reflect that it is a serialized-read-through-write-conn wrapper, not a read-only guard, and update docs accordingly.

Refactoring pattern: Rename to match semantics; optionally add enforcement.
Motivation: readability, correctness (misuse-resistance).
Estimated scope: 1 struct rename + doc update in `connection_pool.rs`.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: zero for rename; medium for adding a separate read-only in-memory connection.

title: kb_stubs placeholder in public struct leaks internal roadmap into stable API
description: Current state: `ResumeContext::kb_stubs: Vec<String>` is part of the public (re-exported in `lib.rs:54`) struct. It is always set to `Vec::new()` and the doc comment explicitly calls it 'Placeholder: KB reference URIs for Phase 5'. The field does nothing today. Target state: remove the field until Phase 5 actually lands, or gate it behind a Cargo feature flag so it doesn't appear in consumers' type signature until the backing implementation exists. Refactoring pattern: YAGNI / Deferred Design. Motivation: a permanently-empty public field signals intent without delivering behaviour, forces any consumer doing exhaustive struct initialization or serialization to carry a dead weight, and — because `ResumeContext` derives `serde::Serialize` — it also appears in every JSON snapshot, creating a migration obligation when Phase 5 changes its shape. Estimated scope: 1 file (`context.rs`), plus downstream serde consumers. Risk: API break if any consumer already reads this field (unlikely given it is always empty).

title: ResumeConfig has no validate() despite containing unconstrained float fields
description: Current state: `ResumeConfig::high_importance_min: f64` is compared directly against `importance_score` in the `list_by_importance_score` call at `context.rs:84-89`, but nothing enforces it is in `[0.0, 1.0]`. Similarly `pinned_cap`, `high_importance_cap`, `due_cap`, `recent_cap` are unsigned but could be 0 (silently returning empty tiers). The established in-crate precedent is `DreamCycleConfig::validate()` (`types.rs:454-473`) which guards its f64 fields with `is_finite()` + range checks. Target state: add a `validate(&self) -> Result<()>` method to `ResumeConfig` mirroring that pattern, and call it at the top of `resume_context`. Refactoring pattern: Extract Validation / Defensive Contract. Motivation: misuse resistance; a consumer that passes `high_importance_min = 2.0` silently gets an empty high-importance tier with no diagnostic. Estimated scope: 1 file (`context.rs`). Prerequisites: none. Risk: low — additive change, no breakage.

title: `path_for_id(root)` returns `"/"` which `resolve_path` cannot parse back
description: Current state: `path_for_id(root_id())` returns the string `"/"` (line 152). `resolve_path("/")` splits on `'/'`, producing an empty first segment, hits the `is_empty()` guard at line 48, and returns `None`. The doc comment (lines 144–146) acknowledges this asymmetry by calling `"/"` 'display-only', but that is a leaky contract: any caller that round-trips through `path_for_id` and then passes the result back into `resolve_path` (or any API accepting a path string) will silently fail. Target state: choose one canonical representation for root and honour it throughout. Option A — `path_for_id(root_id())` returns `None` (signals 'no addressable path'); callers that want a display string add their own sentinel. Option B — `resolve_path` accepts the empty string `""` as a synonym for root ID. Option B is backward-compatible and matches how `ScopeStore::ensure_path` already skips empty paths. Pattern: Eliminate Non-invertible Representation. Motivation: misuse-resistance; the current contract is easy to break silently. Scope: 1 file, 2 methods. Prerequisites: agreement on canonical root string; update doc comments and the one test that asserts `"/"`. Risk: low — callers that currently print root paths for display only are unaffected by Option A; Option B adds a code path to `resolve_path`.

title: `resolve_path` accepts inputs that `ScopeStore::ensure_path` would reject, silently returning `None`
description: Current state: `resolve_path` trims each path segment (line 47) and rejects only the empty string (line 49). `ScopeStore::validate_label` (store/scopes.rs:76-99) additionally rejects: labels with leading/trailing whitespace, labels longer than 256 bytes, and labels containing `'/'`. Because scope creation enforces these rules, a segment that violates them can never exist in the tree — so `resolve_path` will always `None` for such inputs. However, the `None` return is indistinguishable from 'path exists but not found', masking caller bugs (e.g. a path with a 300-byte label silently resolves to `None` instead of indicating the path is malformed). Target state: either (a) add the same validation rules to `resolve_path` and return a `Result<Option<i64>, MemoryError>` (API change, HEAVY) so callers can distinguish 'invalid path' from 'path not found', or (b) extract `ScopeLabel` as a validated newtype used in both creation and resolution, so the compiler enforces that only valid labels are passed (HEAVY, highest misuse-resistance). A lighter Option (c): add a `validate_path_syntax` free function usable by both `resolve_path` and `ensure_path` so the rules are co-located, and document the `None` semantics. Pattern: Replace stringly-typed Input with Validated Newtype (Option b) / Guard Clause Reuse (Option c). Motivation: misuse-resistance, single source of validation truth. Scope: 2 files (tree.rs + store/scopes.rs). Prerequisites: decide API shape (Option vs Result); existing tests are sufficient. Risk: Option c is low; Option b is moderate (breaks method signatures in 5+ callsites).

title: HnswStrategy::search issues two DB round-trips per candidate (N+1 pattern)
description: Phase 2 of `HnswStrategy::search` iterates over HNSW candidates and calls `check_fact_filters(conn, fact_id, ...)` then `load_embedding(conn, fact_id, ...)` for each one — two `query_row` calls per candidate. With `overfetch = limit * 3` default and `MAX_WIDEN_ATTEMPTS = 3`, this is up to `limit * 9` round-trips in the worst case. Current state: two private functions each issuing a single-row query in a loop (ann.rs:354-388). Target state: one batched query `SELECT id, embedding, fact_type, scope_id FROM facts WHERE id IN ({candidates}) AND t_expired IS NULL AND (…filters…)` that fetches filtered rows and their embeddings in one pass; then cosine-score from the returned blobs in Rust. Refactoring pattern: Replace N+1 Queries with Batch. Motivation: performance (especially under aggressive scope/fact_type filters), connection contention reduction. Estimated scope: ann.rs, 1 file, ~40 lines changed. Prerequisites: note this file is lint-blind under `--all-features` (ANN feature flag); tests in the `hnsw_strategy_tests` submodule provide coverage. Risk: medium — query construction with `IN (?)` for a dynamic list requires either `rusqlite`'s repeated parameter binding or JSON expansion (same pattern as the existing scope_ids approach); correctness must be verified by the existing test suite.

title: hybrid_search is a 120-line function mixing three distinct phases
description: The function combines: (1) candidate collection from FTS5 and vector (lines 155-174), (2) RRF ranking / mode dispatch (lines 184-197), and (3) fact materialization, temporal filtering, and diagnostics assembly (lines 205-254). These phases have different error modes and testability profiles. Current state: single monolithic `pub fn hybrid_search`. Target state: three focused private helpers — `collect_candidates`, `rank_candidates`, `materialize_results` — called in sequence from a thin `hybrid_search` shell. Refactoring pattern: Extract Method. Motivation: readability, unit-testability of each phase in isolation, easier extension (e.g., adding graph-search as a fourth source). Estimated scope: 1 file, no API change. Prerequisites: proptest suite and integration tests provide coverage. Risk: low — the public signature is unchanged; risk is accidentally reordering operations, mitigated by existing tests.

title: SearchQuery is a fully-public struct constructed via struct-literal, with no builder
description: All eight fields of `SearchQuery` are `pub`, and callers construct it with struct literals specifying all fields explicitly — including `rerank_depth: None`, `valid_at: None`, `fact_type: None`, `scope: None` at every call site (engine/query.rs:210-219, async_engine.rs:585-595, async_engine.rs:625-635). This is inconsistent with `MemoryQuery`, which offers a fluent builder. As the struct grows (e.g., a `min_score` field) every call site becomes a compile error. Current state: plain public struct, struct-literal construction. Target state: either (a) a builder mirroring `MemoryQuery`'s pattern, or (b) `#[non_exhaustive]` plus a `SearchQuery::builder()` / `SearchQuery::new(text, embedding, mode, limit)` smart constructor with optional setters. Refactoring pattern: Introduce Builder. Motivation: misuse-resistance, forward-compatibility (struct-literal forces callers to update on every field addition), consistency with `MemoryQuery`. Estimated scope: hybrid.rs + 3 call sites in engine/ and async_engine.rs. Prerequisites: none. Risk: medium — all call sites are inside the crate; this is a crate-internal API, but the type is `pub`, meaning downstream crates (`memory-engine-mcp`) could construct it if exposed via `lib.rs` (currently it is not re-exported from lib.rs, so the risk is contained).

title: All search submodules are pub, exposing impl-internal paths to downstream crates
description: Every submodule (`ann`, `fts`, `hybrid`, `query`, `strategy`, `vector`) is declared `pub mod`, giving any external crate full path access to functions like `fts_search`, `vector_search`, `rrf_merge`, and `cosine_similarity` that are implementation details of the search pipeline. The re-export list in mod.rs selectively re-exports a curated subset, but that curation is bypassed because the submodules themselves are fully public. Downstream crates already exploit this: `memory-engine-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:10` imports `memory_engine::search::hybrid::SearchMode` and `memory-engine-mcp/src/depth.rs:3` imports `SearchResult` and `QueryDiagnostics` directly from `search::hybrid` rather than from the crate root. Current state: 6× `pub mod`, downstream imports reach submodule paths. Target state: either (a) convert all submodules to `pub(crate) mod` and extend `mod.rs` re-exports to cover the items downstream actually needs (requires moving `SearchMode`, `SearchResult`, `QueryDiagnostics`, `MatchType` to top-level re-exports in `lib.rs`), or (b) accept submodule paths as part of the public API and remove the redundant re-export layer. Option (a) is preferred: it makes the public API surface explicit and prevents accidental coupling to unstable paths. Refactoring pattern: Restrict Visibility / Move Re-exports. Motivation: encapsulation, API stability guarantees, prevents consumers from bypassing the curated interface. Estimated scope: mod.rs (visibility changes) + lib.rs (add ~5 re-exports) + 2 downstream import paths. Prerequisites: none. Risk: medium — breaking change if other external consumers (not visible in this workspace) use submodule paths; requires semver bump if the crate is published.

title: str_to_fact_type and str_to_event_type return MemoryError::NotFound for invalid enum variants
description: facts.rs:29: `Err(MemoryError::NotFound(format!("unknown fact type: {other}")))` and events.rs:45 does the same for event types. NotFound semantics are 'the requested resource does not exist in the store'. Parse failures are a completely different error class — the input string is malformed, not that a DB row is missing. This causes callers that match `MemoryError::NotFound` to conflate 'fact not in DB' with 'invalid fact_type string from DB'. Target state: add `MemoryError::InvalidData(String)` or `MemoryError::Corruption(String)` variant (since if a bad string comes from the DB column it is data corruption), or reuse `MemoryError::Internal`. Refactoring pattern: Replace Error Code with Exception / Rename. Motivation: correctness, prevents silent conflation of error semantics. Estimated scope: error.rs + facts.rs + events.rs + any match sites on NotFound. Risk: low — purely additive error variant.

title: ArchiveManifestStore::insert has 10 positional parameters, suppressed with #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
description: Current state: `insert` takes 10 individual parameters (pak_path, created_at, fact_count, edge_count, fact_id_min, fact_id_max, t_created_min, t_created_max, size_bytes, blake3_hash) with a clippy suppress at line 26. This makes call sites error-prone (argument order confusion) and prevents default/partial construction. Target state: introduce a `NewArchiveManifest` struct (or `ArchiveManifestEntry` reuse) and accept `&NewArchiveManifest`. Refactoring pattern: Introduce Parameter Object. Motivation: readability, reduced call-site errors, removes clippy suppress. Estimated scope: archive_manifest.rs + call sites. Risk: low.
suggested_fix:
pub struct NewArchiveManifest<'a> {
    pub pak_path: &'a str,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub fact_count: i64,
    pub edge_count: i64,
    pub fact_id_min: i64,
    pub fact_id_max: i64,
    pub t_created_min: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub t_created_max: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub size_bytes: i64,
    pub blake3_hash: &'a str,
}

pub fn insert(&self, m: &NewArchiveManifest<'_>) -> Result<i64> { ... }

title: never-used methods
`read_pak` has no `# Errors` section; omits `MemoryError::Serialization` return path
description: `read_pak` at line 65 uses `?` on `serde_json::from_reader`, which converts via `#[from] serde_json::Error` to `MemoryError::Serialization` — not `MemoryError::Archive`. The single-line doc says only 'Caps at 4 GiB decompressed' with no `# Errors` section at all. Callers matching on `MemoryError::Archive` to catch all parse failures will silently miss deserialization errors. Additionally: when the 4 GiB `Take` limit is reached, `serde_json` sees truncated input and returns a Serialization error — the limit-exceeded case is indistinguishable from ordinary JSON corruption.

title: Documented pipeline order is wrong: marker event ingested first, not last
description: Both the module-level doc comment (lines 3-4) and the `bootstrap_session_inner` doc (lines 32-33) describe the pipeline as: `parse → reconstruct turns → classify outcome → keyword pre-filter → extract facts → ingest marker event + add facts`. In reality, `bootstrap_within_savepoint` ingests the marker event at line 133 — before turn reconstruction (line 152), outcome classification (line 158), and fact extraction (line 198). The marker is inserted first to anchor the savepoint idempotency check. The documented order inverts this, misleading readers about when the idempotency anchor is written.

title: `BootstrapConfig::max_turns` doc omits tail-selection semantics
description: The field doc says only "Maximum turns to process per session. `0` = no limit." The actual behaviour in `bootstrap_within_savepoint` (mod.rs:162-166) is that when the turn count exceeds `max_turns`, the TAIL (most recent turns) is kept — not the head. This is a deliberate design decision (outcome evidence lives at session end), documented only in an inline comment. Public field docs don't surface this, so consumers who expect head-truncation will be surprised.

title: Stale #[ignore] with obsolete bug rationale on export_import_roundtrip test
description: The `export_import_roundtrip` test is suppressed with `#[ignore]` and the comment claims the cause is "CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION=5 but running schema is v6 after #78/#92". That bug is long gone: `src/store/schema.rs:8` shows `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 9`; `src/engine/archive.rs:178` writes the constant dynamically; `src/inspect/restore.rs:134` compares dynamically. Running the test with `cargo test -p memory-engine-cli export_import_roundtrip -- --ignored` passes (1 passed, 0 failed). The stale comment and attribute cause a real regression test to never run in CI.

title: Public function ingest_from_reader has no /// doc comment
description: `pub fn ingest_from_reader` is extracted specifically for testability (it is the hot path exercised by the unit tests in the same file). It is undocumented: no description of what the function does, no `# Errors` section documenting the non-obvious error path at lines 269-273 ("0 ingested AND >0 skipped → bail"), and no documentation of the `default_scope` vs per-record `scope` precedence rule (line 136: the JSONL record's own scope wins when present).

title: resolve_conflict doc omits synthetic-fact caveat for ConflictArbiter implementers
description: The public doc-comment for `resolve_conflict` (lines 18–34) describes each `CrudDecision` branch but never warns `ConflictArbiter` implementers that the `new_fact` argument they receive inside `arbitrate` is a pre-insert synthetic. Concretely, two fields diverge from the eventually-stored values: `id` is hardcoded to 0 (placeholder, not yet inserted, line 49) and `importance_score` is hardcoded to 0.5 (line 65) regardless of `new_fact.importance`, whereas `FactStore::insert` (store/facts.rs:95) seeds `importance_score` from `fact.importance`. An arbiter that reads `new_fact.id` for cross-referencing or `new_fact.importance_score` for ranking will silently get wrong data. The analogous warning already exists in traits.rs:87–92 for `PersistenceClassifier::should_pin` ('The Fact passed … is a pre-insert synthetic with id=0 … Classifiers should only rely on content, fact_type, importance …') but is absent from the call-site where the same constraint applies to the arbiter.

title: local_dedup return doc omits Vec<i64> component and usize::MAX sentinel
description: The function doc says "Returns count of duplicates removed" but the actual return type is `Result<(usize, Vec<i64>)>`. The second element — the list of expired fact IDs — is entirely undocumented in the public doc comment. Additionally, the sentinel value `usize::MAX` meaning "dedup skipped due to safety cap" is only explained in an inline comment at line 43 inside the function body; it is never mentioned in the public-facing doc, making the contract invisible to callers who pattern-match on the count.

title: Section comment "Phase 2 placeholder traits" is stale — SummaryGenerator and ConflictArbiter are fully implemented and in production use
description: The comment at line 38 reads `// --- Phase 2 placeholder traits and types ---` and the /// doc on SummaryGenerator (line 40) says "(Phase 2)." Both SummaryGenerator and ConflictArbiter are actively called from production code (consolidation/cluster.rs, consolidation/global.rs, engine/consolidation.rs, conflict/temporal.rs) and are exposed in AsyncMemoryEngine's public API. Labelling them placeholders misleads consumers and downstream developers about their production status.
suggested_fix:
Replace the section comment with:
```rust
// --- Consumer-implemented LLM-delegation traits ---
```
Remove "(Phase 2)" phase labels from SummaryGenerator and ConflictArbiter doc comments. Optionally add a note explaining why SummaryGenerator bundles embed() (consolidation needs both in one round-trip).

title: AsyncMemoryEngine struct-level doc example uses sync MemoryEngine::open_memory (blocking call in async context) and references undefined `embedder`
description: The struct-level code example (lines 28-34, marked `rust,ignore`) shows `let engine = MemoryEngine::open_memory(768)?` as the first step. This is the synchronous blocking constructor — calling it directly in an async context blocks the Tokio executor. The idiomatic async equivalent, `AsyncMemoryEngine::open_memory(768).await?`, exists and dispatches to the blocking thread pool. Additionally, the variable `embedder` on line 33 is used but never defined in the example. The `rust,ignore` attribute suppresses compilation, masking both issues.

title: 26 of ~30 Result-returning async methods lack # Errors doc sections
description: Methods including ingest (line 91), add_fact (99), add_facts_batch (122), query (143), execute_query (151), consolidate (162), forget (174), resolve_conflict (182), get_fact (197), list_active_facts (205), list_summaries (213), get_config (221), set_config (229), resume_context (237), list_due (245), next_due_time (253), pin_fact (261), unpin_fact (269), link_session_facts (277), sample_dormant (504), record_insight (521), run_dream_cycle (535), restore_json (455), restore_json_memory (468), restore_sqlite (477), and write_snapshot (492) all return `Result<_, MemoryError>` but carry no `# Errors` documentation. Consumers cannot distinguish which error variants are possible for each operation without reading the wrapped synchronous engine source.

title: ConsolidationConfig fields lack doc comments, range constraints, and a Default impl
description: The public ConsolidationConfig struct (line 185) exposes two fields with no documentation: `dedup_threshold: f32` (line 186) — no doc on whether it is a cosine similarity threshold in [0,1] or some other metric — and `min_cluster_size: usize` (line 187) — no doc on what constitutes a valid minimum. There is also no `Default` impl, so consumers must construct it with magic constants they cannot look up. The struct label says "(Phase 2)" (same stale label as finding above). Callers of AsyncMemoryEngine::consolidate() and MemoryEngine::consolidate() cannot determine correct values from docs alone.

title: Crate root lib.rs has no //! inner-documentation
description: lib.rs consists solely of `mod http;` and `pub use http::HttpEmbeddingProvider;` with no //! crate-level doc block. For a published library crate (memory-engine-embed), the crate root is the first thing rustdoc renders.
