description: The doc-comment at temporal.rs:33 promises `MemoryError::NotFound` when the old fact doesn't exist. The guard at temporal.rs:183 (`if changed == 0`) implements this for `expire_and_invalidate`, and `fact_store.get(old_fact_id)?` at temporal.rs:45 would also propagate NotFound before the match. Neither the inline tests (temporal.rs:270-487) nor the integration conformance suite (tests/eval/conformance/conflict_resolution.rs) passes a nonexistent or already-deleted `old_fact_id`. The promised error contract is structurally correct but coverage-zero.

title: Delete decision's edge-cascade and in-memory graph removal are untested
description: The Delete branch (temporal.rs:151-171) calls `edge_store.expire_by_fact(old_fact_id, now)?` at line 159 and `remove_edges_for_fact(graph, old_fact_id)` at line 164 — the same cascade logic as Update. The existing `delete_expires_old_no_new` test (lines 377-403) inserts no edges into the store and makes no graph assertions. There is no test that sets up pre-existing edges on a fact, then resolves with `CrudDecision::Delete`, and verifies both SQLite edges are expired and the in-memory graph is cleaned. Only the Update path has such coverage (`update_cascades_edges_on_old_fact`, line 405).

title: update_cascades_edges test verifies DB state but not in-memory graph after cascade
description: In `update_cascades_edges_on_old_fact` (temporal.rs:405-458): `graph.edge_count() == 2` is asserted at line 438 (before `resolve_conflict`). After the call, only `edge_store.list_active()` on the SQLite side is checked (lines 455-458). The in-memory `MemoryGraph` is never re-queried post-resolve. If `rebuild_graph_for_fact` (temporal.rs:191-202) silently failed to remove the two stale edges or failed to add the new contradicts edge, the test would still pass. The graph and DB can diverge invisibly.

title: No property-based tests despite proptest being a workspace pattern
description: `proptest = "1"` is a declared dev-dependency (Cargo.toml:41) used in src/search/hybrid.rs, src/search/vector.rs, src/scope/tree.rs, and src/store/{facts,schema,mod}.rs. The conflict module has no proptest coverage at all. A strong candidate property: for any `CrudDecision` ∈ {Add, Update, Delete, Noop}, after `resolve_conflict` succeeds the set of active edges involving `old_fact_id` in the DB is exactly mirrored in the in-memory `MemoryGraph`. A second candidate: for Update and Delete, the `now` timestamp stored in `t_expired` / `t_invalid` equals the `now` argument passed in, under any valid `DateTime<Utc>` — guarding against accidental re-snapshotting inside the function.

title: Arbiter receives hardcoded importance_score=0.5 for the candidate fact; no test verifies arbiter inputs
description: At temporal.rs:65, `new_as_fact.importance_score` is hardcoded to `0.5` when constructing the synthetic `Fact` passed to `arbiter.arbitrate()`. A real arbiter that branches on `importance_score` (e.g. "prefer higher-importance fact") receives a fabricated value regardless of the `NewFact.importance` field. No existing test asserts what values the arbiter actually receives — `FixedArbiter` ignores both arguments. This is a correctness gap surfaced as a test infrastructure gap: a test arbiter that captures and asserts its inputs would have caught the hardcoding.

title: Watermark suppression when dedup is skipped (usize::MAX sentinel) has no integration test
description: When `local_dedup` returns `usize::MAX` (over-cap path, dedup.rs:45), `consolidate()` must NOT advance `last_consolidated_at` so skipped facts are retried later. This logic (mod.rs:55-66) is critical for correctness: if the watermark were advanced despite the skip, those facts would be silently excluded from the next dedup window. No test exercises this path end-to-end via `engine.consolidate()`. The sentinel contract is documented only in a comment.
suggested_fix: Add an integration test that: (1) inserts at least two near-duplicate facts, (2) directly manipulates the store to make `list_active` return a list longer than `MAX_DEDUP_FACTS` (e.g., by temporarily lowering the cap via a feature flag or by inserting inline via `FactStore`), (3) calls `consolidate()`, and (4) asserts `get_config("last_consolidated_at")` is still `None` (or unchanged from before). Because 50_000 is too large to insert in a test, a better approach is to expose the cap as a testable constant or add a `#[cfg(test)]` override path.

title: greedy_cluster() has no direct unit tests; edge cases not exercised
description: The `greedy_cluster()` function is private and only tested indirectly through `cluster_fusion()`. Direct unit tests are absent for: (1) empty input (`facts = []` → should return `vec![]`); (2) single-element input (→ one cluster of size 1); (3) threshold = 1.0 exactly (all facts in separate singletons unless embedding identical); (4) transitivity: A∼B, B∼C but A≁C — does C end up in A's cluster via B? The current greedy expansion would include C (since it expands from each member), but this is not asserted. All four cluster tests use only `CLUSTER_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` (0.85) with hand-crafted embeddings at dim=4.
suggested_fix: Add a `#[cfg(test)] mod greedy_cluster_tests` in cluster.rs that calls `greedy_cluster()` directly (it is private so tests are in the same file). Cover: empty slice, single element, threshold=0.0 (all in one cluster), threshold=1.0 (all singletons unless identical), and the transitive chaining case (A≃B, B≃C, A≁C).

title: Majority-vote scope_id selection (including tie-break) has no test
description: The cluster scope_id is computed by a majority vote across source facts (cluster.rs:76-84), with the deterministic tie-break: 'equal counts → lowest scope_id wins' (implemented via `.then_with(|| b.0.cmp(&a.0))`). All existing cluster tests (`cluster_formation`, `min_cluster_size_respected`, `cluster_summaries_stored`, `idempotent_rebuild`) insert facts with the hardcoded `scope_id: 1`. The comment in `tests/eval/quality/consolidation.rs:82` says 'Use scope to verify majority-vote scope propagation' but all 8 facts in that test share the same scope (`project:rust`). Neither the majority path nor the tie-break is ever verified to produce the correct `scope_id` on the resulting summary.
suggested_fix: Add a unit test in cluster.rs that inserts facts split across two scopes (e.g., 3 facts in scope 10 and 2 facts in scope 20), runs `cluster_fusion`, retrieves the resulting summary via `SummaryStore::list_by_level`, and asserts `summary.scope_id == 10`. Add a second test with an even split (2 and 2) across scope IDs 10 and 5, and assert `summary.scope_id == 5` (lowest wins).

title: greedy_cluster() has algebraic invariants well-suited for property-based testing
description: `proptest` is already a dev-dependency (Cargo.toml:41) and is used in `src/search/hybrid.rs` and `src/search/vector.rs`. `greedy_cluster()` has strong structural invariants that example-based tests cannot adequately cover: (1) **partition**: every index 0..n appears in exactly one cluster; (2) **within-cluster similarity**: for any two facts in the same cluster, there exists a chain of pairwise-similar facts connecting them; (3) **between-cluster dissimilarity**: no fact in cluster A is similar (> threshold) to a fact in cluster B; (4) **monotonicity**: lowering the threshold never reduces cluster count. None of these are verified.
suggested_fix: Add a `#[cfg(test)] mod proptest_greedy_cluster` block in cluster.rs (mirroring `proptest_rrf` in hybrid.rs). Generate random `Vec<Fact>` with random unit-normalized embeddings and random thresholds in [0.0, 1.0]. Assert partition invariant: `clusters.iter().flatten().sorted().collect::<Vec<_>>() == (0..n).collect::<Vec<_>>()`. Assert no index appears twice. The similarity-chain and monotonicity properties can be checked with bounded exhaustive loops over the generated data.

title: 8 error variants have no Display/format assertion
description: The inline test mod in error.rs covers `NotFound`, `Database` (From impl only, no `to_string` check), `Serialization` (From impl only), `Reranker`, `ReadOnly`, `Lineage`, and `EmbeddingDimension`. The following variants have no `to_string()` assertion: `Conflict` (line 17), `Migration` (line 20), `NotImplemented` (line 23), `Pool` (line 26), `UnsupportedEpoch` (line 31, struct variant with interpolated fields `db_epoch`/`supported_epoch`), `Internal` (line 34), `Io` (line 37, `#[from]` but no display test), `Bootstrap` (line 40), `Archive` (line 46). The `UnsupportedEpoch` case is the highest risk: its format string references two numeric fields; a future rename would silently break the message without a test catching it.

title: ActivityStatus::from_str impl has no test — error path entirely uncovered
description: `ActivityStatus` implements `std::str::FromStr` at types.rs:511. The implementation and its error path (`"unknown activity status: {other}"` at line 520) are not exercised anywhere in the inline test mod (types.rs:598-868) or in tests/. The `Display` impl at types.rs:437-446 is also untested. Since `ActivityStatus` is stored in SQLite and round-tripped through string form, a mismatch between `Display` output and `from_str` input arms would be a silent data corruption bug.

title: Serde roundtrips for core types use only handcrafted examples; proptest would cover optional-field combinations
description: The serde tests in types.rs are example-based with fixed inputs. The most under-explored invariant is `PromotionProvenance`: `lineage_id` is marked `#[serde(skip_serializing, default)]` (line 217-218), so `decode(encode(x)).lineage_id` must always equal 0 regardless of input — a property that is currently checked for a single value (lineage_id=42, types.rs:836-854) but not against arbitrary values. Similarly, `Fact`'s `#[serde(default)] surfaced_at` (line 141) is tested with two JSON strings (lines 782-833) but not against arbitrary timestamp/null combinations. `proptest` is already in `Cargo.toml` dev-dependencies (line 42) and is used in subdirectory modules (`src/store/mod.rs`, `src/search/hybrid.rs`) — no infrastructure cost to add it here.

title: No fuzz targets exist; multiple deserialization entry-points are unfuzzed
description: The `fuzz/` directory is absent. The following types in scope are derived `Deserialize` and serve as entry-points for untrusted bytes: `Event`, `Fact`, `Edge`, `Summary`, `NewEvent`, `NewFact`, `PromotionProvenance`, `LineageRecord`, `LineageSnapshotEntry`, `Activity`, `SessionCheckpoint`, `Insight`, `CycleReport`. The MCP server (separate crate, not in scope) deserializes JSON from network; its payloads eventually flow through these types. `MemoryError::Serialization` (`#[from] serde_json::Error` at error.rs:11) is the expected failure mode — but whether deserialization panics on structurally valid but semantically extreme inputs (e.g. 768-dim embedding JSON with `Infinity` floats, or `importance` outside [0,1]) is untested. `Cargo.toml` has no `cargo-fuzz` or `libfuzzer-sys` dependency.

title: wiremock and tokio declared as dev-deps but unused in this crate
description: memory-engine-embed/Cargo.toml declares wiremock = "0.6" and tokio (with rt-multi-thread, macros) as dev-dependencies. There is no tests/ directory and no #[cfg(test)] block that uses either. The actual wiremock tests live in memory-engine-mcp/tests/embedding_integration.rs. Dead dev-deps inflate compile time and signal that intended integration tests were never written in this crate.
suggested_fix:
Either (a) add memory-engine-embed/tests/http_integration.rs that actually uses wiremock and tokio (resolves finding embed/testing-public-api-untested-in-crate at the same time), or (b) remove the two dev-deps from Cargo.toml until integration tests are added:

```toml
[dev-dependencies]
# wiremock and tokio removed — no tests/ yet
```

title: Several parse_openai_batch error branches have no inline tests
description:
parse_openai_batch has four distinct error paths; only two are covered by inline tests:
- Line 60-62: missing 'index' field → MemoryError::Internal — NOT tested.
- Line 66-71: unparseable 'embedding' value → MemoryError::Internal — NOT tested.
- Line 79-83: gap in index sequence (e.g. [0, 2] for expected 2) — tested by parse_openai_batch_gap_in_indices.
- Line 79-83: duplicate index (e.g. [0, 0]) — the error message says 'gap or duplicate' but only the gap case is exercised. A duplicate produces pairs [(0,_),(0,_)] after sort, so at i=1 idx=0 ≠ 1 → error. This branch is untested.

Similarly, parse_ollama_batch line 104-110 — unparseable inner array value — is not tested.

title: NaN/Inf rejection logic in embed() and embed_batch() is untested
description: Lines 174-177 (embed single) and 240-244 (embed_batch) guard against NaN and Inf values in embedding vectors, returning MemoryError::Internal. Neither path has any test — inline or integration. JSON does not natively represent NaN, but the validation operates on Vec<f32> after deserialization; a unit test can directly call a private or extracted validate function, or the MCP integration test layer can serve a body with specially crafted f64 values. Currently, if this guard were accidentally deleted, no test would catch it.

title: Strong proptest candidates with no property-based tests
description:
parse_openai_batch has a clean algebraic invariant: for any permutation P of indices 0..N with arbitrary Vec<f32> payloads, parse_openai_batch(&P, N) should succeed and return embeddings in index order — i.e. output[i] == P.embedding_where_index_eq_i. For any input that is NOT a permutation of 0..N (duplicate, gap, wrong length), the function should return Err. This invariant is ideal for proptest: it exercises the sort, the continuity check, and the count guard together with arbitrary inputs, not just the three hand-chosen cases currently present.

A secondary candidate: both parse_openai_batch and parse_ollama_batch should never panic on arbitrary serde_json::Value inputs (panic-safety property) — proptest can generate random Value trees and assert no_panic.

proptest is already a workspace dev-dep (root Cargo.toml line 41) but is not listed in memory-engine-embed/Cargo.toml.

title: No cargo-fuzz target for JSON response parsing
description: embed() and embed_batch() parse arbitrary JSON received over the network (lines 138-165 and 209-230). The format auto-detection logic branches over up to three response shapes and calls serde_json::from_value on untrusted content. A malformed or adversarially crafted server response (e.g. from a compromised or misconfigured endpoint) could trigger unexpected code paths. No fuzz/ directory exists anywhere in the workspace, so there are no fuzz targets at all. cargo-fuzz + libfuzzer can cheaply cover the parse_openai_batch, parse_ollama_batch, and format-detection paths.

title: Pure temporal helpers `passes_temporal_cutoff` and `fact_overlaps_period` lack property-based tests
description: `passes_temporal_cutoff` (line 690) and `fact_overlaps_period` (line 705) are free functions with clear algebraic invariants — interval containment and overlap — but have only implicit coverage from example-based query tests. No proptest verifies: (a) `passes_temporal_cutoff` is monotone in `cutoff` (if it passes at T it passes at T+ε when `t_invalid` is unbounded); (b) `fact_overlaps_period(f, s, e)` ↔ `fact_overlaps_period(f, s', e')` for all sub-intervals; (c) a fact with `t_valid > cutoff` never passes. These are the kind of off-by-one errors (< vs <=) that example tests routinely miss.

title: Snapshot serde roundtrip covered by a single example test; no property-based roundtrip
description: `snapshot.rs` has a single example-based roundtrip test (the happy path with one fact). The `write_to_file` → `load_from_file` pipeline involves two msgpack serializations, blake3 integrity check, and a u32 LE header length field. A proptest over arbitrary `SnapshotHeader`/`SnapshotPayload` fields (dimension, fact count, timestamps at boundary values like `i64::MIN`, `i64::MAX`) would catch endianness and overflow bugs that example tests miss. The current coverage also leaves the following `load_from_file` branches untested by proptest: truncated file, corrupted hash, mismatched embed_dim.
suggested_fix: Add a proptest in `snapshot.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)]` block that generates random valid fact counts (0..=100), write to a tempfile, and assert `load_from_file` returns `Some` with identical data. Separately, add a proptest that bit-flips a random byte and asserts `load_from_file` returns `None` (blake3 mismatch).

title: Promotion failure silently returns `ActivityStatus::Recorded` with no test
description: At `activity.rs:131-134`, when `add_fact` fails during promotion (e.g., embedding provider returns an error), the code silently swallows the error and returns `ActivityStatus::Recorded`. The activity record already exists in the DB at this point (inserted at line 94) with no `promoted_fact_id`. No test verifies this branch: that the status is `Recorded`, `promoted_fact_id` is `None`, and — critically — that no partial fact was left in the store. A failing embedder that returns `Ok(wrong_dim_vector)` would instead fail inside `add_fact`'s dimension check, leaving the caller unaware promotion was skipped.

title: `MockEmbedder` returns a constant vector, masking vector-ranking correctness
description: `MockEmbedder` always returns `vec![0.5; dim]` for every input. All vector similarity tests therefore see identical cosine scores for all facts, effectively disabling the vector ranking component of hybrid search. Any bug in the HNSW / vector-distance path that produces wrong ordering between distinct embeddings would go undetected. The `ReverseReranker` compensates for reranker ordering tests, but the embedding path itself (ANN distances, RRF weight blending) is never tested with distinguishable vectors in the main `tests.rs` suite.
suggested_fix: Add a `DeterministicEmbedder` to a shared `test_utils` module that maps known keywords to fixed orthogonal vectors (e.g., `"cats" → [1,0,0,0]`, `"dogs" → [0,1,0,0]`). Use it in at least two vector-search tests to verify that `query` returns the semantically closest fact first by cosine similarity. This makes the embedding path a real discriminant rather than a tie between constant vectors.

title: No test for prune() on an empty store
description: The `prune` function iterates `fact_store.list_active(None)` and then loops over `to_expire`. There is no inline or integration test that calls `prune` against a connection with zero active facts. The empty-collection path (`active_facts.len() == 0`) is never exercised: the loop bodies, the `tx.commit()`, and the `PruneStats { facts_expired: 0, facts_evaluated: 0 }` return are untested. If `fact_store.list_active` ever returns an Err on an empty table (schema mismatch, missing FTS5 virtual table, etc.) the regression would be invisible.

title: ebbinghaus_decay and compute_importance lack property-based tests
description: `ebbinghaus_decay(age, half_life)` is a pure mathematical function with well-defined invariants that proptest can exhaustively probe: (a) output is always in (0.0, 1.0] for any finite positive inputs, (b) monotone decreasing in `age_days` for fixed `half_life`, (c) monotone increasing in `half_life` for fixed `age_days`. Similarly, `compute_importance` with normalized inputs should always return a non-negative value (it could theoretically return 0.0 if all weights are 0 and importance is 0). The project already has proptest in `[dev-dependencies]` and six proptest blocks in other modules (`hybrid.rs`, `vector.rs`, `scope/tree.rs`, `store/facts.rs`, `store/schema.rs`, `store/mod.rs`), but none in the forgetting module. The existing example-based tests only check three specific decay values (age=0, half_life, 2×half_life).

title: remove_edges_by_fact has no unit test
description: MemoryGraph::remove_edges_by_fact is called by conflict resolution (src/conflict/temporal.rs:205) and archival (src/engine/archive.rs:85) but has zero tests in the graph module. Neither the happy path (node with both incoming and outgoing edges), the no-op path (unknown fact_id), nor the post-condition (node itself remains, only edges are gone) is exercised.

title: to_snapshot / from_snapshot lack a graph-level roundtrip test
description: to_snapshot and from_snapshot are the recovery path used by MemoryEngine::save and MemoryEngine::restore (src/engine/mod.rs:464, 338). The existing test in src/engine/snapshot.rs:469-498 only exercises file-level MessagePack serialization of GraphSnapshot structs — it does not verify that MemoryGraph state (topology, edge_id, weight, relation_type) is faithfully preserved through the MemoryGraph::to_snapshot → MemoryGraph::from_snapshot cycle. A weight-mangling or edge-drop regression in either function would be invisible.

title: Priority-order invariants in determine_state are untested
description: The priority chain "Expired > Invalidated > Pinned > Due > Active" (comment at line 86) is documented but never checked by a test that combines two conditions. Example gaps: (a) a pinned fact with `t_valid` in the past must return `Pinned`, not `Due`; (b) an expired pinned fact must return `Expired`, not `Pinned`. Without these combination tests, a future refactor that swaps priorities will pass all existing tests silently.
suggested_fix:
Add tests:
- `determine_state_pinned_beats_due`: add pinned fact with `t_valid` in past, assert `FactState::Pinned`.
- `determine_state_expired_beats_pinned`: set `t_expired` on a pinned fact via raw SQL, assert `FactState::Expired { .. }`.

title: build_graph_context tested only with degree-0 isolated facts
description: `build_graph_context` (explain.rs:134) computes `degree`, `neighbor_ids`, `component_size`, and calls `graph.connected_component` + `sort_unstable`. Every test creates facts with no edges, so the snapshot (`.snap`) shows `degree: 0, neighbor_ids: [], component_size: 0`. The paths for `graph.has_node(fact_id)` returning `true` with actual neighbors, the `filter(|&id| id != fact_id)` predicate, the sort, and the `component_size = neighbor_ids.len() + 1` formula are all untested.
suggested_fix: Create two facts, call `engine.consolidate()` (which creates edges) or use a raw `add_edge` path if available, then call `engine.explain_fact(fact_id)` and assert `graph_context.degree >= 1`, `!graph_context.neighbor_ids.is_empty()`, and `graph_context.component_size == graph_context.neighbor_ids.len() + 1`.

title: fact_history Expired timeline entry untested
description: `fact_history` pushes a `HistoryEventKind::Expired` entry (explain.rs:183-188) when `fact.t_expired.is_some()`. The test `fact_history_all_timestamps` (explain.rs:289) explicitly tests `t_valid + t_invalid` but its own comment states "no t_expired" (line 312). No test produces a 4-entry timeline or checks the sort order when `t_expired` is present. The `Expired` branch is dead code from the test suite's perspective.
suggested_fix: Add `fact_history_with_expired`: create a fact, set `t_expired` via raw SQL, call `engine.fact_history(id)`, and assert the timeline contains a `HistoryEventKind::Expired` entry and that the timeline is sorted ascending by timestamp.

title: to_event_filter only tests id_range and default order; six filter fields untested
description: `ReplayFilter` has eight fields: `since`, `until`, `id_range`, `session_id`, `event_type`, `limit`, `upcast`, and `order`. Only `id_range` (replay.rs:46) and `order == InsertionOrder` (replay.rs:68) are exercised end-to-end. The fields `since`, `until`, `session_id`, `event_type`, `limit`, and `ReplayOrder::TimestampOrder` pass through `to_event_filter` but no test verifies their mapping or behavioural effect on the returned events.
suggested_fix:
Add parameterized tests:
- `replay_filter_since`: ingest 5 events, pass `since = timestamp of event 3`, assert only events 3-5 returned.
- `replay_filter_session_id`: ingest events with two different session_ids, filter by one, assert only that session's events returned.
- `replay_filter_event_type`: ingest Interaction and Observation events, filter by type.
- `replay_filter_limit`: assert `limit: Some(2)` returns exactly 2 events.
- `replay_order_timestamp`: assert `TimestampOrder` results are sorted by timestamp not id.

title: SummaryStats.by_level aggregation path entirely untested
description: The `GROUP BY level` query and the three match arms (`"local"`, `"cluster"`, `"global"`) at statistics.rs:72-74 are never reached by any test. All tests call `engine.statistics()` without first producing summaries, so `summary_total == 0` and `by_level` is always empty. The match branch for `_ => continue` (unknown level) and the correct HashMap insertion are also unverified.
suggested_fix: After calling `engine.consolidate()` (which creates Local-level summaries with a mock `SummaryGenerator`), call `engine.statistics()` and assert `stats.summaries.total > 0` and `stats.summaries.by_level.contains_key(&ConsolidationLevel::Local)`.

title: dump_sqlite null-byte path guard untested
description: `dump_sqlite` rejects paths containing null bytes (dump.rs:213-218) with `MemoryError::Internal`. This guard prevents SQL injection via `VACUUM INTO '...'`. No test verifies the rejection. The null-byte check is only reached for file-backed engines (the `!is_file_backed` short-circuit at line 194 means in-memory engines never hit it), so an integration test with a file-backed engine is needed.
suggested_fix: Add `sqlite_dump_rejects_null_byte_path`: open a file-backed engine, construct a `PathBuf` from bytes containing `\0` (via `std::path::PathBuf::from(OsString::from_vec(b"output\0.db".to_vec()))` on Unix), call `dump_sqlite`, and assert `matches!(err, MemoryError::Internal(_))`.

title: MAX_SNAPSHOT_SIZE guard in read_snapshot has no test
description: `read_snapshot` (restore.rs:75-80) rejects files exceeding 4 GiB with `MemoryError::Internal`. This guard is never tested. While creating a 4 GiB file in a test is impractical, the guard uses `file.metadata().len()` which can be mocked by creating a sparse file or by temporarily lowering the constant. The risk: a future refactor that changes the size check silently removes an OOM protection.

title: Lineage restore path never exercised — all tests use lineage: vec![]
description: Step 7 of `restore_snapshot_into` (restore.rs:342-348) calls `LineageStore::insert_raw(entry)` for each lineage record. Every test in `restore.rs` and `restore_roundtrip_test.rs` constructs snapshots with `lineage: vec![]`. The `insert_raw` path, the autoincrement reset for `lineage` (restore.rs:385-391), and the `lineage_count` guard in `assert_empty_db` (restore.rs:180) are all untested.
suggested_fix: Add `restore_roundtrip_with_lineage`: build a `LineageSnapshotEntry` (or use the Phase 5a API when available), include it in the snapshot, restore into a fresh connection, and assert `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lineage` equals 1 and that a new insert after restore gets an id > the imported lineage_id.

title: NotImplemented path when compression feature is disabled has no test
description: `read_snapshot` returns `MemoryError::NotImplemented` when gzip or zstd magic bytes are detected but the corresponding feature is disabled (restore.rs:98-103 under `#[cfg(not(feature = "compress-gzip"))]`, and restore.rs:113-117 under `#[cfg(not(feature = "compress-zstd"))]`). No test exercises this path. Because the functions are feature-gated, a test must run in a configuration that disables both features — the default feature set — and provide a file with gzip or zstd magic bytes.

title: No property-based test for EngineSnapshot serde roundtrip
description: `EngineSnapshot` is the contract between `dump` and `restore`. It is serialized by `stream_snapshot` and deserialized by `read_snapshot` (both JSON). The codebase uses `proptest` (Cargo.toml:41) for embedding roundtrips (`store/mod.rs:122`), content-hash determinism (`store/facts.rs:1427`), and RRF merge (`search/hybrid.rs:503`), but there is no property-based test verifying `serde_json::from_str(serde_json::to_string(snapshot)) == snapshot` for arbitrary `EngineSnapshot` values. Given that `EngineSnapshot` carries bi-temporal timestamps, embeddings, and optional fields, hand-crafted examples may miss corner cases in the custom serde logic.

title: No fuzz targets for read_snapshot (untrusted JSON + compression deserialization)
description: `read_snapshot` (restore.rs:71) opens a file, detects compression from magic bytes, and then passes the content to `serde_json::from_reader` (potentially through `flate2::read::GzDecoder` or `zstd::Decoder`). These code paths accept attacker-controlled bytes and perform complex parsing. There is no `fuzz/` directory in the workspace and no cargo-fuzz targets. `validate_snapshot` is a secondary target — it parses the deserialized struct for invariants. Both are strong candidates for fuzzing given the project's safety posture (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`).
suggested_fix:
Create a `fuzz/` directory with `cargo fuzz init`, add two targets:
1. `fuzz_read_snapshot`: feed raw bytes as the file content to `read_snapshot`.
2. `fuzz_validate_snapshot`: deserialize bytes as `EngineSnapshot` and pass to `validate_snapshot`.
Seed corpus: the existing `*.json` dump files from the test suite.

title: HttpSummaryGenerator multi-format response auto-detection is exercised only by a system-prompt-non-empty smoke test
description: summary.rs implements a three-branch response auto-detector (lines 107-121): OpenAI format (choices[0].message.content), Ollama format (message.content), and neither (returns Err). A fourth branch (line 97-102) handles API-level errors embedded in 200 responses. The only inline test (line 141) checks that SUMMARIZE_SYSTEM_PROMPT is non-empty, which does not exercise any of this logic. The embedding_integration.rs tests exercise HttpEmbeddingProvider but never HttpSummaryGenerator. A broken OpenAI→Ollama format detection would be invisible in CI.
suggested_fix: Add wiremock-based tests for HttpSummaryGenerator mirroring the pattern in embedding_integration.rs: (1) a 200 response in OpenAI format: `{"choices":[{"message":{"content":"summary text"}}]}`; (2) a 200 response in Ollama format: `{"message":{"content":"summary text"}}`; (3) a 200 response with `{"error":{"message":"rate limited"}}`—should return Err; (4) a 200 response in neither known format—should return Err with a message containing the response body. Each case exercises a different branch of the content extraction at lines 107-128.

title: all_tool_definitions_returns_23 hardcodes tool count — will false-positive on every addition
description: Line 764 asserts `defs.len() == 23` with an explanation comment naming the exact breakdown. This assertion will fail on every tool addition even if the list is internally consistent, and it will also silently pass if a tool is accidentally removed and another added. The intent (no duplicates, no gaps) is better served by the uniqueness test on line 773, which is structurally correct and does not need updating.
suggested_fix: Remove the hardcoded count assertion or replace it with a lower-bound and invariant check: `assert!(!defs.is_empty(), "must have tools"); assert!(defs.len() >= 10, "must have at least P0 tools");`. Keep the uniqueness test as the primary structural guard.

title: Strong property-based testing candidates have only example-based tests
description: Two functions are strong proptest candidates: (1) depth::truncate (lines 27-37) — the fn must guarantee both output.len() <= max AND s.is_char_boundary(output.len()) for all UTF-8 inputs; the existing unit test at depth.rs:405-411 uses a single hand-crafted emoji string and cannot explore the full character boundary space. (2) parse_embedding (tools/mod.rs:467-474) — for any Vec<f32> serialised to JSON then parsed back, the round-trip must yield the exact same vector; currently only happy-path dispatch tests exercise it. proptest is already present in the root crate's dev-dependencies (Cargo.toml line 24) but the mcp crate does not declare it.
suggested_fix: Add `proptest = "1"` to [dev-dependencies] in memory-engine-mcp/Cargo.toml. Then add proptest tests in depth.rs: `proptest! { #[test] fn truncate_always_valid_utf8(s in ".*", max in 0usize..500) { let t = truncate(&s, max); assert!(t.len() <= max); assert!(s.is_char_boundary(t.len())); } }`. Add a round-trip test for parse_embedding: `proptest! { #[test] fn embedding_roundtrip(vals in prop::collection::vec(-1.0f32..1.0, 1..128)) { let json = serde_json::to_value(&vals).unwrap(); let map = [("embedding", json)].into_iter().collect(); let result = parse_embedding(&map).unwrap().unwrap(); assert_eq!(result, vals); } }`

title: write() is untested on a read-only pool and silently bypasses the guard
description: ConnectionPool::write() (line 206) locks and returns write_conn unconditionally — it does not check self.read_only. Only try_write() (line 213) enforces the guard. Production callers in src/inspect/replay.rs:50,71 and src/engine/restore.rs:55,84 call pool.write() directly. Those paths are currently only reachable through non-read-only pools, but there is no compile-time or runtime enforcement in write() itself, and no unit test verifies the contract 'write() on a read_only pool still locks the underlying connection (does not error)' versus 'should it panic or be deprecated?'. The intended separation of concerns between write() and try_write() is undocumented at the call-site level and untested.

title: Condvar blocking behavior (pool exhaustion) is never tested with actual threads
description: The test pool_file_backed_concurrent_reads (line 268) opens a pool with read_pool_size=2 and checks out 2 connections simultaneously — but all on the same thread. The Condvar/blocking path (line 195-196: `while conns.is_empty() { self.read_available.wait(&mut conns); }`) is exercised only trivially. There is no test that spawns N+1 threads to actually block one reader until a guard is dropped, proving the Condvar wakeup fires correctly. A deadlock or spurious-wakeup bug in the notify_one path would not be caught by existing tests.

title: scope_path=Some(existing path) branch never exercised by any test
description: All resume_context tests in src/engine/tests.rs and tests/phase3b_lifecycle_test.rs pass either scope_path=None (root) or a nonexistent path to trigger NotFound. The branch at engine/resume.rs:25-35 — where resolve_path succeeds, tree.ancestors(id) is called, and a non-root scope_ids slice is passed to list_by_importance_score and list_by_scopes_recent — is therefore untested. If a child scope exists and has facts, no test verifies that the ancestor chain correctly filters the results, or that facts from a sibling scope are excluded from the 'recent' and 'high_importance' tiers.
suggested_fix: Add a test that: (1) creates a child scope via engine.ensure_scope_path("project/alpha"), (2) adds facts at the child scope and a sibling scope, (3) calls resume_context with scope_path=Some("project/alpha"), and (4) asserts facts from the sibling scope are absent from all non-pinned tiers.

title: Tier mutual-exclusivity invariant covered by a single example test; no property test
description: The headline contract of resume_context — 'no fact appears in multiple tiers' — is verified by exactly one manually constructed scenario in the inline test resume_tiers_mutually_exclusive (context.rs:200). This example covers only a single combination of fact attributes (one pinned, one high-importance, one due, one recent). The invariant is sensitive to changes in the tier-ordering logic or the HashSet exclusion tracking at context.rs:76-102. A property-based test varying fact counts, importance scores, t_valid timestamps, and cap values would give much stronger assurance.

title: No test verifies that a second resume_context call does not re-stamp surfaced_at
description: The is_unsurfaced_due closure at engine/resume.rs:47-51 guards against re-stamping by checking f.surfaced_at.is_none(). The FactStore::stamp_surfaced implementation at store/facts.rs:484-486 also has an 'AND surfaced_at IS NULL' guard. Both gates are correct but neither is covered by a test that calls resume_context twice on the same due fact. A second call should leave surfaced_at unchanged (same timestamp); if either guard drifts, re-stamping would update the timestamp, breaking monotonicity of the surfacing record.

title: is_unsurfaced_due closure duplicates list_due predicate with no shared test
description: The is_unsurfaced_due closure at engine/resume.rs:47-51 re-implements the same temporal predicate as FactStore::list_due (store/facts.rs:403-405): t_valid IS NOT NULL AND t_valid <= now AND (t_invalid IS NULL OR t_invalid > now). The two predicates can silently drift. For example, if the list_due query added a scope filter or changed the null-t_valid handling, the surfacing stamp would become inconsistent. No test verifies both predicates agree on the same fact population.
suggested_fix: Extract the temporal predicate into a shared free function `fn is_temporally_due(fact: &Fact, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> bool` in the resume module and call it from both the closure and (via a FactStore adapter) from the SQL WHERE clause logic. Add a test asserting: facts returned by list_due(now, &[]) == facts for which is_temporally_due returns true, over a corpus with varied t_valid/t_invalid combinations.

title: path_for_id: root-returns-slash and unknown-id-returns-None branches are untested
description: The doc comment (lines 141-142) documents two special cases: path_for_id(root_id) returns Some("/") and path_for_id(unknown_id) returns None. Neither is asserted in any test. The proptest resolve_roundtrip (line 325) exercises only non-root paths generated by scope_path, so the root branch (line 151-152) and the early-None branch (line 148-150) have zero test coverage. The None branch wraps an unreachable? node.parent_id walk that panics on an orphaned node — this is undetected.

title: inherited() only tested on a leaf node — dedup branch for nodes with children is unexercised
description: The existing test inherited_combines_ancestors_and_subtree (line 255) calls inherited(demo_id) where demo_id is a leaf. subtree(leaf) == [leaf], so the `if id != scope_id { result.push(id); }` dedup branch (line 96-98) iterates over only one element and immediately skips. The non-trivial case — a mid-tree node whose subtree has real descendants — is never tested. For example, inherited(user_id) should return [user_id, root_id, demo_id, other_id] (4 items), but no test asserts this.

title: ancestors() and subtree() silently return a singleton vec for an unknown scope_id — undocumented and untested
description: ancestors(99999) pushes 99999, then nodes.get(&99999) returns None, so the loop exits with result = vec![99999]. subtree(99999) similarly returns vec![99999]. Neither the doc comment on ancestors (line 60) nor on subtree (line 71) documents this behavior. Callers in the query path (engine/query.rs, via resolve_query) use these results directly as SQL IN-list filters — an unrecognized scope_id leaks through as if it were a valid scope, potentially returning no rows (benign) but also masking bugs where a scope was never inserted. The behavior is inconsistent with path_for_id(99999) which returns None.

title: `rrf_merge` missing edge-case tests: both-empty, k=0, duplicate IDs within one list
description:
Three edge cases for `rrf_merge` (a pure, public function) are untested:
1. **Both lists empty** — no test for `rrf_merge(&[], &[], k)`, which should return `vec![]`.
2. **k=0** — proptest range at line 508/527/540 is `1..120u32`, so k=0 is never exercised. At k=0 the denominator is `0 + rank + 1`, a valid result, but unverified.
3. **Duplicate IDs within a single list** — e.g. `[(1, -1.0), (1, -2.0)]` in the FTS list; `scores.entry(id)` accumulates the score twice, which may be an unintended boost. No test documents the intended behavior.

title: `cosine_similarity` silently truncates mismatched-length slices — behavior undocumented and untested
description: `cosine_similarity` uses `a.iter().zip(b.iter())` at line 21, which silently computes similarity over the prefix of the shorter slice when `a.len() != b.len()`. This is a public `#[must_use]` function with no length check and no test for the mismatched case. No doc comment mentions truncation behavior. Callers computing partial inner products against higher-dimensional vectors will get a silently wrong result. The proptest strategies at line 284/305 enforce `len = a.len().min(b.len())` before calling, masking the issue. CWE-129 (unchecked slice indexing), CWE-682 (incorrect calculation).

title: `rerank_depth` widening logic untested at `hybrid_search` unit level
description: The invariant at line 144 — `effective_target = rerank_depth.unwrap_or(limit).max(limit)` (can only widen, never shrink) — is exercised by one test in `src/engine/tests.rs:1952` that goes through the full engine stack. The four unit tests inside `hybrid.rs` all pass `rerank_depth: None`. Two specific behaviors have no unit coverage in `hybrid.rs`: (1) `rerank_depth < limit` is clamped to `limit` and (2) `rerank_depth > limit` widens the candidate pool above the limit before truncation.

title: `fts_search` with empty query string `""` is untested
description: No test exercises `fts_search` with `query = ""`. FTS5 treats an empty MATCH string as either a syntax error (returning `vec![]` via the error catch at line 66-70) or an empty result set — the actual behavior is not documented and not verified. Similarly `fts_count_expired` is never called with an empty query. These are easy reachable inputs from `execute_query` when a caller passes an empty text string via `MemoryQuery::text("")` or `SearchQuery { text: Some("".into()), .. }`.

title: `Some(&[])` empty scope_ids slice produces zero results — undocumented, untested
description: When `scope_ids = Some(&[])`, `serde_json::to_string` produces `"[]"`, and `scope_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each('[]'))` returns an empty set — no facts will ever match. The condition `?3 IS NULL OR scope_id IN (...)` evaluates to false for every row because the subquery is empty. This is different from `None` (which matches all scopes) and likely represents a footgun: a caller computing scope IDs dynamically with an empty result will silently get zero search results rather than all results. The same pattern exists in `fts_search` (line 44), `fts_count_expired` (line 108), `vector_search` (line 62), and `check_fact_filters` in `ann.rs` (line 368). None of the tests cover `Some(&[])`.

title: `HnswStrategy::search` early-return for empty index untested
description: The guard at line 251-253 (`if n_items == 0 { return Ok(Vec::new()); }`) handles the case where the HNSW index is empty (no facts in DB). This is also the path exercised at cold start before any facts are inserted. The unit tests in `ann.rs::hnsw_strategy_tests` all start by inserting three facts via `setup_with_facts()`. No test calls `HnswStrategy::search` on an empty index. Feature-gated behind `ann`; cannot be verified without `--all-features`.
fallback_tier: ann feature-gated — not compiled in default build

title: `HnswStrategy::search` dimension-mismatch error path untested
description: The `EmbeddingDimension` error path at line 230-234 (query embedding length != `self.embed_dim`) is not covered by any test in `ann.rs`. The analogous check in `vector_search` has a test (`vector_search_rejects_wrong_query_dimension` at `vector.rs:168`), but the HNSW path does not. Feature-gated behind `ann`.
fallback_tier: ann feature-gated — not compiled in default build

title: schema::list_config has no test
description: get_config and set_config both have tests. list_config (line 136-150) — which returns all key-value pairs from the config table — has none. This is particularly important because list_config is the mechanism through which tooling inspects schema_version and storage_epoch; a regression would be silent.
suggested_fix: Add a test that inserts two config keys via set_config, calls list_config, and asserts both keys and values are present in the returned HashMap.

title: LineageStore::insert with empty source_fact_ids skips validation silently
description: At line 37, insert short-circuits with an early return when source_fact_ids is empty: if !record.source_fact_ids.is_empty() skips the FK-existence check loop entirely, inserting a lineage record with source_fact_ids='[]'. No test covers this path. The empty-source case may represent a logic error in the caller, and it is currently undetectable.
suggested_fix: Add a test inserting a LineageRecord with source_fact_ids: vec![] and assert the resulting stored record has empty source_fact_ids. Consider whether empty source_fact_ids should be an error.

title: SummaryStore::for_each and list_all have no tests
description: list_all (line 117) and for_each (line 138) are both untested. list_all is a full-table scan; for_each is a callback-based iterator used by export and consolidation pipelines. Both are load-bearing for the Phase 5 DreamCycle pipeline.
suggested_fix: Add tests: (1) list_all on empty store returns empty vec; (2) list_all after inserts returns all items; (3) for_each visits every item exactly once.

title: ScopeStore::for_each has no test
description: ScopeStore::for_each (line 165) iterates all scopes via a user-supplied callback. It is untested — neither the happy path (all scopes visited) nor the early-return-on-error case is exercised.
suggested_fix: Add tests: (1) for_each on empty store calls callback zero times; (2) for_each after inserting N scopes visits each exactly once; (3) if callback returns Err, the error propagates.

title: Test setup() uses raw Connection::open_in_memory() — PRAGMA foreign_keys not enabled
description: Both activities.rs and checkpoints.rs define a setup() that calls Connection::open_in_memory().unwrap() followed by init_schema(). They do NOT use open_memory() from schema.rs, which sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON among other pragmas. As a result, FK violations against scopes(id) in the activities.scope_id column and against activities(id) in the session_checkpoints.last_activity_id column are silently ignored in all tests in these two files. Tests can pass with invalid foreign keys that would fail in production.
suggested_fix: Replace Connection::open_in_memory() with a call to open_memory() (or manually execute PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON after opening) in both setup() functions. Alternatively, extract a shared test_utils::in_memory_db() helper that always calls open_memory() and use it everywhere.

title: UpcasterRegistry chain composition lacks property-based tests
description: The upcaster has example-based tests for chains of length 1 and 2, but no proptest that verifies the fundamental composition property: upcast(payload, from_rev, n) applied iteratively for arbitrary chain lengths equals a direct upcast from from_rev to latest. Properties to verify: (1) upcast is idempotent when from_rev == current_rev; (2) chained single-step upcasts produce the same result as a direct multi-step upcast; (3) attempting to upcast from a revision higher than the latest returns an error. A mutant upcaster that skips one step in the chain could pass all existing tests.
suggested_fix: Add a proptest module in upcaster.rs that generates arbitrary revision chains (0..=10), registers incrementing upcasters, and verifies the composition invariant. Use proptest::collection::vec to generate chain lengths.

title: parse_timestamp and parse_optional_timestamp have no property-based roundtrip tests
description: mod.rs has proptest coverage for embedding serialization roundtrips, but not for the two timestamp parse helpers. parse_timestamp and parse_optional_timestamp are called in every row-mapping function across all store modules — a regression here would silently corrupt all datetime fields. The property to verify: for any DateTime<Utc> value d, parse_timestamp(d.to_rfc3339()) == d. parse_optional_timestamp on a non-RFC3339 string should return a rusqlite::Error.
suggested_fix: Add a proptest block in mod.rs alongside the existing proptest_embedding module, generating arbitrary Unix timestamps and verifying the serialize/parse roundtrip. Also add a negative test with arbitrary non-RFC3339 strings (e.g., via proptest::string::string_regex for invalid formats) asserting parse returns Err.

title: No fuzz targets exist — parse_timestamp with arbitrary byte strings is highest priority
description: There is no fuzz/ directory in the workspace. parse_timestamp and parse_optional_timestamp both take &str from SQLite column values. While SQLite controls input in production, a corrupted DB or a migration path that stores a malformed timestamp string would cause rusqlite::Error at read time rather than a panic — but the error conversion path (Box::new(e) into FromSqlConversionFailure) has not been stress-tested. A fuzz target is particularly valuable because DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339 from the chrono crate has historically had edge cases around leap seconds, timezone designators, and sub-second precision that break parsing assumptions.
suggested_fix: Create a fuzz/ directory with cargo-fuzz. Add a fuzz target fuzz_parse_timestamp that takes arbitrary &[u8], converts to str if valid UTF-8, and calls parse_timestamp — asserting it never panics (only returns Ok or Err). Enable with cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_parse_timestamp.

title: No integration test exercises --all-features store interactions
description: The integration tests in tests/roundtrip_test.rs and tests/read_only_test.rs run without feature flags. The archive feature gates ArchiveManifestStore; the ann feature gates HNSW vector search. No integration test verifies that (1) a DB opened with the archive feature behaves correctly when archive_manifest records coexist with live facts, or (2) the ann feature's HNSW index is correctly maintained across ingest/expire cycles. The workspace-level cargo test --all-features is in the CLAUDE.md gate but no test file specifically targets these combinations.
suggested_fix: Add a tests/feature_flags_test.rs that is conditionally compiled per feature (using #[cfg(feature = "archive")] and #[cfg(feature = "ann")]) and exercises at least one round-trip per gated code path.

title: Integration tests do not cover bi-temporal query semantics
description: The roundtrip_test.rs exercises FTS, vector, and hybrid search but no integration test exercises bi-temporal queries: list_active_at (as-of a past time), list_active_in_period (facts valid in a time window), or the interaction between t_valid/t_invalid and expire semantics. The bi-temporal model is a core design invariant (4 timestamps per fact; soft deletion) and is only tested at the unit level in facts.rs — not through the public MemoryEngine facade.
suggested_fix: Add an integration test in tests/ that ingests facts with different t_valid/t_invalid windows, then queries list_active_at for multiple as-of timestamps and asserts the correct subset is returned at each point in time.

title: Consolidate and forget pipelines have no integration-level test
description: The roundtrip integration test covers ingest and query but not consolidate or forget. These are the two highest-complexity pipeline operations and have no end-to-end test through MemoryEngine — only unit-level tests (if any) within the engine module. A regression in the forget decay curve or the consolidation dedup pass would not be caught at the integration level.
suggested_fix: Add integration tests that call MemoryEngine::consolidate() and MemoryEngine::forget() with mock trait implementations and assert post-conditions: facts below importance threshold are expired, duplicate facts are merged into summaries, etc.

title: ROLLBACK TO and RELEASE errors silently discarded in savepoint error path
description: In the `Err(e)` arm at lines 111-112, both `conn.execute_batch("ROLLBACK TO bootstrap")` and `conn.execute_batch("RELEASE bootstrap")` use `let _ = ...`, which discards any error without logging. If the rollback itself fails (e.g., the connection is in a broken state), the savepoint is left open and the write connection's transaction state becomes undefined. The original error `e` is returned, but the rollback failure is invisible.

title: content_truncation test assertion allows 3 extra bytes, contradicting its own comment
description: The comment at line 223 says "The truncated content (minus the '...' suffix) must be <= 2000 chars". `build_content` truncates the prefix to at most `MAX_LEN` (2000) bytes and appends `"..."` (3 bytes), so the maximum total length is 2003. The assertion on line 224 is `content.len() <= 2003 + 3` (i.e., <= 2006), which permits a 3-byte overrun beyond the stated invariant. The correct bound is `<= 2003`.
suggested_fix:
Replace:
```rust
assert!(facts[0].content.len() <= 2003 + 3);
```
with:
```rust
assert!(facts[0].content.len() <= 2003, "truncated content must be at most MAX_LEN + 3 bytes for '...'");
```

title: Bare unreachable!() tightly couples value_parser literal list to match arms
description: The `target` field uses `value_parser = ["facts", "events", "all"]` (line 14) to constrain inputs, and the match at line 53 relies on this to make `_ => unreachable!()` safe. If a new variant is added to the value_parser list without updating the match (easy to do since they are in different locations), the code compiles but panics at runtime on any call with the new value. A typed enum (deriving `clap::ValueEnum`) would make this exhaustive at compile-time and eliminate the implicit coupling.

title: truncate_str produces output longer than max_chars when max_chars < 3
description: When `max_chars` is less than 3, `max_chars.saturating_sub(3)` returns 0 and `take(0)` yields an empty string, so the result is `"..."` (3 chars), which exceeds `max_chars`. No current caller triggers this (callers pass 60 and 80), but the function's contract is violated for small values. The guard `s.chars().count() <= max_chars` also scans the entire string on each call, performing O(n) work even when the string is short enough — a minor inefficiency for a display function.

title: `expire_and_invalidate` returns `MemoryError::NotFound` for both missing and already-expired facts
description: The SQL is `UPDATE facts SET t_expired = ?1, t_invalid = ?1 WHERE id = ?2 AND t_expired IS NULL`. If the row exists with `t_expired IS NOT NULL`, `changed == 0` and the function returns `MemoryError::NotFound(format!("fact {fact_id}"))`. Callers cannot distinguish "row gone" from "already soft-deleted", which matters because the latter is a benign race while the former is a real bug. Distinct error variants give the engine room to retry or no-op on already-expired facts.

title: list_active has no ORDER BY — iteration order is non-deterministic across SQLite versions/vacuums
description: `FactStore::list_active(None)` issues `SELECT … FROM facts WHERE t_expired IS NULL` with no `ORDER BY`. SQLite does not guarantee row order for such queries; it can change after a VACUUM, page shuffle, or across library versions. `local_dedup` iterates `new_facts` in this unspecified order, and the dedup winner when multiple facts have equal importance depends on which fact appears first in the iteration (the first-encountered fact wins all subsequent comparisons). This makes the surviving fact — and therefore which `importance_score` is inherited — non-deterministic across runs.
suggested_fix: Add `ORDER BY id ASC` to `FactStore::list_active` (or a dedicated `list_active_ordered` variant) so that `local_dedup` always iterates facts in insertion order. This gives deterministic behavior: the lowest-id (oldest) fact always wins multi-way equal-importance comparisons, which matches the documented tie-break intent.

title: tokio::task::JoinError silently mapped to MemoryError::Pool (connection-pool variant)
description: The `join_err` helper at async_engine.rs:41 maps any `tokio::task::JoinError` to `MemoryError::Pool`. The `Pool` variant's doc (error.rs:25-26) says "connection pool error", meaning it is semantically reserved for failures in the SQLite connection pool. A Tokio task panic or cancellation is a fundamentally different failure mode and will be misclassified. Callers that match on `MemoryError::Pool` expecting a pool exhaustion error will silently mishandle panics in the blocking thread pool.
references: CWE-390 (Detection of Error Condition Without Action)

title: Outcome Display produces lowercase but serde JSON and payload doc specify PascalCase
description: The doc comment for `EventType::OutcomeSignal` at types.rs:17 states the payload carries `"outcome": "Positive"|"Negative"|"Neutral"`. Because `Outcome` derives `Serialize`/`Deserialize` with no `rename_all` attribute, serde uses PascalCase enum variant names ("Positive", "Negative", "Neutral"). However, the `Display` impl (types.rs:33-41) produces lowercase (`"positive"`, `"negative"`, `"neutral"`). Any code that constructs or validates payload JSON via `outcome.to_string()` rather than `serde_json::to_value(&outcome)` will silently produce the wrong casing, causing mismatches when DreamCycle queries outcome history by comparing string values.
references: CWE-116 (Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output)

title: `embed()` format detection does not guard that `data` is an array, so it short-circuits before trying the `embeddings` fallback
description: At line 145, `body.get("data")` returns `Some` for any JSON value under the key `"data"` — including objects and scalars. `data.get(0)` on a non-array `Value` silently returns `None`, so `embedding` is set to `None` and the `embeddings`/`embedding` branches are never tried. If a server returns `{"data": {"count": 0}, "embeddings": [[...]]}` (a valid Ollama-style response with an extraneous `data` key), `embed()` fails with an unhelpful "cannot extract embedding" error. By contrast, `embed_batch()` correctly uses `.and_then(|d| d.as_array())` at line 216, making only `embed()` vulnerable. Severity is low because most real endpoints don't mix these keys.

title: Silent narrowing cast `u64 as usize` can corrupt index validation on 32-bit targets
description: At line 62, `item.get("index").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).ok_or_else(...)? as usize` casts a `u64` index value to `usize` via `as`, which truncates modulo 2^32 on 32-bit targets. A malicious or buggy server returning `index = 2^32 + 1` (u64) becomes `idx = 1` (usize on 32-bit). The subsequent continuity check at lines 78-84 verifies `idx == i`, so it would accept `[(0, emb0), (1, emb1)]` as valid when the real indices were `[0, 4294967297]` — silently returning a wrong embedding for the second text. The crate's deployment context is almost exclusively 64-bit AI inference hosts, so practical impact is negligible, but the cast is still unsound by construction.

title: Serialization failure in Depth::Full silently returns json!(null)
description: `shape_explanation` at `Depth::Full` calls `serde_json::to_value(explanation).unwrap_or_else(|e| { tracing::error!(...); json!(null) })`. A serialization error swallows the failure and returns a `null` value to the caller as if it were valid data. `FactExplanation` currently derives `Serialize` on all primitive/stdlib types, so the error is unreachable in practice, but the pattern masks future fields that might introduce fallible serialization. The caller (`handle_explain_fact`) has no way to distinguish a null explanation from an error.
suggested_fix: Change the return type of `shape_explanation` to `Result<Value, ErrorData>` and propagate the error via `serde_json::to_value(explanation).map_err(|e| ErrorData::internal_error(...))`.

title: Doc comment incorrectly claims PRAGMA query_only=ON is set for read-only connections
description: The doc comment for open_read_only() at lines 143-144 states: 'All connections have `PRAGMA query_only = ON`, including the internal slot used for cache loading during initialization.' In practice, open_connection_read_only() (schema.rs:38-46) opens connections with SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX flags and calls set_pragmas_read_only() which sets only foreign_keys and busy_timeout (schema.rs:60-66) — no query_only pragma is issued. The OS-level flag is actually a stronger guarantee than the pragma, so the implementation is correct; only the doc is wrong. A reader relying on the doc to audit the security boundary will be misled.

title: ResumeConfig::Default captures Utc::now() at construction time — stale if config is stored before use
description: The `Default` implementation for `ResumeConfig` (context.rs:29-41) captures `now: Utc::now()` at struct-construction time. If a caller stores a `ResumeConfig::default()` value and passes it to `resume_context` after a delay, the `now` field is stale: due-fact evaluation (`t_valid <= now`) and the `is_unsurfaced_due` closure in `engine/resume.rs:49` will use a past timestamp, causing future-dated facts to be surfaced prematurely or not at all. The MCP handler (memory-engine-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:755) correctly overrides `now: Utc::now()` at call time, so the production path is safe today — but a caller relying solely on `Default` in any non-immediate pattern (e.g., building a config at startup and reusing it across sessions) will get wrong due-tier results silently.

title: ancestors() called with an unknown scope_id returns [scope_id] instead of empty
description: ancestors() takes any i64 without precondition. If scope_id is not present in self.nodes, the loop body executes once (pushing scope_id), then self.nodes.get(&id) returns None so the loop terminates, yielding vec![scope_id]. The caller receives a one-element vec containing an invalid ID — indistinguishable from a valid leaf-only scope. This is currently low-risk because all in-engine callers obtain scope_id from resolve_path first, but the method is public (pub) and the contract is undocumented, making misuse easy. A consumer calling tree.ancestors(some_unknown_id) would silently pass a bogus scope list to SQL queries.

title: Fact-ID validation query uses string interpolation instead of parameterized binding
description: In `LineageStore::insert`, the validation query is built by formatting `i64` IDs directly into SQL: `format!("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM facts WHERE id IN ({placeholders})")` where `placeholders` is comma-joined `i64::to_string()` outputs. While `i64` values cannot contain SQL metacharacters, this pattern diverges from the parameterized-query discipline used everywhere else in the store, and SQLite cannot cache the statement plan across different call sites. The correct pattern (already used in several other methods) is `json_each` with a single JSON-array parameter.

title: `ArchivePolicy::default()` calls `Utc::now()`, making `Default` non-deterministic and untestable
description: Current state: `impl Default for ArchivePolicy` sets `expired_before: Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::days(30)` (types.rs:31). Every call to `ArchivePolicy::default()` produces a different value, which is unexpected for `Default` semantics and makes deterministic testing impossible — the test at types.rs:81 already works around this with `diff.num_days() == 30 || diff.num_days() == 29`. Target state: document this explicitly or change the design so the caller supplies `expired_before`. One approach: remove `Default`, add a constructor `ArchivePolicy::last_n_days(n: u32) -> Self` that computes the cutoff at call time. Another: keep `Default` but document it as a snapshot of 'now'. Refactoring pattern: Replace Magic Default with Named Constructor. Motivation: correctness — snapshot semantics are surprising; testability. Estimated scope: src/archive/types.rs, any caller using `ArchivePolicy::default()`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: low — API change only, and `ArchivePolicy` is re-exported only under `#[cfg(feature = "archive")]`.

title: `commit_archive` takes 7 arguments — introduce a local value-object
description: Current state: `commit_archive` at engine/archive.rs:219 takes `&self`, `pak_filename`, `facts`, `edges`, `fact_ids`, `pak_size_bytes`, `blake3_hash` — 7 parameters. The caller at archive.rs:72-79 must pass `candidate_facts`, `candidate_edges`, `fact_ids`, `pak_size_bytes`, `blake3_hash` individually, some of which are derived from `candidate_facts` inside `commit_archive` itself (fact_id_min/max, t_created_min/max). This is a data-clump: the pak metadata belongs together. The function also has `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_wrap)]` for `facts.len() as i64` and `pak_size_bytes as i64`. Target state: extract a `PakMetadata { pak_filename, pak_size_bytes, blake3_hash }` struct (private) and pass `(&PakMetadata, &[Fact], &[Edge])`, letting `commit_archive` derive the aggregates. The `cast_possible_wrap` suppression can then be replaced with `i64::try_from(...).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)` or documented with a range invariant. Refactoring pattern: Introduce Parameter Object / Extract Value Object. Motivation: coupling reduction — the call site and callee share a data dependency that is currently expressed through parallel variables. Estimated scope: 1 file (engine/archive.rs). Prerequisites: none. Risk: low (private helper; no public API surface change).

title: `max_turns: usize` uses `0` as a sentinel for "no limit" — stringly-typed boolean embedded in an integer
description: `BootstrapConfig::max_turns` uses the value `0` to mean "unlimited" (see `mod.rs:162`: `if config.max_turns > 0`). This is a boolean-in-integer encoding that the type system cannot enforce and that callers must learn from documentation. Current state: `pub max_turns: usize` with default `0`, guarded by `> 0` check. Target state: `pub max_turns: Option<NonZeroUsize>` — `None` means unlimited, `Some(n)` means limit to n. This eliminates the sentinel and makes the API self-documenting. The MCP layer (`memory-engine-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:1235`) would change from `max_turns: get_usize(&args, "max_turns").unwrap_or(0)` to `max_turns: NonZeroUsize::new(get_usize(...).unwrap_or(0))`. Refactoring pattern: Replace Magic Number with Type. Motivation: misuse-resistance, no documentation needed. Scope: `src/bootstrap/metrics.rs`, `src/bootstrap/mod.rs:162-163`, `memory-engine-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:1235`, `tests/bootstrap_test.rs:190`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — `BootstrapConfig` is a public struct with named fields; the change is a semver-breaking field type change, but the crate is pre-1.0.

title: `format!("{:?}", episode.category)` embeds Rust Debug repr into stored JSON metadata
description: In `KeywordExtractor::extract` (line 79), the `EpisodeCategory` discriminant is stored into fact metadata as `format!("{:?}", episode.category)`, producing `"Bug"`, `"Decision"`, etc. This couples stored data to Rust's auto-derived `Debug` output, which is not a stable serialization format — a rename of a variant (e.g. `Bug` → `Defect`) silently changes the string stored in the database without a migration. Current state: `"category": format!("{:?}", episode.category)` with no `Display` or `Serialize` on `EpisodeCategory`. Target state: either (a) derive `serde::Serialize` on `EpisodeCategory` and use `serde_json::to_value(&episode.category)` (giving `"Bug"` from `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` → `"bug"`), or (b) implement `Display` and use `.to_string()`. Either approach makes the stored string explicit and rename-proof. Refactoring pattern: Replace Debug Serialization with Explicit Representation. Motivation: data stability, schema integrity. Scope: `src/bootstrap/filter.rs` (add derive), `src/bootstrap/extract.rs:79`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — only affects newly bootstrapped facts; existing stored strings are already `"Bug"`/`"Decision"`/etc.

title: Non-exhaustive `MatchType` match silently renders `Archive` variant as `"?"`
description: Current state: query.rs line 124-130 matches `MatchType` with four explicit arms and a `_ => "?".into()` wildcard. `MatchType` has five variants (Fts, Vector, Both, ImportanceRank, Archive — confirmed from src/search/hybrid.rs:23-32). The `Archive` variant is a real, stable variant present for serde ABI reasons, not a future extension. The wildcard silently hides it; when archive-backed facts appear in results the table column shows `?` with no indication. Target state: explicit `MatchType::Archive => "ARCH".into()` arm; compiler will then flag any future new variants at build time. Refactoring pattern: Make Implicit Explicit / Complete Wildcard Match. Motivation: correctness under future `MatchType` extension, diagnostic clarity. Scope: 1 file, 1 line. Prerequisites: none. Risk: none.
suggested_fix:
MatchType::Fts => "FTS".into(),
MatchType::Vector => "VEC".into(),
MatchType::Both => "BOTH".into(),
MatchType::ImportanceRank => "RANK".into(),
MatchType::Archive => "ARCH".into(),
// (remove wildcard arm)

title: ConflictArbiter doc does not warn that importance_score on the new Fact is a placeholder
description: Current state: `Fact::importance_score` for the transient new-fact passed to `arbiter.arbitrate()` is hardcoded to `0.5` (line 65), diverging from `new_fact.importance`. The `PersistenceClassifier` trait already has an explicit caveat (traits.rs:86-91) warning implementors that the pre-insert `Fact` has unreliable `importance_score`. The `ConflictArbiter` trait has no equivalent warning. Target state: add a documentation caveat to `ConflictArbiter::arbitrate` mirroring the `PersistenceClassifier` caveat, listing which fields on `new_fact` are reliable (`content`, `fact_type`, `importance`, `metadata`) and which are not (`id=0`, `importance_score` is a seed approximation, `scope_id` may be zero). This is a doc-only change unless the From impl from finding conflict/refactoring-manual-newfact-to-fact is applied first (which would fix the `importance_score` discrepancy). Motivation: misuse-resistance — an arbiter author comparing `old_fact.importance_score` with `new_fact.importance_score` gets silently wrong results. Estimated scope: 1 file (`traits.rs`). Risk: none (doc-only). LIGHT.

title: `Edge.relation_type` and `NewEdge.relation_type` are untyped strings with a closed value set in practice
description: Current state: `Edge.relation_type: String` (line 150) and `NewEdge.relation_type: String` (line 336). At all internal call sites the values are the string constants `"supplements"`, `"contradicts"`, `"co_session"` (conflict/temporal.rs:88,103,132; engine/graph.rs:87). Target state: `pub enum RelationType { Supplements, Contradicts, CoSession, Custom(String) }`. Refactoring pattern: Stringly-typed → enum with open variant. Motivation: coupling — consumers adding new relation types cannot discover existing variants via the type system; misspellings produce silent DB-level inconsistencies not caught until a query. Estimated scope: types.rs, conflict/temporal.rs, engine/graph.rs, engine/snapshot.rs, store/edges.rs. Prerequisites: none. Risk: medium — affects store serialization path (edges stored as raw strings in SQLite; `Display`/`FromStr` implementations must roundtrip the existing string values exactly).
suggested_fix: Define `pub enum RelationType { Supplements, Contradicts, CoSession, Custom(String) }` with `Display` yielding `"supplements"`, `"contradicts"`, `"co_session"`. The `Custom(String)` arm keeps open-world extensibility. Add `FromStr` for DB deserialization.

title: `SummaryGenerator` duplicates `EmbeddingProvider::embed` instead of composing
description: Current state: `SummaryGenerator` declares both `fn summarize(&self, facts: &[Fact]) -> Result<String>` and `fn embed(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>>` (traits.rs:56), duplicating the full signature of `EmbeddingProvider::embed`. Target state: `trait SummaryGenerator: EmbeddingProvider { fn summarize(...) -> Result<String>; }` — composition via super-trait. Refactoring pattern: Super-trait composition. Motivation: coupling and testability — every `SummaryGenerator` implementor must provide two embedding methods that could diverge; callers have two ways to obtain embeddings from the same type; the duplication violates the single-responsibility principle. Estimated scope: traits.rs + all SummaryGenerator impls (likely in consumer code or tests). Prerequisites: confirm that `SummaryGenerator::embed` and `EmbeddingProvider::embed` are intended to be identical (same model, same dimension). Risk: low — composing via super-trait is backward-compatible if implementors already satisfy `EmbeddingProvider`.
suggested_fix: Change `pub trait SummaryGenerator` to `pub trait SummaryGenerator: EmbeddingProvider` and remove `fn embed` from the trait body. Callers that need embedding from a `SummaryGenerator` already obtain it through the `EmbeddingProvider` bound.

title: `ConsolidationConfig` has no `Default` impl and no `validate()`, inconsistent with `ForgetPolicy` and `DreamCycleConfig`
description: Current state: `ConsolidationConfig { dedup_threshold: f32, min_cluster_size: usize }` at traits.rs:185 has no `Default`, no `validate()`, and `dedup_threshold` is unbounded — a consumer can pass `NaN` or a value outside `[0,1]`. Compare with `ForgetPolicy` (traits.rs:238 — has `Default` + `validate()`) and `DreamCycleConfig` (types.rs:413 — has `Default` + `validate()`). Target state: add `impl Default for ConsolidationConfig` with sensible defaults, and `fn validate(&self) -> Result<()>` checking `dedup_threshold` is finite and in `[0, 1]` and `min_cluster_size > 0`. Refactoring pattern: Consistent validation pattern. Motivation: misuse-resistance — currently nothing prevents `dedup_threshold = f32::NAN`, which will silently produce wrong clustering results. Estimated scope: traits.rs only. Prerequisites: decide on default values (e.g. `dedup_threshold: 0.85`, `min_cluster_size: 3`). Risk: low.
suggested_fix: Add `impl Default for ConsolidationConfig { fn default() -> Self { Self { dedup_threshold: 0.85, min_cluster_size: 3 } } }` and `fn validate(&self) -> Result<()>` mirroring the pattern in `ForgetPolicy::validate`.

title: Several consumer-facing types from `traits.rs` are not re-exported from the crate root
description: Current state: lib.rs:57 re-exports only four traits from `traits`: `DreamCycle, EmbeddingProvider, InsightStream, Reranker`. But `ForgetPolicy`, `ConsolidationConfig`, `PruneStats`, `ConsolidationStats`, `CrudDecision`, `ConflictResolution`, `SummaryGenerator`, `ConflictArbiter`, and `PersistenceClassifier` are also part of the public API (they appear in async_engine.rs method signatures at lines 162-165, 174, 182-187) but require consumers to `use memory_engine::traits::ForgetPolicy` rather than `use memory_engine::ForgetPolicy`. Target state: all types that appear in public method signatures should be re-exported from the crate root. Refactoring pattern: Re-export propagation. Motivation: API surface — consumers should not need to know the internal module layout to use public method signatures; the ergonomic bar for using `forget()` is higher than for using `query()` because the policy type is buried. Estimated scope: lib.rs only (add names to existing re-export line). Prerequisites: none. Risk: low — additive only.
suggested_fix: Change lib.rs:57 to: `pub use traits::{ConflictArbiter, ConflictResolution, ConsolidationConfig, ConsolidationStats, CrudDecision, DreamCycle, EmbeddingProvider, ForgetPolicy, InsightStream, PersistenceClassifier, PruneStats, Reranker, SummaryGenerator};`

title: `endpoint` stored as raw `String` — invalid URLs fail only at first network call
description: Current state: The `endpoint` field is a `String` accepted and stored as-is. A caller supplying `"not-a-url"` will get a confusing reqwest transport error on the first `embed()` call rather than a descriptive error at construction time. Target state: Parse and validate as `reqwest::Url` (or `url::Url`) in `new()`, storing the validated URL. This surfaces misconfig eagerly and is self-documenting. Refactoring pattern: Parse-don't-validate / constructor validation. Motivation: misuse-resistance, fail-fast. Estimated scope: 1 file. Risk: low — reqwest accepts `reqwest::Url` directly in `.post()`.

title: Telescoping constructors — open() and open_memory_with_config() are strict subsets of their reranker variants
description: Current state: Four public constructors exist where two are redundant. `open()` (lines 134-152) and `open_with_reranker()` (lines 188-209) have identical bodies except the latter passes `reranker` instead of `None` to `init_from_pool()`. `open_memory_with_config()` (lines 169-181) and `open_memory_with()` (lines 218-231) are similarly related. `open()` is literally `open_with_reranker(config, None)` — confirmed by diff. Target state: Two constructors plus an `EngineBuilder` (or keep the primary variants and make `open()`/`open_memory_with_config()` one-line delegates). Refactoring pattern: Telescoping Constructor → Delegating Wrapper or Builder. Motivation: readability — four near-identical functions that must be kept in sync; any logic change requires four edits. Estimated scope: mod.rs only (1 file). Prerequisites: none. Risk: trivial — pure delegation, no logic changes.
suggested_fix:
pub fn open(config: EngineConfig) -> Result<Self> { Self::open_with_reranker(config, None) }
pub fn open_memory_with_config(embed_dim: usize) -> Result<Self> { Self::open_memory_with(embed_dim, None) }

title: EngineConfig has all-pub fields — constructor invariants can be bypassed
description: Current state: All fields of `EngineConfig` (lines 59-74) are `pub`. Callers can construct arbitrary configs via struct-literal syntax, bypassing any intended constraints (e.g., read_only=true with a path that doesn't exist, or conflicting feature flag combos). Target state: Fields `pub(crate)` or private; expose setters or a builder. Refactoring pattern: Encapsulation / Builder. Motivation: misuse-resistance — the `read_only` path has a documented multi-step validation chain (file existence → schema check → query_only pragma → Rust guard); struct-literal construction bypasses the Rust-level intent, even if the runtime guards still fire. Estimated scope: mod.rs + any external crates that construct EngineConfig by struct literal (check memory-engine-cli and memory-engine-mcp). Prerequisites: audit all call sites. Risk: breaking change for downstream crates that construct via struct literal. Low for internal code.
suggested_fix: Change fields to pub(crate); expose EngineConfig::new(path, embed_dim) and a builder pattern with .read_only(bool) / .snapshot_policy(...) methods. Re-export only EngineConfig (not its fields) from lib.rs.

title: activity_filter and cognitive are pub mod — whole-module internals leak through the engine facade
description: Current state: mod.rs lines 22 and 24 declare `pub mod activity_filter` and `pub mod cognitive`. lib.rs (lines 50 and 61) re-exports only selected types: `ActivityFilterConfig`, `ActivityFilterDecision`, `PromoteAction` from activity_filter, and `DreamContext` from cognitive. But because the modules themselves are `pub`, any type in those modules is reachable via `memory_engine::engine::activity_filter::*` without going through lib.rs. This means helper functions, internal enums, or intermediate types added to those modules become part of the public API surface unintentionally. Target state: `pub(crate) mod activity_filter` and `pub(crate) mod cognitive`. lib.rs re-exports already provide the public surface. Refactoring pattern: Reduce Visibility (pub → pub(crate)).
