Motivation: API surface hygiene — consumers should access types through the documented re-export path only. Estimated scope: mod.rs (1 file). Prerequisites: verify no external crates address items through the engine:: path. Risk: breaking change if any consumer uses the engine:: path directly; negligible if only lib.rs re-exports are used.

title: Outcome counts matched against literal strings — brittle to serde rename on the Outcome enum
description: Current state: `get_outcome_counts()` matches the result of `json_extract(metadata, '$.outcome')` against the string literals `"Positive"`, `"Negative"`, `"Neutral"` (outcome.rs:91-93). This works today because `Outcome` derives `Serialize` with default PascalCase, but is silently broken if `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` or a variant rename is ever added to `Outcome` in types.rs. There is no `FromStr` or `Deserialize`-based deserialization at the match site. Target state: deserialize via `serde_json::from_value::<Outcome>(json_val)` and match on the enum variant, or add a compile-time assertion tying the literal strings to `serde_json::to_string(&Outcome::Positive)`. Refactoring pattern: Replace Magic Literal with Type-Safe Deserialization. Motivation: correctness + coupling — serde representation is a cross-cutting concern; the SQL extraction and the Rust matching must stay in sync silently. Estimated scope: outcome.rs (1 file). Prerequisites: none. Risk: negligible — deserialization path is better.

title: `ReplayFilter` is a public struct with `Default` but lacks `#[non_exhaustive]`, making every new optional field a breaking change
description:
`ReplayFilter` is declared as a plain `pub` struct (types.rs:111). External consumers constructing it with struct-literal syntax (`ReplayFilter { id_range: Some((2,4)), ..Default::default() }`) will get a compile error whenever a new field is added — exactly the breakage pattern that `#[non_exhaustive]` is designed to prevent. `DumpFormat` at line 137 correctly uses `#[non_exhaustive]`. `ReplayFilter` and `EngineSnapshot` (line 150) are missing it. Both have `..Default::default()` spread at every call site, which is the idiomatic escape hatch — but only if `#[non_exhaustive]` enforces that callers must use it.

Current state: `pub struct ReplayFilter { … }` without `#[non_exhaustive]`.
Target state: add `#[non_exhaustive]` to `ReplayFilter` and `EngineSnapshot`.
Refactoring pattern: Add `#[non_exhaustive]`.
Motivation: forward compatibility, library API stability.
Estimated scope: 2 attributes in `src/inspect/types.rs`.
Prerequisites: verify callers already use `..Default::default()` for `ReplayFilter` (confirmed from test usage) and struct-update syntax or builder for `EngineSnapshot` in tests.
Risk: low for `ReplayFilter`; moderate for `EngineSnapshot` (test code constructs it with explicit field lists at restore.rs:471-484 — those will need `..Default::default()` added, but that's inside the crate and acceptable).

title: get_depth parses Depth from string manually despite Depth deriving serde::Deserialize
description: Current state: `get_depth` does a manual `match s.as_str() { "sparse" => ..., "standard" => ..., "full" => ..., _ => None }` instead of using serde. `Depth` already derives `Deserialize` with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`. Target state: `serde_json::from_value::<Depth>(value.clone()).ok().unwrap_or_default()` — a one-liner. Refactoring pattern: Replace Manual with Derived. Motivation: readability + consistency. The silent `_ => Default::default()` also means a misspelled depth (e.g., `"Sparse"`) silently becomes Standard — same concern as the scope_mode issue. Estimated scope: 9 LOC → 3 LOC. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LIGHT.

title: All 8 modules re-exported pub in lib.rs — exposes internal modules as crate API
description: Current state: every module (`activity_policy`, `config`, `depth`, `embedding`, `error`, `server`, `summary`, `tools`) is `pub`. This crate is a binary (`memory-engine-mcp` bin) with a `lib` target used only for integration tests. Publishing all modules as `pub` exposes implementation details — `depth`, `tools`, `activity_policy`, `summary` have no external consumers outside the test suite. Target state: expose only what integration tests genuinely need (`pub use error::*`, `pub use server::MemoryMcpServer`); move the rest to `pub(crate)`. Refactoring pattern: Restrict Visibility. Motivation: API surface hygiene — prevents accidental stabilization of internal types if this lib target is ever published. Estimated scope: `lib.rs` + individual module `pub` → `pub(crate)` markers. Prerequisites: run `cargo test --workspace` to confirm no test directly names an internal path. Risk: LOW — binary crates are not semver-stable anyway, but this is still correct practice.

title: EmbeddingSection.dimensions is parsed from TOML but never read in the server logic
description: Current state: `pub dimensions: usize` is a field on `EmbeddingSection` documented as "Expected embedding dimensions. Used to validate responses." However, `build_embedder` in `main.rs` ignores it — the `embed_dim` actually used comes from `mcp_config.engine.embed_dim` (config) or `probe_embed_dim` (DB probe). No code reads `b.dimensions`. Target state: either (a) use `b.dimensions` as the authoritative `embed_dim` when set (resolving the two-source-of-truth problem), or (b) remove the field if it is truly unused. Refactoring pattern: Remove Dead Field / Consolidate Config. Motivation: maintainability — a documented field that does nothing is a trap for future maintainers who will trust the TOML documentation. Estimated scope: `config.rs` + `main.rs`. Prerequisites: decide which source of truth for embed_dim is preferred. Risk: MEDIUM — removing changes the TOML schema (breaking change for existing configs).

title: schemars::JsonSchema derive on Depth is unused — the crate carries the schemars dep for one dead derive
description: Current state: `Depth` derives `JsonSchema` (`use schemars::JsonSchema`) but no code in the crate calls `schema_for!(Depth)` or passes `Depth` to any function requiring `JsonSchema`. The `schemars` crate is listed as a normal dependency in `Cargo.toml`. Target state: remove the `JsonSchema` derive and the `use schemars::JsonSchema` import; if schemars is needed nowhere else, drop it from `Cargo.toml`. Refactoring pattern: Remove Dead Dependency. Motivation: dependency hygiene — schemars pulls in `dyn-schema` and `indexmap` among others; carrying it for one unused derive increases compile time and attack surface. Estimated scope: 2 lines in `depth.rs`, 1 line in `Cargo.toml`. Prerequisites: confirm schemars is used nowhere else in the crate (confirmed: grep finds no other usage). Risk: LIGHT.

title: probe_embed_dim opens a raw rusqlite connection — duplicates engine-internal DB access outside the engine boundary
description: Current state: `config.rs` directly opens a raw `rusqlite::Connection` to read the `embed_dim` from the config table. This bypasses the `MemoryEngine` abstraction and couples the MCP crate to the internal schema detail (the `config` table, the `embed_dim` key). The `rusqlite` dependency is consequently listed in the MCP crate's `Cargo.toml` even though it is used only for this probe. Target state: expose a `MemoryEngine::read_embed_dim(db_path: &Path) -> Result<usize, MemoryError>` (or similar) static method on the engine — the engine owns the schema, so it should own the probe. Alternatively, open the engine first and read dim from the already-open connection. Refactoring pattern: Move Method to Owner / Remove Leaky Abstraction. Motivation: coupling — if the schema table name or key changes in the engine, `config.rs` silently breaks; maintainability — removes the raw `rusqlite` dep from the MCP crate. Estimated scope: `config.rs` + `memory-engine/src/` (add one method). Prerequisites: confirm the engine does not already expose such a method (it does not — the probe is currently duplicated identically in `memory-engine-cli/src/db.rs` too). Risk: MEDIUM — requires a core engine API addition.

title: `pub mod tree` leaks the internal module into the `pub(crate) mod scope` namespace
description: Current state: `scope/mod.rs` declares `pub mod tree` (line 3) and re-exports `ScopeTree` with `pub use tree::ScopeTree` (line 5). Because `scope` itself is `pub(crate)` (lib.rs:43), the effective visibility ceiling on everything inside it is `pub(crate)`. However, `pub mod tree` means any crate-internal code can reach `crate::scope::tree::ScopeTree` as well as `crate::scope::ScopeTree`, and all non-`ScopeTree` items in `tree.rs` (e.g. the test helpers inside `#[cfg(test)]`) are reachable by name. Target state: change `pub mod tree` to `pub(crate) mod tree` (or `mod tree` with only the re-export kept `pub(crate) use`). This matches the existing pattern in `lib.rs` where internal modules are explicitly `pub(crate)`. Pattern: Restrict Visibility. Motivation: encapsulation — the implementation module should not be a separately addressable path; consumers should only see the re-exported type. Scope: 1 line in mod.rs. Prerequisites: verify no external crate refers to `crate::scope::tree` directly (only `memory-engine-cli` and `memory-engine-mcp` consume this crate; `pub(crate)` already bars them). Risk: zero for crate-internal uses; the re-export covers all legitimate access.

title: `search_archives` `# Errors` omits `MemoryError::Serialization` returned by `read_pak`
description: The doc states: 'Returns `MemoryError::Archive` on I/O or decompression failure.' However `read_pak` (called at line 54) propagates `MemoryError::Serialization` for JSON deserialization failures. The `# Errors` section is incomplete: callers exhaustively matching on `MemoryError::Archive` will miss malformed `.pak` content.

title: `write_pak` suppressed as dead_code with forward reference to unimplemented restore tooling
description: The inline comment on line 14 reads `// Used in unit tests below; restore tooling will also use this.` The `#[allow(dead_code)]` is present because `write_pak` is never called from production code — only from test code. The 'restore tooling' referenced does not exist anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by search). This is a planned-but-unimplemented path suppressing a legitimate compiler signal. If the restore feature is not scheduled, the suppress and dead function accumulate indefinitely.

title: `archive()` `# Panics` section uses weak 'in practice' language without structural argument
description: The `# Panics` doc on the public `archive` method says: 'Cannot panic in practice — the `.pak` path is always constructed with a filename.' The actual `expect` is at line 68, in the private `write_pak_to_disk` helper. The guarantee is structural: the path is `archive_dir.join(format!("archive-{}-{nanos:08x}.pak", ...))`, where the format string always produces a non-empty last component. The phrase 'in practice' implies a probabilistic claim rather than a structural one, which is misleading for a public API. The doc should state why it cannot panic.

title: Public API structs re-exported at crate root lack field-level documentation
description: `ArchivePolicy`, `ArchiveStats`, `ArchivePak`, and `ArchiveManifestEntry` are all re-exported at the crate root via `pub use archive::{ArchiveManifestEntry, ArchivePolicy, ArchiveStats, ArchiveVerifyResult}` in `lib.rs:48`. None of their fields carry `///` doc comments. Key semantics are non-obvious: `ArchivePolicy::min_facts` (minimum candidate count before archival runs, not the count of facts to archive), `ArchiveStats::blake3_hash` (hex string of the compressed file), `ArchivePak::pak_version` (separate from `engine_schema_version`). `ArchiveSearchResult::search_ms` (unit: milliseconds) in `search.rs:18-22` is also undocumented.

title: `# Errors` for `bootstrap_session_inner` mentions scope resolution, but scope is pre-resolved before calling the inner function
description: The `# Errors` section at line 37 reads: "Returns errors from the engine (DB, embedding, scope resolution)". However, `bootstrap_session_inner` receives `scope_id: i64` as a parameter (line 49) — scope resolution is already done by the caller (`engine/bootstrap.rs:32-40`). The inner function never performs scope resolution and therefore cannot return scope-resolution errors. This inaccuracy could lead consumers to incorrectly expect scope errors from this call site.

title: `BootstrapConfig::scope` does not document `None` → root-scope fallback
description: The field doc reads: "Scope path to ingest facts into (e.g., `"project:memory-engine"`)." When `scope` is `None`, the engine silently falls back to `scope_id = 1` (the root scope), as seen in `engine/bootstrap.rs:40`. This is non-obvious — a consumer who passes `None` expecting "no scope" gets the root scope instead.

title: `KeywordExtractor::extract` silently omits `session_outcome` from metadata for `Indeterminate` sessions
description: `KeywordExtractor::extract` sets `metadata["session_outcome"]` to `"success"` or `"failure"` (lines 84-85) but does nothing for `SessionOutcome::Indeterminate` (line 86-87). The `session_outcome` key is therefore absent from the returned `ExtractedFact::metadata` when outcome is `Indeterminate`. This behaviour is undocumented in the trait, the impl, and the `ExtractedFact` struct. Consumers who rely on `metadata["session_outcome"]` being present will get a JSON `null` for indeterminate sessions without warning.

title: `OutcomeSignals::final_user_sentiment` typed `Option<Sentiment>` but is always `Some` in `classify_outcome`
description: `OutcomeSignals::final_user_sentiment` is declared as `Option<Sentiment>` and has no doc comment. `classify_outcome` (outcome.rs:76) always assigns `Some(detect_sentiment(turns))`, and `detect_sentiment` returns `Sentiment::Neutral` for an empty turns slice — never `None`. `None` can only arise through the derived `Default` impl (which is used for `OutcomeSignals::default()` but not by `classify_outcome`). The `Option` wrapper is misleading: the field's doc should clarify when `None` is expected, or the type should be narrowed. Lack of any doc comment makes this ambiguous for consumers.
suggested_fix:
Add a field-level doc comment:
```rust
/// Sentiment of the final user message. Always `Some` when produced by
/// [`classify_outcome`]; `None` only in manually constructed defaults.
pub final_user_sentiment: Option<Sentiment>,
```
Alternatively, remove the `Option` wrapper (breaking change) and return `Sentiment::Neutral` directly, updating `OutcomeSignals::Default`.

title: Section comment announces a no-op action
suggested_fix:
Remove both lines, or replace with a single accurate comment:
```rust
// Outcome is not written back into the marker event; it lives in extracted-fact metadata.
```

title: Query command doc says 'FTS5 full-text search' but the engine runs hybrid search
description: Two doc strings describe the query path as pure FTS5: `main.rs:51` says "Search facts by text (FTS5 full-text search)" and `query.rs:13` says "Search text (FTS5 full-text search)". In reality `execute_query` in the core library runs a hybrid pipeline — FTS5 + vector similarity + RRF merge + optional importance ranking. The table output's "Match" column can return VEC, BOTH, RANK, or ARC, directly contradicting the "FTS5 only" claim. A user who reads the help text and searches by text without embeddings would not know vector matches are being attempted.
suggested_fix:
In `main.rs:51`, change:
```rust
/// Search facts by text (FTS5 full-text search)
```
to:
```rust
/// Search facts by text (hybrid FTS5 + vector + importance-rank)
```

In `query.rs:13`, change:
```rust
/// Search text (FTS5 full-text search)
```
to:
```rust
/// Search text (FTS5 full-text + vector hybrid; results show match origin)
```

title: open_engine_writable doc lists an incomplete set of write-requiring commands
description: `db.rs:46-47` documents `open_engine_writable` with "Needed for commands that mutate the database (e.g., `add-fact`, `export` with SQLite format)". The `record-outcome` command (`commands/record_outcome.rs:39`) also uses it, so the example list is already stale. Additionally, `batch-ingest` mutates the database but calls `open_engine` (read-only) for the non-`--create` path (line 305), which will fail every write with `MemoryError::ReadOnly` — but that is a code bug, not a doc issue in itself. The incomplete doc example list misleads anyone adding a new write command about which open helper to use.

title: # Errors section uses vague catch-all instead of enumerating concrete error variants
description: The `# Errors` section for `resolve_conflict` reads: 'Returns `MemoryError::NotFound` if the old fact doesn't exist. Propagates errors from the arbiter or database operations.' The second sentence is accurate but obscures concrete variants that callers may want to handle: `MemoryError::EmbeddingDimension` (raised by `FactStore::insert` on dim mismatch, line 81/126), `MemoryError::Serialization` (raised by metadata JSON serialisation inside `FactStore::insert`), and `MemoryError::Database` (SQL failures across branches). The pattern differs from the rest of the codebase where `# Errors` enumerates specific variants (e.g. store/edges.rs:39-41, store/edges.rs:62-64).

title: local_dedup # Errors omits MemoryError::NotFound
description: The `# Errors` section states only `MemoryError::Database on SQL failure`, but `FactStore::expire()` (src/store/facts.rs:265) returns `MemoryError::NotFound` when the target row has `t_expired IS NOT NULL` — a condition that can be reached during the pairwise loop if a fact was expired by an earlier iteration before the current one reaches it. The error propagates uncaught via `?` at dedup.rs:87.

title: cluster_fusion # Errors omits EmbeddingDimension and Serialization variants
description: The `# Errors` section documents only `MemoryError::Database` and `SummaryGenerator` errors. However, `SummaryStore::insert` (src/store/summaries.rs:50-54) returns `MemoryError::EmbeddingDimension` when the generator returns a vector whose length does not match `embed_dim`, and line 58 of summaries.rs propagates `MemoryError::Serialization` from JSON-encoding `source_fact_ids`. Both propagate via `?` into `cluster_fusion` at cluster.rs:87-94.

title: global_integration # Errors omits EmbeddingDimension and Serialization variants
description: Same gap as cluster_fusion: `# Errors` lists only `MemoryError::Database` and `SummaryGenerator` errors, but `SummaryStore::insert` (called at global.rs:71) can return `MemoryError::EmbeddingDimension` and `MemoryError::Serialization` for the same reasons described in the cluster_fusion finding.

title: consolidate # Errors omits MemoryError::Migration returned directly by the orchestrator
description: The `# Errors` doc says "Propagates errors from any pass or the SummaryGenerator", implying all errors originate in sub-passes. But at mod.rs:45, `consolidate` itself constructs and returns `MemoryError::Migration` directly when the `last_consolidated_at` config value cannot be parsed as RFC3339. This is a distinct, locally-originated error variant, not propagated from a pass.

title: CLUSTER_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD is a private constant not exposed in ConsolidationConfig, with no explanation of why it is non-configurable
description: `CLUSTER_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` is hardcoded at 0.85 (cluster.rs:11) and used unconditionally in `greedy_cluster` (line 56). `ConsolidationConfig` exposes `dedup_threshold` (configurable) and `min_cluster_size` (configurable) but not the cluster similarity threshold. The single-line comment `/// Cluster threshold for grouping related facts (lower than dedup threshold)` does not explain: (a) why the threshold is intentionally below typical dedup thresholds (~0.90+), (b) why it is not a field in `ConsolidationConfig`, or (c) whether this was a deliberate API decision or an omission. Callers cannot tune clustering granularity without forking the constant.

title: Crate-level storage doc only mentions brute-force cosine search, omitting the ann/HNSW feature
description: The `//!` doc block at lib.rs:15 states `Pure Rust brute-force vector similarity (cosine)` as the only vector search backend. The `ann` feature enables HNSW (hierarchical navigable small world) via `engine/query.rs:35-37` and is explicitly called out in CLAUDE.md as a first-class feature flag. A consumer reading the crate docs would not know approximate nearest-neighbor search exists or how to enable it.
suggested_fix:
Replace line 15 with:
```rust
//! - Pure Rust brute-force vector similarity (cosine); optional HNSW ANN via the `ann` feature
```

title: AddFactOptions::importance doc promises [0, 1] but no validation is enforced
description: The doc comment at line 256 reads `/// Override default importance (0.5). Must be in [0, 1].` However, `engine/ingest.rs` uses `opts.importance.unwrap_or(0.5)` without clamping or rejecting out-of-range values. A caller supplying `importance: Some(5.0)` will silently persist an importance of 5.0, which corrupts the Ebbinghaus decay math and the forgetting pipeline comparisons. The doc makes a normative claim (`Must`) that the implementation does not enforce.
suggested_fix: Either (a) enforce the invariant in the ingest path: `let base_importance = opts.importance.unwrap_or(0.5).clamp(0.0, 1.0);` and update the doc to say "Clamped to [0, 1]."; or (b) add a validation error: if the value is outside [0,1] return `MemoryError::Conflict("importance must be in [0, 1]")`. Option (a) is more robust for an embedded library.

title: lib.rs re-exports only 4 of the ~10 consumer-facing traits, leaving SummaryGenerator / ConflictArbiter / PersistenceClassifier / ForgetPolicy / ConsolidationConfig undiscoverable at the flat re-export level
description: The pub use traits line (line 57) only re-exports {DreamCycle, EmbeddingProvider, InsightStream, Reranker}. However AsyncMemoryEngine::consolidate() requires SummaryGenerator, AsyncMemoryEngine::resolve_conflict() requires ConflictArbiter, AsyncMemoryEngine::add_fact() requires PersistenceClassifier, and AsyncMemoryEngine::forget() requires ForgetPolicy. None of these appear in the flat namespace. Consumers discover the gap at compile time and must navigate to memory_engine::traits::SummaryGenerator etc. The crate module-level doc does not mention this asymmetry or provide guidance.

title: Most MemoryError enum variants have no doc comment; Conflict is semantically overloaded for parameter validation without documentation
description: Of 14 MemoryError variants, only ReadOnly (line 48) carries a `///` doc comment explaining when it occurs. Variants like NotImplemented (line 22), Archive (line 44), Lineage (line 52), UnsupportedEpoch (line 29), Pool (line 25), and Bootstrap (line 39) have no doc. Additionally, MemoryError::Conflict (line 16-17) has message text `"conflict: {0}"` implying fact-conflict semantics, but it is also returned by DreamCycleConfig::validate() and ForgetPolicy::validate() for out-of-range numeric parameters — a semantic mismatch that is undocumented on the variant.
suggested_fix:
Add a `///` comment to each variant explaining the triggering condition. For the semantic overload, either: (a) add a dedicated `InvalidConfig(String)` variant and migrate validate() callers to it, or (b) document the Conflict variant as covering both fact-conflict and config-validation scenarios:
```rust
/// A semantic conflict: contradicting facts, or invalid configuration parameters
/// in [`ForgetPolicy::validate`] or [`DreamCycleConfig::validate`].
#[error("conflict: {0}")]
Conflict(String),
```

title: Private helper docs missing # Errors section despite returning Result
description: `parse_openai_batch` (http.rs:44-45) and `parse_ollama_batch` (http.rs:89) each have a brief `///` summary but no `# Errors` section. Both return `Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>, MemoryError>` with multiple paths: count mismatch, missing `index` field, unparseable embedding at a given index, and (for `parse_openai_batch`) index gap/duplicate. These are private methods so this does not affect public docs, but the missing `# Errors` section violates the project's own clippy `missing_errors_doc` lint that fires at `pedantic` level.

title: `add_facts_batch` # Errors omits `MemoryError::Internal`
description: Lines 153-159 explicitly return `MemoryError::Internal` when `embed_batch()` returns a vector of different length than the input entries slice. The current doc says 'Returns errors from batch embedding, dimension validation, or DB insert.' `Internal` is not one of those described buckets, so a consumer reading only the docs has no way to anticipate this variant.

title: `open()` doc incorrectly states it writes `embed_dim` on first open even in read-only mode
description: The doc says 'On first open, writes `embed_dim` to the config table.' This is only true for the read-write path. When `config.read_only = true`, `init_from_pool` calls `validate_embed_dim()` (mod.rs:414-429), which does not write and instead returns `MemoryError::Migration("embed_dim not set in database; open in read-write mode first")` if no `embed_dim` was previously stored. A caller using `read_only = true` on a fresh database will get a `Migration` error, not a write — the doc misleads them. Same issue applies to `open_with_reranker`.

title: `next_due_time()` has no `# Errors` section despite returning `Result`
description: `next_due_time()` returns `Result<Option<DateTime<Utc>>>` and can fail with `MemoryError::NotFound` (via `resolve_scope_ids` at line 40, if `scope` is `Some` but the path is not in the tree) and `MemoryError::Database` (from the SQL query). The doc comment is a single description line with no `# Errors` section at all.

title: `DreamContext::get_fact` doc claims it returns `NotFound` for non-active facts — incorrect
description: The doc says 'Returns `MemoryError::NotFound` if no **active** fact with this ID exists.' It delegates to `FactStore::get()` (facts.rs:106-121), which queries `FROM facts WHERE id = ?1` with no filter on `t_expired`. An expired fact with the given ID is returned successfully; `NotFound` is only returned when the ID is absent from the table entirely. The word "active" in the error condition is wrong and would mislead a consumer who expires a fact and then calls `get_fact` expecting `NotFound`.
suggested_fix:
Change the `# Errors` line to:
```rust
/// Returns `MemoryError::NotFound` if no fact with this ID exists (active or expired).
```

title: Three stale Phase-5 forward-reference comments in public API docs
description: Three doc comments carry open-ended Phase-5 placeholder notes that appear in rendered API docs: (1) `resume_context()` lists 'KB stubs — placeholder for Phase 5' as tier 5 (resume.rs:17); (2) `CO_SESSION_WEIGHT` const says 'it will matter once weighted traversal ships (Phase 5)' (graph.rs:19); (3) `explain_fact()` says `ExpiredReason` is 'best-effort … until event-based audit trail is added in a future version' (inspect.rs:52). These are accurate today but will become stale once Phase 5 lands, and they expose internal roadmap scheduling to library consumers.
suggested_fix: Track each against a GitHub issue so they are cleaned up when Phase 5 ships. For public-facing API docs, prefer describing current behaviour without referencing future phases: e.g., replace 'placeholder for Phase 5' with 'always empty in the current release'.

title: `compute_importance` inherits the undocumented `half_life > 0` precondition from `ebbinghaus_decay`
description: `compute_importance` is `pub` and `#[must_use]`. Its doc comment lists the four signals accurately but does not state that `policy.half_life_days` (and any applicable override from `policy.half_life_overrides`) must be positive and finite. If called with a zero-override half-life for the fact's `fact_type`, the recency signal computes to `NaN`, propagating into the weighted sum. This is only validated by `policy.validate()` inside `prune()`; the public function itself has no guard.

title: remove_node has no # Panics section; petgraph remove_node panics on out-of-bounds index
description: petgraph::DiGraph::remove_node panics with an index-out-of-bounds if the NodeIndex is invalid (nodes.get(a.index()) returns None — see petgraph src, lines 649-650 which do a bounds check but rely on correct Ix arithmetic; accessing self.nodes[a.index()] without a bounds guard in the swap_remove path can panic if the graph has been used incorrectly). While normal usage via MemoryGraph::remove_node should not produce an invalid index (the idx comes from node_map which is populated only by DiGraph::add_node), the stale-index bug documented in graph/documentation-remove-node-stale-index means that if a future call path passes a recycled NodeIndex to an internal petgraph operation, a panic is possible. The doc has no # Panics section. This is a minor gap that should be resolved alongside the stale-index fix.
suggested_fix: Add a `# Panics` section explaining that this method cannot panic under normal operation, but that callers must not call it while holding a stale NodeIndex from a previous call (which is an internal invariant, not a public-API concern). After fixing the stale-index bug, this is trivially documented as non-panicking.

title: read_snapshot # Errors lists Internal only for the size cap, silently omitting zstd init failure
description: The `# Errors` doc states `MemoryError::Internal` is returned "if the file exceeds 4 GiB". Under the `compress-zstd` feature the `zstd::Decoder::new` call at line 108 also maps its `io::Error` to `MemoryError::Internal` via the explicit `map_err` there. The doc therefore under-specifies when `Internal` can arise and may mislead callers who assume it only guards against oversized files.

title: FactProvenance fields importance and importance_score are completely undocumented
description: The public struct `FactProvenance` (part of `FactExplanation`, the return type of `MemoryEngine::explain_fact`) exposes four fields with no doc comments at all: `importance`, `importance_score`, `is_pinned`, and `access_count`. The distinction between `importance` and `importance_score` is non-obvious: `importance` is the consumer-set base weight (in [0, 1], from `AddFactOptions::importance`) while `importance_score` is the runtime-computed/decayed score used for ranking. Without docs, callers are likely to conflate them. The analogous fields in `crate::types::Fact` (lines 133 and 139) are also undocumented at field level, but that struct is not the inspection surface — `FactProvenance` is.

title: explain_fact_with_graph_context (pub(crate)) has no # Errors section
description: The crate-internal function `explain_fact_with_graph_context` has a `# Consistency note` doc section but no `# Errors` section. It calls `FactStore::get` (returns `MemoryError::NotFound` or `MemoryError::Database`) and `EventStore::get_upcasted` (additionally returns `MemoryError::Migration`). Since the function is `pub(crate)` it is called from `MemoryEngine::explain_fact` and its callsite-level errors need to be discoverable by the engine maintainer, not just consumers.

title: all_tool_definitions() doc says 'P0 + P1' but function returns 23 tools across 5 tiers
description: The doc comment on `all_tool_definitions()` reads "Returns all tool definitions (P0 + P1) with JSON schemas." The function actually returns 23 tools: 10 P0, 5 P1, 3 P2 (memory_replay_events, memory_fact_history, memory_bootstrap_session), 2 Phase 5a (memory_record_outcome, memory_outcome_counts), and 3 activity-stream tools (memory_record_activity, memory_checkpoint_session, memory_load_context). The stale tier list in the doc will mislead maintainers adding new tools.
suggested_fix: /// Returns all tool definitions (P0, P1, P2, Phase 5a, and activity-stream) with JSON schemas.

title: Reference doc tool count and table are stale — 5 tools missing
description: The MCP server reference document states "18 tools (10 P0 + 5 P1 + 3 activity stream)" and the tool table contains 18 rows. The actual implementation has 23 tools. Missing from the table: `memory_replay_events` (P2), `memory_fact_history` (P2), `memory_bootstrap_session` (P2), `memory_record_outcome` (Phase 5a), `memory_outcome_counts` (Phase 5a). The reference doc is the primary operator documentation and should be accurate.
suggested_fix: Update the heading count to "23 tools (10 P0 + 5 P1 + 3 P2 + 2 Phase 5a + 3 activity stream)" and add the five missing rows to the tool table with their purpose and depth support.

title: Misleading comment claims both-or-neither validation for since/until that is not implemented
description: The comment at line 1140 reads "Both-or-neither validation (like period_start/period_end in handle_query)" but the actual code only validates ordering when both `since` and `until` are present — one-sided values are silently accepted (unlike `handle_query` which returns an error on one-sided `period_start`/`period_end`). Whether one-sided filtering is intentional for `replay_events`, the comment actively misleads reviewers into thinking parity enforcement exists when it does not.

title: shape_explanation(Full) silently returns json!(null) on serialization failure with no doc
description: In `shape_explanation`, the `Depth::Full` arm calls `serde_json::to_value(explanation).unwrap_or_else(|e| { tracing::error!(...); json!(null) })`. If `FactExplanation` fails to serialize (e.g., a future field with a non-serializable type), the function silently returns `null` to the MCP client instead of propagating an error. The function signature returns `Value`, so error propagation would require a signature change, but the silent-null fallback is undocumented and surprising. There is no `# Panics` or inline comment explaining why `null` is safe here.

title: MemoryMcpServer::new() hardwires filter_config with no doc on the limitation
description: `MemoryMcpServer::new()` accepts `engine`, `embedder`, `summary_gen`, and `embed_dim` but hardwires `filter_config` to `crate::activity_policy::default_filter_config()`. The field is declared `pub`, suggesting consumers can read it, but there is no constructor parameter to inject a custom `ActivityFilterConfig`. The struct-level doc does not mention this. Consumers who want to customize dedup windows or ignore/promote patterns must work around the constructor (struct-literal init or post-construction field mutation), which is non-obvious from the public API.

title: `ConnectionPool::open` `# Errors` omits `MemoryError::Migration` and `MemoryError::UnsupportedEpoch`
description: The `# Errors` section for `open()` (lines 85–87) documents only `MemoryError::Database`. However `open()` calls `migrate()` (schema.rs:198), which can return `MemoryError::Migration` (on parse failure of `schema_version`, line 202; on version-too-new, line 218) and `MemoryError::UnsupportedEpoch` (on db_epoch > STORAGE_EPOCH, line 211). Both variants propagate via `?` to `open()` callers.

title: `ConnectionPool::open_read_only` `# Errors` omits `MemoryError::Database`
description: The `# Errors` section for `open_read_only()` (lines 146–150) documents `MemoryError::Migration` and `MemoryError::UnsupportedEpoch` but omits `MemoryError::Database`. The call to `open_connection_read_only()` (schema.rs:38–46) can fail with `MemoryError::Database` if `Connection::open_with_flags` or the pragma setup fail — both propagate via `?` to `open_read_only()` callers.

title: "all pinned facts" claim ignores `pinned_cap` truncation
description: The `resume_context` doc (line 62) says "Pinned — **all** pinned facts (always present, cross-scope)" and `ResumeContext::pinned` field doc (line 46) says "Pinned (unforgettable) facts — agent identity, core beliefs" with no mention of a cap. The implementation at line 80 applies `.take(config.pinned_cap)` after querying, silently dropping any pinned facts beyond the cap (default 50). "All" is incorrect; agents with more than `pinned_cap` pinned facts will receive a partial set with no indication of truncation.

title: `ResumeContext::recent` doc says "active scope" (singular); impl uses scope ancestors (plural)
description: `ResumeContext::recent` is documented as "Most recent facts from **active scope**" (singular). The `MemoryEngine::resume_context` caller at `src/engine/resume.rs:32-33` resolves `scope_ids` via `tree.ancestors(id)`, which returns the target scope plus all ancestor scopes. So Tier 4 actually queries across the full ancestor chain, not just the leaf scope. The singular "active scope" wording understates coverage.

title: ancestors silently returns empty Vec for unknown scope_id — not documented
description: If `scope_id` is not present in `self.nodes`, `ancestors` immediately terminates the while loop (the first `self.nodes.get(&id)` returns `None`, so `current` becomes `None`). The result is an empty `Vec`, indistinguishable from a successfully traversed scope that has no ancestors (impossible in practice but conceptually ambiguous). The doc says 'Get ancestor scope_ids from leaf to root (inclusive)' with no note about missing IDs. Callers like `resolve_scope_ids` in `engine/mod.rs:668` call `resolve_path` before `ancestors` and so guard this case, but the function contract is silent.

title: #[allow(dead_code)] on entire ScopeStore impl — accumulating API surface with no callers
description: The annotation `#[allow(dead_code)] // complete CRUD API — not all methods called through engine facade yet` suppresses warnings for `get`, `find_by_label`, `insert`, and `for_each`. These are real public API surface area: `get` and `find_by_label` are only called from tests, and `for_each` is only used in dump/streaming paths (not through the engine facade). The allow suppresses any future signal if the methods drift further from production use. The comment does not reference a tracking issue or planned work, making this a permanent dead-code allowance with no exit criterion.
suggested_fix: Either link to the GitHub issue that will wire these methods into the engine facade (e.g. `// TODO(#NNN): remove allow when get/find_by_label are exposed via MemoryEngine`), or move the untested methods to a `#[cfg(test)]` block until the facade is ready. `for_each` is legitimately used by streaming dump paths and can be removed from the suppression scope.

title: Doc example variable named `results` but holds a `QueryResponse`, not a `Vec`
description: The `rust,ignore` example uses `let results = engine.execute_query(...)` and then iterates as if `results` were a `Vec<SearchResult>`. `execute_query` returns `Result<QueryResponse>`, so after `?` the binding holds a `QueryResponse`. The code as written compiles (with `rust,ignore` it isn't checked), but a reader copying it would need `.results` to access the facts. The misleading variable name increases copy-paste error risk.

title: Bare `.unwrap()` on `serde_json::to_string` in production code, no panic message
description: `scope_ids.map(|ids| serde_json::to_string(ids).unwrap())` at line 56 uses a bare `unwrap()` while the identical pattern in `fts.rs:51,113` uses `.expect("serialize scope_ids")`. Serialising `&[i64]` is effectively infallible, but the silent `unwrap()` leaves no message in a panic backtrace and is inconsistent with sibling code. Neither site has a `# Panics` doc note.
suggested_fix:
Change to `.expect("serialize scope_ids")` to match `fts.rs` and provide a backtrace-friendly message:
```rust
let scope_json: Option<String> = scope_ids
    .map(|ids| serde_json::to_string(ids).expect("serialize scope_ids"));
```

title: `from_snapshot` and `to_snapshot` missing `# Errors` sections
description: `from_snapshot` returns `Result<Self>` and can return `MemoryError::EmbeddingDimension` (line 192) or `MemoryError::Internal` (line 199), but has no `# Errors` doc block. `to_snapshot` returns `Result<HnswSnapshot>` and can return `MemoryError::Database` or `MemoryError::EmbeddingDimension` (via `deserialize_embedding`), but also lacks `# Errors`. Both are `pub(crate)` (internal API), so severity is low but the omission is inconsistent with `build_from_db` which documents its errors on lines 86-89.

title: Snapshot test and snapshot file are named schema_v7 but test the v9 schema
description: `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 9` (schema.rs:8), but the regression test at line 2060 is named `fn schema_v7_snapshot()`, calls `insta::assert_snapshot!("schema_v7", schema)`, and the snapshot file is `...__schema_v7.snap`. A reader searching for the v9 schema regression test will not find it; a reader looking at `schema_v7` will find the current schema, not the v7 schema. The stale name also means any future addition of a genuine v7-compatibility test will collide.
suggested_fix: Rename the test and snapshot key to `schema_v9_snapshot` / `"schema_v9"`, then rename the snapshot file. Run `cargo test` with `INSTA_UPDATE=new` to regenerate it under the new key.

title: unwrap_or_default silently replaces corrupt stored JSON with null/{}
description:
Both `row_to_activity` (activities.rs:218) and `row_to_checkpoint` (checkpoints.rs:98) contain `serde_json::from_str(&field).unwrap_or_default()`. If the stored column holds invalid JSON (e.g. truncated write, manual DB edit, future schema bug), the error is silently swallowed and the returned struct carries `Value::Null` or `Value::Object({})` instead. Callers see a valid struct with missing data and no indication anything went wrong. SQLite `CHECK(json_valid(...))` on the column mitigates this in practice, but the silent fallback is undocumented and defeats any future relaxation of the constraint.

The two sites are:
- `activities.args` (activities.rs:218)
- `session_checkpoints.metadata` (checkpoints.rs:98)
references: CWE-390 (Detection of Error Condition without Action)

title: ScopeStore public methods lack # Errors doc sections
description: The following methods return `Result<_>` but have no `# Errors` section in their doc comments: `get` (line 18), `find_by_label` (line 41), `insert` (line 61), `ensure_path` (line 107), `list_all` (line 140). The `new` constructor (line 13) also has no doc comment at all. Only `for_each` (line 165) documents its errors.

title: ActivityStore public methods lack # Errors doc sections
description: The following methods return `Result<_>` but have no `# Errors` section: `insert_or_dedup` (line 26), `get` (line 101), `list_by_session` (line 120), `list_recent_by_scope` (line 150), `update_status` (line 177), `count_by_session` (line 197). The `new` constructor (line 16) also has no doc comment.
suggested_fix: Add `# Errors` sections — each method returns `MemoryError::Database` on SQLite failure. `get` also returns `MemoryError::NotFound` when the id is absent. Add a one-line doc to `new`.

title: CheckpointStore public methods lack # Errors doc sections
description: The following methods return `Result<_>` but have no `# Errors` section: `upsert` (line 21), `get` (line 47), `get_by_scope` (line 61), `list_recent` (line 77). The `new` constructor (line 16) also has no doc comment.
suggested_fix: Add `# Errors` sections. All four methods return `MemoryError::Database` on SQLite failure. `get` and `get_by_scope` return `Ok(None)` (not an error) when absent — note that too so callers do not confuse absence with error. Add a one-line doc to `new`.

title: Multiple FactStore public methods lack # Errors doc sections
description: The following methods return `Result<_>` but have no `# Errors` section in their doc comments: `list_pinned` (line 369), `list_due` (line 397), `next_due_time` (line 432), `stamp_surfaced` (line 473), `set_pinned` (line 503), `list_all` (line 519), `update_importance_score` (line 564), `list_by_importance_score` (line 574), `list_active_by_session` (line 633), `list_by_scopes_recent` (line 677), `list_active_in_period` (line 717), `hard_delete_ids` (line 793). Methods earlier in the file (`insert`, `get`, `list_active`, etc.) correctly include `# Errors`.
suggested_fix: Add `# Errors` sections matching the pattern used by the already-documented methods. For `next_due_time`, also document `MemoryError::Internal` for a malformed `t_valid` timestamp (and fix the wrong variant per finding `store/documentation-wrong-error-variant`). For `hard_delete_ids`, note that it performs a hard DELETE (permanent removal) — distinct from the soft-delete semantics used elsewhere — and should document that too.

title: Several FactStore methods call expect on serde_json::to_string without # Panics doc
description: Multiple `FactStore` methods serialize `Vec<i64>` scope or exclusion id lists with `serde_json::to_string(...).expect("serialize scope_ids")` / `expect("serialize exclude_ids")`. In practice the serialization of `Vec<i64>` cannot fail, but the contract is undocumented. The following methods have the pattern without a `# Panics` section: `list_pinned` (lines 382-384), `list_by_importance_score` (lines 603-605), `list_by_scopes_recent` (lines 684-686), `list_active_in_period` (lines 736-738). By contrast, `list_by_scopes_importance` (lines 218-220) correctly includes a `# Panics` note explaining why the expect is safe.

title: says 3 crates, actual 4
Nested if-let chains in search loop are candidates for let-else or combinators
description: The per-fact scoring loop uses nested `if let Some(ref ft) = …` / `if let Some(ref text) = …` / `if let Some(ref query_emb) = …` patterns. Edition 2024 (which this crate targets, per `Cargo.toml:8`) stabilises `let-else` and encourages early-continue patterns. The current code is readable but the query.text.is_none() && query.embedding.is_none() default-match check at line 88 duplicates the condition already implicit in the two if-let arms above — a minor logic duplication.

title: parse_datetime is identically duplicated across two command modules
description: The same 4-line function `fn parse_datetime(s: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>, String>` appears verbatim in both `add_fact.rs:72-76` and `query.rs:43-47`. Any future change (e.g. adding support for date-only strings) must be applied in both places, creating a silent divergence risk. The shared `output.rs` module or a new `util.rs` is the natural home.

title: Non-exhaustive MatchType wildcard renders Archive results as uninformative "?"
description: `MatchType` is `#[non_exhaustive]` (search/hybrid.rs:21) so a wildcard arm is required for the match to compile. The current label is `"?"`, which would be shown to the user if a result with `MatchType::Archive` appears (possible when the `archive` feature flag is enabled and `include_archives=true` is set on the query). The CLI Cargo.toml does not currently enable the `archive` feature, so this is not triggered today, but if the feature is later added the display will be silently misleading.
suggested_fix:
Replace the catch-all label with a descriptive string that names the variant:

```rust
_ => "ARCH".into(),   // covers MatchType::Archive and any future non_exhaustive variants
```

Optionally add a `cfg(debug_assertions)` panic in the wildcard to catch genuinely unexpected variants during development.

title: std::collections::HashMap/HashSet use the SipHash-1-3 default hasher for small integer keys
description: `scope_counts` in `cluster_fusion` (lines 76-77) and `expired_ids` in `local_dedup` (line 59) both use the standard SipHash-1-3 hasher, which is designed for DOS resistance at the cost of throughput. Both maps use `i64` keys, for which a faster non-cryptographic hasher (e.g., `FxHashMap` from `rustc-hash`, or `AHashMap` from `ahash`) would be 2-5× faster. While neither map is in an extremely hot inner loop, `expired_ids` is probed on every iteration of the O(N×M) double loop in dedup.
suggested_fix: Add `rustc-hash` or `ahash` to `[dependencies]` and replace `std::collections::HashMap::new()` / `HashSet::new()` with `FxHashMap::default()` / `FxHashSet::default()` (or `AHashMap::new()` / `AHashSet::new()`) for these integer-keyed maps. Since the crate already depends on `blake3` and `serde_json`, adding one of these zero-overhead hashmap crates adds minimal dependency weight.

title: ActivityStatus::FromStr uses String as error type instead of a typed error
description: `impl std::str::FromStr for ActivityStatus` (types.rs:511-523) uses `type Err = String`. The rest of the crate uses `thiserror`-derived typed errors consistently. A raw `String` error (a) cannot be matched by variant, (b) does not implement `std::error::Error`, so it cannot be wrapped with `?` into `MemoryError` without a manual `map_err`. This is an API consistency defect on a public type.

title: use rusqlite::OptionalExtension placed at bottom of file
description: The use rusqlite::OptionalExtension; import at line 247 is positioned at the very bottom of the file, 230 lines after the code that uses it (the .optional() call at line 177). Rust edition convention and rustfmt both place use statements at the top of the module. In this position the import is functionally equivalent but misleading: readers scanning the top-of-file imports will not see it, and any automated formatter will move it. This is a code hygiene issue with no semantic consequence.
suggested_fix: Move use rusqlite::OptionalExtension; to the top-level use block alongside the other rusqlite imports.

title: fact.t_invalid.unwrap() in production code relies on a non-local guard
description: determine_state line 101: `if t_valid <= now && (fact.t_invalid.is_none() || fact.t_invalid.unwrap() > now)`. The unwrap cannot panic given the priority block at lines 92-95 — if t_invalid is Some AND <= now the function already returned Invalidated. But that invariant is non-local: refactoring the priority order silently turns this into a panic site. forbid(unsafe_code) does not guard against panics. This is on the public explain_fact path which consumers may call on arbitrary stored facts.
suggested_fix: Replace with `if t_valid <= now && fact.t_invalid.map_or(true, |ti| ti > now) { ... }` — semantically identical, no unwrap, invariant is self-contained.

title: Bare .unwrap() on serde_json::to_string in vector_search inconsistent with sibling callers
description: `vector.rs:56` uses `.unwrap()` on `serde_json::to_string(ids)` while the identical pattern in `fts.rs:51`, `fts.rs:113`, and `ann.rs:373` all use `.expect("serialize scope_ids")`. A plain `.unwrap()` provides no diagnostic message when the impossible (serializing `&[i64]`) somehow fails. Consistency with the rest of the module requires `.expect()`.

title: SearchMode missing Copy derive — forces avoidable clones at call sites
description: `SearchMode` is a unit-variant enum with no heap data (Fts / Vector / Hybrid). It does not derive `Copy`, so every pass-by-value in `matches!(query.mode, ...)` and struct initialization moves or borrows rather than copies. Call sites in `engine/query.rs` and `async_engine.rs` clone or move it repeatedly. Deriving `Copy` is a one-line fix and aligns with the pattern used for `FactType` and `Outcome`.

title: Lossy `as u32` cast on `usize` loop index
description: `let target = (i as u32) + 2;` casts `usize` to `u32` via `as`, which silently truncates on hypothetical platforms where `usize > 2^32`. While the MIGRATIONS array has 8 elements so `i` never exceeds 7 in practice, the `as` cast itself triggers `clippy::cast_possible_truncation`. The established pattern in the codebase for this conversion is `i64::try_from(n).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)` (used in facts.rs and events.rs). Consistency and future-proofness favor the checked form.

title: Unchecked `limit as i64` cast in `CheckpointStore::list_recent`
description: `params![limit as i64, ...]` at checkpoints.rs:88 converts `limit: usize` to `i64` via `as`. If `limit > i64::MAX` (only possible on 64-bit where `usize` can reach 2^63), the cast wraps to a negative number, causing SQLite to receive a negative LIMIT and return 0 rows unexpectedly. The rest of the codebase uses `i64::try_from(limit).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)` for this pattern (e.g., facts.rs:311, 341, 581, 683). This site is inconsistent.
suggested_fix:
```rust
let limit_i64 = i64::try_from(limit).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
let rows = stmt
    .query_map(params![limit_i64], row_to_checkpoint)
```

title: build_pak clones candidate_facts and candidate_edges unnecessarily
description: `build_pak(&candidate_facts, &candidate_edges)` calls `facts.to_vec()` and `edges.to_vec()` inside, producing full owned clones including all embedding `Vec<f32>` data. The caller (`archive()`) accesses `candidate_facts` only to read `len()` and iterate `f.id` after this call — both of which do not require the original data to remain alive. The `ArchivePak` is serialized immediately and then dropped; the clones are only needed for the lifetime of the encoder, not beyond.
suggested_fix:
Change `build_pak` to consume its arguments:
```rust
fn build_pak(&self, facts: Vec<Fact>, edges: Vec<Edge>) -> ArchivePak
```
Then capture `facts_len` and `fact_ids` before moving into `build_pak`, eliminating the clone entirely.

title: FactType is a unit enum without Copy, causing unnecessary .clone() in the fact-insertion hot loop
description: `FactType` has three unit variants (no data) and derives `Clone` but not `Copy`. In `bootstrap_within_savepoint`, `fact.fact_type.clone()` is called twice per fact (lines 212 and 234) to build the temp `Fact` and `NewFact`. The `match fact.fact_type` at line 252 then also moves. Deriving `Copy` eliminates both `.clone()` calls and clarifies the intent: this is a trivially-copyable discriminant.
suggested_fix:
In `src/types.rs`, add `Copy` to `FactType`'s derive list:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum FactType { Episodic, Semantic, Procedural }
```
Then remove the `.clone()` calls on `fact_type` fields throughout bootstrap.

title: EpisodeCategory is a unit enum without Copy, causing unnecessary .clone() in extract
description: `EpisodeCategory` has four unit variants and derives `Clone` but not `Copy`. `extract.rs:94` calls `episode.category.clone()` to store the category in `ExtractedFact`. Deriving `Copy` eliminates the clone and is the semantically correct choice for a trivially-copyable discriminant.
suggested_fix:
In `src/bootstrap/filter.rs`, add `Copy` to `EpisodeCategory`'s derive list:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum EpisodeCategory { Bug, Decision, Convention, Learning }
```
Then replace `episode.category.clone()` with `episode.category` in `extract.rs:94`.

title: keyword_prefilter allocates three lowercased strings per turn where two suffice
description: For each `ConversationTurn`, `keyword_prefilter` calls (a) `build_searchable_text` (allocates a lowercased concatenation of user text + assistant text + all stderrs), (b) `turn.assistant_text.to_lowercase()` (second allocation of the already-lowercased assistant text), and (c) `collect_stderr` (third allocation of already-lowercased stderr). The `assistant_lower` and `stderr_text` strings are strict subsets of `searchable`, making allocations (b) and (c) redundant. They exist because `check_error_keyword` needs to distinguish the source of an "error" match, but `searchable` could expose those components as `&str` slices instead of re-lowercasing.
suggested_fix: Restructure `build_searchable_text` to return `(String, usize, usize)` — the combined string plus byte offsets delimiting the assistant and stderr sections — so `check_error_keyword` can receive `&str` slices into the already-allocated buffer. Alternatively, inline the bug check into a single pass over the combined string, tracking which segment the match falls in. This reduces per-turn allocations from three to one for the common path.

title: Building the synthetic `Fact` clones embedding, content, metadata, and content_hash on every conflict resolution
description: Every conflict resolution allocates: `content.clone()` (String), `content_hash.clone()` (String), `embedding.clone()` (Vec<f32> — typically 768 × 4 = 3 KB; up to 12 KB for 3072-dim models), `fact_type.clone()`, and `metadata.clone()` (serde_json::Value — can be arbitrarily large). The synthetic `Fact` is consumed once by the arbiter and dropped. The trait signature `arbitrate(&self, &Fact, &Fact)` forces materialization of a full owned `Fact` for a pre-insertion value that has no DB row yet.
suggested_fix:
Introduce a `NewFactView<'a>` borrowing struct and change the trait to `arbitrate(&self, old: &Fact, new: NewFactView<'_>) -> Result<CrudDecision>`. This removes all 5 clones per resolution:

```rust
pub struct NewFactView<'a> {
    pub content: &'a str,
    pub embedding: &'a [f32],
    pub importance: f64,
    pub metadata: &'a serde_json::Value,
    pub t_valid: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub t_invalid: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
}
```

title: `RELATION_SUPPLEMENTS.to_string()` / `RELATION_CONTRADICTS.to_string()` allocated twice per mutation branch
description: Each mutation branch allocates the relation-type literal twice: once for the persisted `NewEdge.relation_type` and again for the in-memory `EdgeData.relation_type`. Allocations are small (≤12 bytes each) but redundant on every conflict resolution call.

title: Vec<Fact> constructed solely to satisfy SummaryGenerator trait, cloning embeddings unnecessarily
description: `global_integration` builds a `Vec<Fact>` (pseudo_facts) by cloning `s.content` and `s.embedding` from each cluster `Summary` (lines 39, 41). The embedding clone alone is 4 × embed_dim bytes per cluster summary. This allocation exists only because `SummaryGenerator::summarize` takes `&[Fact]` rather than a lighter reference type. The `metadata: serde_json::json!({})` call also allocates a fresh JSON `Value` per item.
suggested_fix: In the short term, pre-size the vec with `Vec::with_capacity(cluster_summaries.len())` to avoid reallocation. For a deeper fix, introduce a `SummaryInput` reference type (containing `content: &str`, `embedding: &[f32]`, and `id: i64`) and change `SummaryGenerator::summarize` to accept `&[SummaryInput]`. This avoids all clones. If the trait signature is frozen, at minimum remove the per-item `serde_json::json!({})` allocation by sharing a static `Value::Object(Default::default())`.

title: source_ids and all_source_ids Vecs allocated without pre-sizing
description: In `cluster_fusion` (line 68): `let source_ids: Vec<i64> = cluster_facts.iter().map(|f| f.id).collect();` allocates without knowing the cluster size. In `global_integration` (lines 63-66): `all_source_ids` flattens all cluster `source_fact_ids` slices without pre-computing the total count. Both cases cause unnecessary reallocations.
suggested_fix: Use `Vec::with_capacity(cluster_facts.len())` for `source_ids`. For `all_source_ids`, pre-compute the capacity with `let cap = cluster_summaries.iter().map(|s| s.source_fact_ids.len()).sum(); let mut all_source_ids = Vec::with_capacity(cap);` followed by an `extend` loop, or equivalently keep `flat_map(...).collect()` but pre-size via `.size_hint()`.

title: Ref parameters immediately cloned to satisfy spawn_blocking 'static bound
description: `replay_events` (async_engine.rs:307-316) takes `filter: &crate::inspect::ReplayFilter` and then immediately clones it (`let filter = filter.clone();`) to move it into the `spawn_blocking` closure. `dump_state` (async_engine.rs:350) does the same with `format: &crate::inspect::DumpFormat`. Taking a reference only to clone it immediately is worse than taking the value by ownership: it forces an unnecessary clone on every call, adds a lifetime annotation that buys nothing, and misleads callers into thinking the function borrows cheaply. The clone is unconditional and per-call.

title: Unnecessary deep clone of `serde_json::Value` per embedding vector when parsing
description: `serde_json::from_value::<Vec<f32>>(e.clone())` clones the entire `Value::Array` (e.g. 1536 `Number` elements for OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small) before deserializing. In `parse_openai_batch` (line 66) this clone is repeated once per text in the batch — so a batch of 100 texts triggers 100 full array clones before a single float is extracted. The same pattern appears in `parse_ollama_batch` (line 105) and three times in `embed()` (lines 148, 152, 155). The clone is avoidable: `Value::as_array()` gives a `&[Value]` whose elements expose `Value::as_f64()` without transferring ownership.
suggested_fix:
Replace `serde_json::from_value::<Vec<f32>>(e.clone())` with a zero-clone iterator path. Note: `filter_map` silently drops non-numeric elements, so use `map`+`ok_or` to preserve the parse-error detection:

```rust
// Generic helper (place in impl block):
fn parse_embedding(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<Vec<f32>, MemoryError> {
    v.as_array()
        .ok_or_else(|| MemoryError::Internal("embedding is not an array".into()))?
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, n)| {
            n.as_f64()
                .map(|f| f as f32)
                .ok_or_else(|| MemoryError::Internal(format!("embedding[{i}] is not a number")))
        })
        .collect()
}
```
Then replace `serde_json::from_value::<Vec<f32>>(e.clone()).ok()` with `Self::parse_embedding(e).ok()` (for the detection branches) and `Self::parse_embedding(v).map_err(...)` (for the parse branches that already return `Result`).

title: CO_SESSION_RELATION.to_string() allocated inside O(N²) nested loop
description: link_session_facts() iterates over all fact pairs in a session in an O(N²) nested loop (lines 76-96). Inside the innermost body, Self::CO_SESSION_RELATION.to_string() is called at line 87 (for the NewEdge struct) and again at line 111 (inside graph.add_edge for EdgeData). This allocates a new String from a static str on every iteration — for N=20 co-session facts that is 400*2 = 800 String allocations of a 20-byte literal. While session sizes are typically small, this is a pure waste on a trivially-fixable pattern.
suggested_fix: Hoist the allocation outside both loops: let relation = Self::CO_SESSION_RELATION.to_string(); then use relation.clone() for NewEdge and relation.clone() for EdgeData, or use Arc<str> to amortize the clone cost.

title: remove_edge_by_id performs an O(E) full edge scan
description:
remove_edge_by_id iterates self.graph.edge_indices() and filters by EdgeData.edge_id, making it O(E) over all edges in the graph. The method has no production callers at present (only used in a test at line 333), but its public API implies it is the intended path for expiring a single edge by its SQLite row id. If called in a future hot path (e.g. per-fact conflict expiry loop), it will scan the entire edge set for each removal.

A complementary HashMap<i64, EdgeIndex> (keyed on edge_id, analogous to node_map) would bring this to O(1), at the cost of maintaining a second index. That overhead is likely worthwhile if the method ever acquires a production caller.

title: MemoryGraph::has_node looked up twice for the same fact_id
description: build_graph_context calls graph.has_node(fact_id) at line 138 and again at line 145 to compute component_size. has_node performs a HashMap lookup in node_map each time. On a per-fact batch call path (CLI inspector, bulk explain), the duplication is unnecessary since the first call's result is already known at line 145.
suggested_fix: Cache the bool: `let has_node = graph.has_node(fact_id); let mut neighbor_ids: Vec<i64> = if has_node { graph.connected_component(fact_id).into_iter().filter(|&id| id != fact_id).collect() } else { Vec::new() }; neighbor_ids.sort_unstable(); let component_size = neighbor_ids.len() + usize::from(has_node);`

title: snapshot.scopes cloned just to sort by (depth, id)
description: restore_snapshot_into clones snapshot.scopes (line 213) solely to sort by (depth, id) to satisfy the parent FK ordering. Since snapshot is &EngineSnapshot, in-place sort is not possible on the original — but sorting indices avoids cloning every ScopeNode (each carrying an owned String label). Allocations drop from O(n * (label_len + sizeof(ScopeNode))) to O(n * 8).
suggested_fix: Sort indices instead: `let mut idx: Vec<usize> = (0..snapshot.scopes.len()).collect(); idx.sort_by_key(|&i| (snapshot.scopes[i].depth, snapshot.scopes[i].id)); for &i in &idx { let scope = &snapshot.scopes[i]; stmt.execute(rusqlite::params![scope.id, scope.parent_id, scope.label, scope.depth])?; }`

title: parse_embedding clones JSON Value to satisfy from_value ownership requirement
description: `parse_embedding` calls `serde_json::from_value::<Vec<f32>>(v.clone())` because `from_value` consumes the `Value`. The function takes `&Map<String, Value>` (shared reference), so it cannot move out of the map. For large embeddings (e.g., 1536-dimensional float arrays common with OpenAI models), this clones a JSON array of ~1536 elements before deserializing it into `Vec<f32>`. `args` is owned in `handle_add_fact` (`Map<String, Value>` by value), so the embedding entry can be moved out instead.
suggested_fix: Change `parse_embedding` to accept `&mut Map<String, Value>` and use `args.remove("embedding")` to take ownership of the value, eliminating the clone. Call site: `parse_embedding(&mut args)?` after all preceding `get_*(&args, ...)` reads that don't touch `"embedding"`.

title: path.to_string_lossy() is called N+1 times inside hot open paths instead of being bound once
description: In ConnectionPool::open() the expression &path.to_string_lossy() is evaluated once on line 94 (write connection) and once per read connection inside the loop on line 100 (up to read_pool_size times). In open_read_only() the same pattern repeats at lines 163 and 168. to_string_lossy() allocates a Cow<str> (heap String if the path contains non-UTF-8 bytes, stack Borrowed otherwise) each time. Even in the common UTF-8 case it traverses the OsStr bytes on every call. These are one-time startup allocations so latency impact is negligible for typical pool sizes, but the repetition is needlessly verbose and would become measurable for large read_pool_size values.

title: children HashMap initialized without capacity hint in load() and from_snapshot()
description: In both load() (line 25) and from_snapshot() (line 180), the nodes HashMap is allocated with `HashMap::with_capacity(all.len())` (or snap.nodes.len()), but children is initialized with `HashMap::new()`. For a tree with N nodes, up to N-1 distinct parent IDs may be inserted into children, causing multiple rehash/realloc cycles during construction. The asymmetry is inconsistent: both maps should use with_capacity for the same iteration.
suggested_fix:
In load():
```rust
let mut children: HashMap<i64, Vec<i64>> = HashMap::with_capacity(all.len());
```
In from_snapshot():
```rust
let mut children: HashMap<i64, Vec<i64>> = HashMap::with_capacity(snap.nodes.len());
```

title: String cloned on every upcasting step in the hot loop
description: In `UpcasterRegistry::upcast`, the while loop at line 98 calls `type_key.clone()` on every iteration to construct the HashMap key `(type_key.clone(), rev)`. Since `type_key` is a `String` and the upcaster map is keyed by `(String, u16)`, this allocates a new `String` on each step. For events with long upcasting chains this is wasteful. The `HashMap` could be keyed by `(&str, u16)` (with lifetime on the registry), or the lookup could borrow the existing key.

title: `.expect()` on `serde_json::to_string` for `&[i64]` / `HashSet<i64>` — should propagate as error
description: Multiple sites call `.expect("serialize scope_ids")` or `.expect("serialize exclude_ids")` on `serde_json::to_string(&[i64])` and `serde_json::to_string(&Vec<i64>)`. Serialization of plain integer slices/vecs cannot actually fail, so these never panic in practice. However, using `?` propagation (via `serde_json::to_string(...)? `) is already the established pattern in this codebase (e.g., facts.rs:71, 482). The `.expect` form is inconsistent and would crash the process (rather than returning `MemoryError`) if the invariant ever breaks. These are not panics at risk of triggering, but they are unsound under the library's error handling contract.

title: Nested `if let Some(ref …)` scoring chain in `search_archives` should be flattened
description: Current state: the inner per-fact loop at search.rs:57-100 uses three sequential `if let Some(ref …)` blocks for fact_type filter, text match, and embedding match, plus a trailing `if query.text.is_none() && query.embedding.is_none()` catch-all for the match-all case. This 44-line block spans 3 concepts and requires reading to the end to understand the match-all path. Target state: extract a `fn score_fact(fact: &Fact, query: &MemoryQuery) -> Option<f64>` that returns `Some(score)` when the fact matches, `None` otherwise — the match-all case becomes `Some(1.0)` at the top of the function. The outer loop becomes a flat `filter_map`. Refactoring pattern: Extract Function + Replace Nested Conditionals with Guard Clauses / let-else. Motivation: readability — the match-all fallback at the end is non-obvious; extraction makes testability of scoring logic independent of I/O. Estimated scope: 1 file (search.rs). Prerequisites: none. Risk: low — pure refactor with same observable behaviour; existing tests cover write/read roundtrip but not scoring, so add a unit test for `score_fact` as part of this change.

title: Stderr iterated twice per turn in `keyword_prefilter`: once in `build_searchable_text`, once in `collect_stderr`
description: Inside `keyword_prefilter`'s per-turn loop, three strings are computed from the same `ConversationTurn`: `searchable` (via `build_searchable_text`, which already concatenates user_text + assistant_text + all stderr lowercased), `assistant_lower` (a second lowercasing of `turn.assistant_text`), and `stderr_text` (via `collect_stderr`, which iterates tool_calls again to collect stderr). The assistant text is lowercased twice (once inside `build_searchable_text`, once separately for `assistant_lower`), and stderr is iterated and lowercased twice (once in `build_searchable_text`, once in `collect_stderr`). `check_error_keyword` receives `assistant_lower` and `stderr_lower` separately even though `searchable` already contains both. Current state: 2× stderr iteration + 2× assistant lowercasing per turn. Target state: compute `searchable` once; extract `assistant_lower` and `stderr_text` from it or pass slices. Refactoring pattern: Extract Common Computation / Eliminate Redundant Traversal. Motivation: readability, O(n) allocation reduction per turn. Scope: `src/bootstrap/filter.rs:318-435`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — pure logic refactor, tests cover keyword matching.

title: Three structurally identical `CandidateEpisode` push blocks in `keyword_prefilter` — extract data table
description: The Decision, Convention, and Learning branches (lines 344–383) are structurally identical: call `match_keywords`, check `!is_empty()`, push a `CandidateEpisode` with the category hardcoded. Only the category and keyword table differ. Current state: 3 × 9-line nearly-identical blocks. Target state: a compile-time table `[(EpisodeCategory, &[&str])]` iterated uniformly. Bug has a special-case path for the `"error"` keyword (handled by `check_error_keyword`), so it remains separate. Refactoring pattern: Replace Repetition with Data-Driven Table. Motivation: if a new category is added, the table gets one entry; the loop stays unchanged. Adding a category currently requires duplicating the block and forgetting to update counts. Scope: `src/bootstrap/filter.rs:318-383`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — functionally equivalent, well-covered by tests.

title: `BootstrapReport::merge` is a 30-line manual field-by-field accumulator — fragile under new field addition
description: `BootstrapReport::merge` lists every field explicitly (lines 44–72). The five `usize` scalar fields, three `OutcomeCounts` fields, and four `CategoryCounts` fields are all `+= other.*`. This is correct but brittle: adding a new counter requires updating `merge` in a separate step, and the compiler won't warn if the update is missed (all fields have defaults). The pattern is also duplicated for `OutcomeCounts` (3 fields) and `CategoryCounts` (4 fields). Current state: 30-line explicit merge. Target state: implement `std::ops::AddAssign` for `OutcomeCounts`, `CategoryCounts`, and the `usize`-only projection of `PrewarmMetrics`, then have `merge` delegate. Alternatively, a derive macro or trait-based approach. Motivation: adding a new counter requires exactly one change (the struct field), not two. Scope: `src/bootstrap/metrics.rs`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — pure refactor; all paths covered by the `report_merge` test.

title: Scope resolution block copy-pasted identically in `bootstrap_session` and `bootstrap_directory`
description: Both `MemoryEngine::bootstrap_session` (lines 31–41) and `MemoryEngine::bootstrap_directory` (lines 71–81) contain an identical 10-line `match &config.scope { Some(path) => { ... } None => 1 }` block that resolves a scope path to an `i64` scope_id and updates the scope tree cache. Current state: exact duplication. Target state: extract to a private `fn resolve_scope_for_bootstrap(&self, conn: &Connection, config: &BootstrapConfig) -> Result<i64>` helper. Refactoring pattern: Extract Method. Motivation: DRY; the scope tree update in particular (`self.scope_tree.write().insert(node)`) must not be missed when adding future bootstrap variants. Scope: `src/engine/bootstrap.rs`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: LOW — trivial extract, both call sites identical.

title: Verbatim-duplicate `parse_datetime` function in two command files
description: Current state: `parse_datetime(s: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>, String>` is defined identically in add_fact.rs:72-76 and query.rs:43-47. Both parse RFC 3339 and produce the same error message string. Target state: move the single definition to `output.rs` (or a new `util.rs`) as `pub(crate) fn parse_datetime`, import it in both command files. Refactoring pattern: Extract Method / Consolidate Duplicate Code. Motivation: DRY, single point of change if error wording or date parsing is updated. Scope: 2 files + 1 shared location. Prerequisites: none. Risk: none — purely mechanical.

title: local_dedup exceeds 60 LOC — importance-inheritance block is extractable
description: Current state: `local_dedup` runs 95 lines (dedup.rs:21-115), exceeding the 60 LOC threshold. The importance-inheritance block at lines 92-103 computes `(survivor, loser)` and conditionally updates two importance fields. This block is a distinct concern — 'after expiry, promote survivor importance' — embedded in the middle of the comparison loop. Target state: extract to a private helper `fn inherit_max_importance(survivor_id: i64, loser: &Fact, fact_store: &FactStore<'_>) -> Result<()>`. The inner loop body drops to ~25 LOC and the invariant ('survivor always carries max importance of merged pair') is explicitly named. Refactoring pattern: Extract Method. Motivation: readability, testability (importance inheritance can be unit-tested independently), loop body cognitive complexity. Scope: 1 file. Prerequisites: none. Risk: low.

title: Embedding validation (dimension + NaN/Inf) duplicated in `embed` and `embed_batch`
description: Current state: `embed()` checks `embedding.len() != self.expected_dim` and NaN/Inf (lines 167–178). `embed_batch()` repeats the same two checks in a loop (lines 232–245), with only minor formatting differences. Target state: Extract a private helper `fn validate_embedding(&self, embedding: &[f32], index: Option<usize>) -> Result<(), MemoryError>` that centralises both invariants. Refactoring pattern: Extract Method. Motivation: DRY — adding a new invariant (e.g., L2-norm check, zero-vector check) currently requires two edits. Coupling: self-contained. Risk: trivial. Estimated scope: 1 file.

title: Bootstrap scope-resolution block duplicated twice — ensure_scope_with_conn() already exists
description: Current state: `bootstrap_session()` (lines 34-37) and `bootstrap_directory()` (lines 74-77) each inline a 4-line block: `scope_store.ensure_path(path)?` → `scope_store.get(id)?` → `self.scope_tree.write().insert(node)`. `ensure_scope_with_conn()` in mod.rs:528-534 does exactly this, but bootstrap.rs does not call it. Target state: both bootstrap functions call `self.ensure_scope_with_conn(&conn, path)?`. Refactoring pattern: Inline Duplicate → Extract Existing Helper (the helper already exists). Motivation: readability + coupling — duplicating the 3-step tree-mutation sequence risks the two sites diverging. Estimated scope: bootstrap.rs (1 file). Prerequisites: none. Risk: none — behaviour is identical.

title: HNSW strategy dispatch block duplicated at query() and execute_search_path()
compute_importance called twice per fact — once to classify, once to materialize
description:
Current state: `prune` makes two passes over `active_facts` that both invoke `compute_importance`:
1. Lines 97–107: filter loop calls `compute_importance` per non-pinned fact to build `to_expire`.
2. Lines 114–118: materialization loop calls `compute_importance` *again* for every fact (including pinned ones) to persist the score.

For N active facts this is up to 2N calls to the function. While the function is cheap (a handful of floating-point ops), the duplication makes the code harder to follow — the reader must confirm both calls produce the same result with the same inputs.

Target state: A single pass that scores each fact once, yielding `(fact, score)`, then partitions into `to_expire` (score < min_importance && !pinned) and the full set for materialization.

Refactoring pattern: Merge Loops / Collect-then-Partition.

Motivation: Readability — single source of truth for the score. Coupling — removes the implicit invariant that both calls use identical arguments.

Estimated scope: 1 file (policy.rs lines 97–118). Prerequisites: existing test coverage is solid (5 integration tests). Risk: LOW — output-identical refactor.

title: ensure_node is pub but has zero external callers; should be private
description: Current state: `ensure_node` is declared `pub fn ensure_node(...)` and re-exported via `graph/mod.rs` (`pub use memory_graph::{EdgeData, MemoryGraph}`). The method is only called by `add_edge` (line 59-60) and test code in the same module (lines 277, 313). No call site outside `src/graph/` uses it (confirmed by grep). Publishing a method that returns `NodeIndex` (a petgraph type) leaks the underlying graph representation to any future crate-internal caller who bypasses `node_map`. Target state: demote to `fn ensure_node` (private). Refactoring pattern: Restrict-visibility. Motivation: encapsulation — callers cannot construct stale `NodeIndex` references. Estimated scope: 1 file. Prerequisites: none. Risk: NONE.

title: load_from_db and from_snapshot duplicate identical edge-building loops
description: Current state: `load_from_db` (lines 194-207) and `from_snapshot` (lines 236-248) both iterate a list of edges and call `self.add_edge(source, target, EdgeData { edge_id, relation_type, weight })`. The comment at line 234 explicitly acknowledges the duplication: "Rebuild graph from a snapshot (same logic as `load_from_db`)". Any future change to edge-building logic (e.g. adding a new EdgeData field) must be applied to both sites. Target state: extract a private `fn build_from_edges(edges: impl IntoIterator<Item=(i64, i64, EdgeData)>) -> Self` (or a `fn add_edges_from(&mut self, ...)`) and have both methods delegate to it. Refactoring pattern: Extract-Method. Motivation: DRY / maintainability. Estimated scope: 1 file. Prerequisites: none. Risk: NONE.
