ConnectionPool is pub and forms part of the public API (re-exported from crate::pool), but there are no integration tests that construct a ConnectionPool directly, nor tests that exercise the interaction between a ConnectionPool instance and the schema layer from an external consumer perspective. This means pool-specific invariants (e.g., that read-only pools reject schema-mutating PRAGMAs, that query_only is actually enforced) are only tested inline.

title: open() with backup_dir=Some(...) is not tested in the pool module
description: ConnectionPool::open() accepts an optional backup_dir (line 92) passed to migrate() (line 96). All ten inline tests call open(..., None) for backup_dir. The backup path inside migrate() — which performs a VACUUM INTO before migration — is therefore not exercised by any pool-level test. A regression in the backup-before-migrate path would be invisible at this layer.

title: Cap fields never tested at boundary values 0 or 1
description: ResumeConfig exposes pinned_cap, high_importance_cap, due_cap, and recent_cap. The logic at context.rs:80 (.take(config.pinned_cap)), context.rs:87, context.rs:97, and context.rs:102 all respect these caps. However, no test in src/resume/context.rs or src/engine/tests.rs ever sets any cap to 0 or 1 — the grep for those field names in test files returned zero matches. A cap of 0 should yield an empty tier without panicking; cap=1 should return exactly one fact when multiple exist.

title: No serde roundtrip test for ResumeConfig or ResumeContext
description: Both ResumeConfig (context.rs:11) and ResumeContext (context.rs:44) derive Serialize and Deserialize. The MCP server serializes ResumeContext to JSON for the wire response and the CLI inspector may serialize ResumeConfig. No test verifies that serde_json::from_str(serde_json::to_string(x).unwrap()) == x for either type, leaving silent regressions possible if new fields are added without updating custom Deserialize logic or if chrono's DateTime<Utc> serialization format changes.

title: Public resume_context fn and MemoryEngine::resume_context have no runnable doc-test examples
description: The free function resume_context (context.rs:69) and the facade method MemoryEngine::resume_context (engine/resume.rs:22) each have doc-comments explaining the 5-tier structure and error conditions, but neither carries a /// ```rust example block. The tier structure and the ResumeConfig/ResumeContext types are the primary public API surface of the resume module, making doc-tests the first documentation a consumer reads. Compare with FactStore methods that have more complete documentation.

title: node_count() and max_depth() have zero test coverage
description: grep of the test block (lines 193-365) finds no call to tree.node_count() or tree.max_depth(). These methods are consumed by the inspect/statistics path (src/inspect/statistics.rs:83, 114) and exposed via the CLI stats command (memory-engine-cli/src/commands/stats.rs:73-74). Their correctness is assumed but never asserted in isolation. For example, max_depth() on an empty tree returns 0 (line 136), and on the setup_tree() fixture it should return 2 (depth of project:demo or project:other) — neither is checked.

title: Proptest strategies cover only colon-containing segments and at most 3-depth paths
description: scope_segment() generates '[a-z]{1,8}:[a-z]{1,8}' — every segment contains exactly one colon. Labels without a colon (valid per ScopeStore::validate_label, which only bans empty, leading/trailing whitespace, '/', and >256 bytes) are never generated. scope_path(4) uses 1..4 (exclusive end), capping depth at 3. Edge cases like single-segment paths with no colon (e.g., 'global') or deeply nested (4+ segments) paths are never property-tested. The case count of 32 is also low for two structural properties (line 322).

title: No public item in src/scope/ has a runnable doc-test example
description: Every pub fn in ScopeTree has a /// doc comment but none includes a ```rust code block. The functions are core navigation primitives (resolve_path, ancestors, subtree, inherited, path_for_id) with non-obvious return semantics (e.g., path_for_id returns "/" for root, ancestors returns inclusive leaf-to-root ordering). Doc-tests would serve as living examples and catch API-breaking refactors. Currently `cargo test --doc` produces zero tests from this module.

title: `HnswStrategy::to_snapshot` / `from_snapshot` round-trip semantics not tested
description: `to_snapshot` (line 145) and `from_snapshot` (line 174) are `pub(crate)` and exercised only through `engine::open` / `engine::close` paths. No test in `ann.rs` builds an index, serializes a snapshot, rebuilds from snapshot, and asserts the rebuilt index returns the same top-K for the same query as the original. This is an important property-based candidate: `search(original, q) ≈ search(from_snapshot(to_snapshot(original)), q)`. Feature-gated behind `ann`.
fallback_tier: ann feature-gated — not compiled in default build

title: Proptest for `cosine_similarity` missing anti-parallel property
description: The three proptest properties in `proptest_cosine` cover symmetry, `identical → 1.0`, and `bounded [-1, 1]`. The anti-parallel / negation property — `cosine_similarity(v, -v) = -cosine_similarity(v, v) = -1.0` for nonzero `v` — is missing. The `identical_vectors_equal_one` example test at `vector.rs:149` covers the specific case of a manually chosen opposite vector but the proptest suite should generalize it. The bounded test catches the value being outside `[-1, 1+ε]` but doesn't constrain the exact expected value for `a = -b`.

title: Only doc-example is `rust,ignore` — no compile-checked runnable examples across the public search API
description: The sole doc example in the search module is on `MemoryQuery` at line 17, marked `rust,ignore`, meaning it is not compiled or run as a doctest. Public functions `fts_search`, `vector_search`, `hybrid_search`, `rrf_merge`, and `cosine_similarity` have no runnable doc examples. The `rust,ignore` doc-test is useful for motivation prose but provides no protection against API drift. For pure functions like `rrf_merge` and `cosine_similarity`, a runnable doctest is trivially achievable and serves as both documentation and a compile-check.

title: No fuzz targets for FTS5 query text — untrusted string input path
description: No `fuzz/` directory exists in the workspace. `fts_search` and `fts_count_expired` accept an arbitrary `&str` query that is passed verbatim to SQLite FTS5 MATCH. The FTS5 syntax error path is intentionally swallowed (returns `Ok(vec![])` or `Ok(0)`), but the swallowing logic uses a catch-all `Err(e)` at `fts.rs:67` that would also silently suppress non-FTS5 database errors. A fuzz target exercising arbitrary UTF-8 strings as FTS5 queries would verify the error boundary and guard against future regressions if the error handling is tightened.

title: list_recent test inserts all checkpoints with Utc::now() — ordering non-deterministic
description: The list_recent test (line 198) inserts 5 checkpoints all timestamped Utc::now() in a tight loop. If multiple checkpoints receive identical checkpoint_at values (microsecond resolution on fast CI), the ORDER BY checkpoint_at DESC order is non-deterministic. The test only checks list.len() == 3, so it does not currently fail — but any refactor adding an ordering assertion would produce a flaky test.
suggested_fix: Use deterministic fixed timestamps spaced apart (e.g., Utc::now() + Duration::seconds(i)) when inserting checkpoints in tests. This makes ordering assertions safe to add.

title: Fact type and edge relation type string roundtrips lack proptest coverage
description: The existing proptest_content_hash test in facts.rs verifies content hashing, but the fact_type string encoding (episodic/semantic/procedural) and edge relation_type encoding are not tested as proptest roundtrips. Any change to the string representation would break existing stored data without a failing test.
suggested_fix: Add a proptest that generates arbitrary FactType enum values, converts to string, and verifies parsing back yields the original variant. Also cover the invalid-string path (parse of an unknown string should return an appropriate error or None).

title: build_filter_query dynamic SQL construction lacks fuzz coverage
description: build_filter_query in events.rs constructs SQL strings by appending clauses based on filter fields. Dynamic SQL construction is a classic source of injection and malformed query bugs when field values contain special characters. No fuzz target exercises arbitrary string content in EventFilter fields.
suggested_fix: Add a fuzz target fuzz_event_filter that constructs EventFilter structs with arbitrary string values for event_type, session_id, and source, calls build_filter_query, and executes the resulting prepared statement against an in-memory DB — asserting it never panics and either returns Ok or a structured error.
references: CWE-89: SQL Injection (parameterized queries mitigate but do not eliminate all risks in dynamic query builders)

title: Public store types and key methods lack runnable doc examples
description: FactStore, EventStore, EdgeStore, and SummaryStore have no /// ```rust ... ``` runnable doc examples on their impl blocks or primary methods. The existing doc comments describe errors and panics correctly but do not show usage. This means cargo doc --no-deps produces API reference pages with no executable examples, and cargo test --doc runs zero doctests for the store layer. Doctests serve as both documentation and a lightweight regression test.
suggested_fix: Add a runnable doctest to at least FactStore::insert and EventStore::insert showing minimal setup (Connection::open_in_memory + init_schema) and a round-trip. Use # to hide boilerplate lines. Mark tests that cannot run in isolation with no_run rather than omitting them entirely.

title: no [profile.release] tuning
Doc comment claims partial read but serde_json::from_reader deserializes the whole file
description: The function `peek_embed_dim` at `import.rs:42` is documented as "peek at a JSON snapshot file to extract embed_dim without loading everything", but `serde_json::from_reader(reader)` fully buffers and deserializes the entire file to construct the `SnapshotHeader`. For a multi-gigabyte snapshot this will OOM or take significant time before returning a single integer. The implementation should use a streaming deserializer (`serde_json::Deserializer::from_reader`) to read only the first key-value pair, or the doc comment should be corrected to not promise partial I/O.

title: Insta snapshot test named `schema_v7` but tests current schema (v9)
description: `insta::assert_snapshot!("schema_v7", schema)` at schema.rs:2065 is called after `init_schema` which creates the current v9 schema. The snapshot file is named `memory_engine__store__schema__tests__schema_v7.snap`. The name `v7` does not match the actual schema version tested (v9). This means the snapshot will silently drift whenever the schema version advances but the snapshot name stays at `v7`, and new contributors may misunderstand which version the snapshot covers.
suggested_fix:
Rename the snapshot to match the current schema version:
```rust
insta::assert_snapshot!("schema_v9", schema);
```
And rename the snapshot file accordingly. Update this every time `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` advances.

title: `ArchiveSearchResult` fields are fully `pub` but the struct is never exposed externally
description: Current state: `ArchiveSearchResult` at search.rs:18-22 has all three fields `pub`. The struct is used only in `engine/archive.rs:317` (`search_archives_fallback`) which is `pub(crate)`, and in `search.rs` itself. It is never re-exported from `lib.rs`. Target state: all fields could be `pub(crate)` or left pub with a note, but since the enclosing `mod archive` is `pub(crate)` in `lib.rs:36`, the effective visibility is already crate-private. No external exposure risk exists today, but if the feature visibility is ever changed, blanket `pub` will leak the type. Marking fields `pub(crate)` makes intent explicit. Refactoring pattern: Reduce Visibility. Motivation: encapsulation intent clarity. Estimated scope: 1 file. Prerequisites: none. Risk: none (purely additive restriction on already-unreachable public surface).

title: use rusqlite::OptionalExtension placed at end of file after all function definitions
description: Current state: `use rusqlite::OptionalExtension;` is the last line of activity.rs (line 247), placed after all impl methods and helper functions. Idiomatic Rust groups all `use` declarations at the top of the module. This import was likely added at the call site during a refactor and never moved. Target state: move to the top-level use block (lines 3-16). Refactoring pattern: Move Import. Motivation: readability — IDE tools and reviewers expect imports at the top; a trailing import is easily missed in review. Estimated scope: activity.rs (1 line move). Prerequisites: none. Risk: none.
suggested_fix: Move `use rusqlite::OptionalExtension;` from line 247 to the import block at the top of activity.rs (after line 16).

title: CO_SESSION_* constants are pub(super) but used only within graph.rs
description: Current state: `CO_SESSION_RELATION` (line 15), `CO_SESSION_WEIGHT` (line 20), and `CO_SESSION_SCOPE_ID` (line 22) are declared `pub(super)`, making them visible to the entire `engine` module. All 8 usage sites are within graph.rs itself — none appear in sibling modules. Target state: no visibility qualifier (file-private constants, or `const` inside the `impl MemoryEngine` block where they are used). Refactoring pattern: Reduce Visibility. Motivation: API surface — over-broad visibility signals these constants are part of an inter-module contract when they are not. Estimated scope: graph.rs (1 file). Prerequisites: grep confirms no other file in src/engine/ uses CO_SESSION_*. Risk: none.
suggested_fix: Remove `pub(super)` from the three CO_SESSION_* constants in graph.rs:15-22. They become file-private (the Rust default for module-level items without a visibility modifier).

title: promote_with_lineage() contains use declarations inside the function body
description: Current state: `promote_with_lineage()` (lines 143-231) opens with three `use` statements inside the function body: `use crate::error::MemoryError`, `use crate::store::lineage::LineageStore`, and `use crate::types::{NewFact, NewLineageRecord}`. These are module-level concerns placed at function scope. Target state: move to the top of cognitive.rs's import block. Refactoring pattern: Move Import. Motivation: readability — function-body imports obscure the function's logic and violate Rust convention. Estimated scope: cognitive.rs (trivial move). Prerequisites: check for name collisions with existing module-level imports. Risk: none.
suggested_fix: Move the three use declarations from inside promote_with_lineage() to the top-level import section of src/engine/cognitive.rs.

title: UpcasterFn is a bare fn pointer — stateful upcasters (e.g. needing a schema version map) are impossible
description: Current state: `pub type UpcasterFn = fn(serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value>` (line 6). Bare function pointers cannot capture environment. If a future upcaster needs to reference external state (e.g. a lookup table, a schema registry, a connection) it cannot be expressed as a bare fn. Target state: `pub type UpcasterFn = Box<dyn Fn(serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value> + Send + Sync>`. This is a breaking change to the registration API but enables stateful upcasters. The HashMap value type and clone semantics would need adjustment (Arc instead of Clone). Refactoring pattern: Replace Function Pointer with Closure. Motivation: extensibility. Estimated scope: upcaster.rs + all register_upcaster call sites. Risk: medium — API-breaking, affects UpcasterRegistry::clone impl.

title: `PrewarmMetrics` doc cites opaque acronyms `R3` and `APC` with no expansion
description: The doc comment for `PrewarmMetrics` reads: "Pre-warming quality metrics (R3, APC).". `APC` refers to Agentic Plan Caching (arXiv:2506.14852), documented in `docs/ROADMAP.md`, but `R3` is an internal review-round label (from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-10-ann-hnsw-implementation.md`), not a paper or external reference. Neither acronym is expanded or linked in the doc comment. Library consumers reading rustdoc have no way to resolve these abbreviations.

title: "NeuroStack" used as a proper noun in public-facing doc comments without definition or link
description: The module-level doc (`filter.rs:1`) and the `keyword_prefilter` doc (`filter.rs:313`) both reference "NeuroStack" (e.g., "NeuroStack keyword pre-filter", "Apply NeuroStack keyword patterns"). This is a community-research concept mentioned once in `docs/reference/mcp-server.md`, but the term is unexplained and unlinked in the source. Consumers reading generated rustdoc cannot understand what it means.

title: Comment references closed GitHub issue #11
description: The comment `// Global summaries are intentionally root-scoped (scope_id=1). ... See issue #11.` points to GitHub issue #11 ("docs: document global summary scope_id=1 invariant") which is now closed. The design rationale is already fully expressed in the surrounding comment, making the issue reference redundant and misleading — readers may try to follow a dead link or assume the issue is still tracking a pending task.

title: Duplicate `mod archive` declaration visible in source (known blocker, context only)
description: Lines 48-49 and 51-52 both declare `#[cfg(feature = "archive")] mod archive;`. This is documented as a known blocker. Recorded here as context only — do not re-report as new.
suggested_fix: Remove one of the two identical `#[cfg(feature = "archive")] mod archive;` blocks (keep lines 48-49, delete lines 51-52).

title: Constant name `*_NORMALIZATION_CEILING` stores `n+1`, not `n` — doc comment is ambiguous
description: `FREQUENCY_NORMALIZATION_CEILING = 101.0` and `CONNECTIVITY_NORMALIZATION_CEILING = 51.0` hold the values `max_count + 1` (so that `ln_1p(max_count) / ceiling.ln() == 1.0`). The doc comments read "Normalization ceiling for access frequency: ln(100+1). 100 accesses = full score." The phrase "ln(100+1)" describes the formula applied at the call site, not the value stored, creating ambiguity. A reader scanning the constant alone may expect `CEILING = 100` (the semantic ceiling), not `101` (the `+1` offset). The math is correct; only the communication is ambiguous.

title: Module doc describes MemoryGraph as 'knowledge graph' but struct doc calls it entity/relation graph; isolated-node behavior undocumented
description: The module-level doc (mod.rs:1) says 'In-memory knowledge graph backed by petgraph, loaded from SQLite edge table.' The struct doc (memory_graph.rs:22-25) says 'mirroring the active edges in SQLite' and 'The graph only contains active (non-expired) edges.' Neither doc mentions that isolated nodes (nodes with no edges) CAN exist — ensure_node can be called directly and add_edge creates nodes as a side effect even if they later lose all edges after remove_edge_by_id. The to_snapshot doc (line 212) correctly notes 'No isolated nodes — matches load_from_db semantics (edges only)' indicating a discrepancy: the live graph may contain isolated nodes that the snapshot will silently drop, causing a divergence between the live MemoryGraph state and the state reconstructed from a snapshot. This is undocumented on the MemoryGraph struct itself.

title: `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `embed_dim` field and getter references closed issue #108
description: Both the `embed_dim: usize` struct field (line 23-24) and the `embed_dim()` getter method (lines 228-229) are annotated with `#[allow(dead_code)]` and the comment 'complete pool API — used after #108 engine split'. Issue #108 ('engine.rs God Module') is closed — the split already happened. In the current codebase `MemoryEngine` holds its own `embed_dim: usize` field (engine/mod.rs:102) and reads it directly (engine/mod.rs:559-561); `async_engine.rs:397` calls `self.inner.embed_dim()` on `MemoryEngine`, not on `ConnectionPool`. The pool's `embed_dim()` getter is exercised only by the pool's own unit test (connection_pool.rs:305-308). The `#[allow(dead_code)]` suppresses a valid compiler signal. The pool field can be dropped once callers that need the value read it from `MemoryEngine` instead, or the allow can be retained with an updated comment if the field is intentionally kept for a future API contract.

title: root_id() is missing #[must_use] — inconsistent with node_count and max_depth
description: `node_count` (line 128) and `max_depth` (line 134) both carry `#[must_use]`. `root_id` is a pure computation with no side effects, so it should as well. The inconsistency means the compiler cannot warn callers who call `tree.root_id()` without using the result.

title: Proptest scope_segment generates only colon-namespaced labels — plain-word labels never exercised
description: The `scope_segment()` strategy generates strings matching `[a-z]{1,8}:[a-z]{1,8}`, so all proptest-generated scope paths look like `"abc:def/gh:ijk"`. Labels without a colon (plain words), labels with digits, or longer labels are never generated. The `resolve_roundtrip` and `ancestors_always_end_at_root` property tests only witness a narrow label alphabet. This does not affect production correctness, but a label like `"session-42"` or `"tenant_prod"` could surface edge cases in `resolve_path` or `path_for_id` that the current proptest misses.
suggested_fix:
Broaden `scope_segment()` to cover a wider label space, e.g.:
```rust
fn scope_segment() -> impl Strategy<Value = String> {
    "[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,30}".prop_map(|s| s)
}
```
This exercises plain-word labels, digit-prefixed labels, and common separator characters while remaining consistent with what `validate_label` accepts.

title: `SearchMode` enum variants have no doc comments on a public type
description: `SearchMode` is a public type exported from the crate root (via `mod.rs:15`). Its variants `Fts`, `Vector`, and `Hybrid` carry no doc comments. Consumers cannot determine from `rustdoc` what each variant does without reading the source or the `SearchQuery` context. This is a low-friction omission on a core query-control type.

title: Comment describes a use import as a re-export
description: The comment at line 239 reads `/// Re-export for use by rusqlite::Connection::query_row.` followed by `use rusqlite::OptionalExtension;`. This is a private trait import used inside the module, not a `pub use` re-export. The comment is misleading and may confuse readers looking for the module's public API surface.

title: Payload-free `CrudDecision` enum should derive `Copy`, eliminating forced `.clone()` at callsites
description: `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum CrudDecision { Add, Update, Delete, Noop }` has no payload — `Copy` is trivially sound. Consumer arbiters and internal code are forced to `.clone()` the decision unnecessarily. Adding `Copy` also enables matching on a moved value after-the-fact without cloning.
suggested_fix:
Add `Copy` and `Hash` to the derive list:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum CrudDecision { Add, Update, Delete, Noop }
```

Then audit for `.clone()` calls on `CrudDecision` values and remove them.

title: choices.get(0) should use choices.first() per Clippy get_first lint
description: `choices.get(0)` is flagged by the Clippy `clippy::get_first` lint (enabled via `#![warn(clippy::nursery)]` in the workspace). The idiomatic Rust equivalent is `choices.first()`, which is clearer and the lint-preferred form. This codebase targets `clippy::all = deny` + pedantic/nursery warnings, so this will produce a build warning under `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`.
suggested_fix: Replace `choices.get(0)` with `choices.first()` at line 109.

title: Proptest scope_segment() uses a no-op identity prop_map
description: scope_segment() (line 314) calls `.prop_map(|s| s)` which is an identity transform — it passes the generated String through unchanged, adding zero value. This is dead code in the test that subtly implies a transformation exists when none does.

title: root_id() is a non-const method returning a compile-time constant
description: root_id() returns the literal 1 but is declared as a regular method taking &self, forcing callers to hold a ScopeTree reference just to obtain a constant. This prevents use in const/static contexts and match arms, and the value is already duplicated as a literal 1i64 on line 45 and line 151 (and in engine/mod.rs line 670). An associated constant would be DRY, const-propagable, and usable everywhere without a self borrow.

title: Manual body truncation (1000-char limit) is a hand-rolled snippet with no test
description: Current state: `let truncated = if body_str.len() > 1000 { format!("{}... (truncated)", &body_str[..1000]) } else { body_str };` — manual UTF-8 boundary-unsafe slice (slicing a `String` at a byte offset can panic on multi-byte characters at position 1000). Target state: Use `body_str.get(..1000).map_or(body_str.as_str(), |s| s)` or the `truncate_str` pattern to avoid the panic. Refactoring pattern: Replace unsafe slice with safe indexing. Motivation: correctness (panic on valid UTF-8 multi-byte boundary), readability. Risk: low but real crash potential on non-ASCII error bodies. Estimated scope: 1 line.

title: serde(default) fields reviewed: defaults are benign, no value-injection risk (CWE-502)
description: Audited the serde(default) attributes on the in-scope types for default-value injection on untrusted deserialization. Event.origin_node_id defaults to "local" (types.rs:100,116-118), Event.sequence_id defaults to 0 (types.rs:103), Event.event_revision defaults to 1 (types.rs:108,112-114), Fact.surfaced_at defaults to None (types.rs:140), PromotionProvenance.lineage_id is skip_serializing + default 0 and is explicitly reconstructed from the DB PK on read (types.rs:217-218, doc 204-205). None of these defaults gate a security decision, grant elevated trust, or silently widen scope on missing input; a snapshot omitting them yields safe, documented values. Reported as INFO to record that this class was examined and found clean, not as a defect.
suggested_fix: No change required. Keep this behavior; if any of these fields later become security-relevant (e.g. origin_node_id used for cross-node trust), revisit whether a missing value should hard-error instead of defaulting.

title: main_db_bytes = page_count * page_size is an unchecked i64 product (defense-in-depth only)
description: main_db_bytes: page_count * page_size (statistics.rs:120) multiplies two i64 PRAGMA values with no checked_mul. In release mode Rust wraps on overflow, so a wrapped product would report a wrong (possibly negative) DB size. This is NOT reachable in practice: SQLite caps page_size at 65536 and page_count at ~2^32, bounding the product to ~2^48, four orders of magnitude below i64::MAX. Reported as info/defense-in-depth, not an exploitable condition. CWE-190 (integer overflow) in form only.
suggested_fix:
Use a checked/saturating product to make the invariant explicit and silence release-mode wrapping:

main_db_bytes: page_count.saturating_mul(page_size),

title: Brute-force vector scan materializes one result entry per active fact before truncation
description: `vector_search` streams every active fact (`t_expired IS NULL`) from SQLite, deserializes each embedding, and pushes a `VectorResult` into the `scored` Vec for ALL matching rows BEFORE any `limit` truncation (the partial-sort/truncate at lines 80-87 happens only after the full scan). The `limit` argument does not bound the size of the intermediate `scored` allocation. The same pattern drives the deserialized `embedding` Vec per row. This is O(active facts) work and O(active facts) peak memory (16 bytes/entry for `scored`, plus a transient per-row `Vec<f32>`), independent of how small `limit` is. This is inherent to brute-force semantics and is the documented reason for the ANN threshold (src/search/strategy.rs:99-119), and the blast radius is bounded by data the consumer itself wrote to the store (data-at-rest), not by a single untrusted request payload -- so it is informational rather than an exploitable request-amplified DoS. Flagged only so the bound is explicit: a query with a tiny `limit` still pays full-scan cost on a large store. CWE-400/CWE-770 in the weak sense (resource use scales with store size, not with the requested result count).
suggested_fix: No mechanical fix; this is a design property of brute-force scan. If a hard ceiling on per-query work is desired, wire the documented `SearchConfig::ann_threshold` dispatch (currently not wired into the engine, per src/search/strategy.rs:82-83) so large stores transparently fall back to the bounded-candidate HNSW path, or push a `LIMIT` into SQL only when no scoring/reranking over the full set is required.

title: Source-fact-ID list interpolated into IN(...) via format! instead of bound json_each
description: LineageStore::insert builds an existence-check query by string-joining the source fact IDs directly into the SQL text: `unique_ids.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect().join(",")` then `format!("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM facts WHERE id IN ({placeholders})")`. Because the elements are `i64`, their `Display` output is digits and an optional leading `-` only, so this is NOT injectable and not currently exploitable. It is flagged as defense-in-depth / consistency: every other ID-array query in this module binds the array through `json_each(?N)` (facts.rs:353, 485, 660, 695; edges.rs:237; activities.rs:164) rather than interpolating it. By contrast, the `LIMIT {n}`/`LIMIT {n}` cases elsewhere (facts.rs:138, activities.rs:122-130) are intentionally NOT flagged: they interpolate a single integer (digits-only Display) which is the idiomatic safe pattern; the discriminating criterion is that lineage diverges from the codebase's own established `json_each(?N)` convention for ID *arrays*, not merely that it uses format!. CWE-89 (informational).
suggested_fix: Match the existing convention: `let ids_json = serde_json::to_string(&unique_ids.iter().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>())?;` then `let count: i64 = self.conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM facts WHERE id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?1))", params![ids_json], |r| r.get(0))?;`

title: VACUUM INTO backup path built by string formatting with manual quote escaping
description: backup_before_migration constructs `let escaped = backup_path.to_string_lossy().replace('\'', "''"); let sql = format!("VACUUM INTO '{escaped}'");` and runs it via execute_batch. SQLite's `VACUUM INTO` does not accept bound parameters for the destination path, so a string literal is unavoidable here, and the `' -> ''` transform is the canonical SQLite string-literal escape, so this is correct and not exploitable as written. The `backup_dir` is supplied by the library caller (migration orchestration), not by external/untrusted input, further lowering risk. Reported as informational because the audit scope explicitly asks about format!-built SQL: the residual concern is that the safety relies entirely on the manual escape being complete (it is, for SQLite single-quote literals) and on the path never being attacker-controlled. The in-code comment already documents the SQLite constraint. CWE-89 (informational, defense-in-depth).
suggested_fix: Optionally harden by validating/normalizing backup_dir to a trusted base directory before formatting, and add a unit test asserting a path containing a single quote round-trips correctly. A fuller (design-level) alternative is to use rusqlite's online backup API (Connection::backup) which takes the destination as a value rather than SQL text, removing the string-built query entirely; this is a judgement call, not a mechanical change.

title: `tempfile` listed in both `[dependencies]` and `[dev-dependencies]`
description: `tempfile = "3"` appears in `[dependencies]` (line 24, needed by `src/engine/snapshot.rs:182` for atomic snapshot writes) and redundantly in `[dev-dependencies]` (line 37). Cargo uses the `[dependencies]` entry for both production and test builds when a crate is already in `[dependencies]`, making the `[dev-dependencies]` entry a no-op that adds confusion. Current state: duplicated. Target state: remove from `[dev-dependencies]`. Refactoring pattern: Remove Redundant Dependency. Motivation: clarity, no accidental version skew. Scope: `Cargo.toml`. Prerequisites: none. Risk: NONE.
suggested_fix: Remove `tempfile = "3"` from the `[dev-dependencies]` section (line 37). The entry in `[dependencies]` is sufficient.

title: `OutcomeSignals` always discarded in the production pipeline — useful only in tests
description: `outcome::classify_outcome` returns `(SessionOutcome, OutcomeSignals)`. In the only production call site (`bootstrap_within_savepoint`, line 158) the signals are silently discarded with `_signals`. `OutcomeSignals` is re-exported at the crate root (`mod.rs:28`) and included in `lib.rs:49` re-exports, signalling it is part of the public API. But no external consumer currently uses it, and it is not stored anywhere. This is not a bug — the signals are available for future logging, tracing, or reporting — but the `_` binding in the production pipeline is a potential documentation gap: someone reading `bootstrap_within_savepoint` has no indication why signals are computed but unused. A `tracing::trace!` or a `#[cfg(feature = "tracing-signals")]` gate would make the intent clear. Current state: signals computed and silently dropped. Suggested improvement: add a `tracing::debug!` log of the signals before dropping, which also makes them observable in production without requiring a public API change.

title: use rusqlite::OptionalExtension placed after impl block — non-idiomatic import placement
description: Current state: `use rusqlite::OptionalExtension;` appears at line 240, after the `impl ActivityStore` block ends. Rust imports (`use`) are conventionally grouped at the top of the file, before any definitions. This placement makes it easy to miss when auditing imports. Target state: move the `use` to the top of the file with the other `rusqlite` imports. Refactoring pattern: Reorganize Imports. Motivation: readability, convention. Estimated scope: 1 line, activities.rs. Risk: zero.

title: 11 duplicate transitive dep versions
archive tests run only under --features archive; combinations with ann and async are never exercised in CI
description: tests/archive_test.rs is fully gated behind #![cfg(feature = "archive")] (line 1). The Cargo.toml defines the feature matrix: archive = [compress-zstd], ann (HNSW vector search), async (tokio), compress-gzip, compress-zstd. There are no tests for archive + ann (where archive search could interact with HNSW-backed facts) or archive + async (where the async engine wraps the sync engine). A default cargo test run never compiles or runs any archive code. The CLAUDE.md mentions cargo test --all-features but does not call this out explicitly as the gate for archive coverage.
suggested_fix: Add a CI step (or document in CLAUDE.md) that explicitly runs cargo test --features archive and cargo test --features archive,ann to ensure cross-feature correctness. The archive + async combination should be tested once async integration tests exist.

title: parse_datetime is duplicated across two modules with no inline unit test in either
description: The identical parse_datetime function appears in both query.rs:43-47 and add_fact.rs:72-76. Neither has an inline unit test; coverage is only incidental via CLI integration tests (query_valid_at_invalid_format_fails and add_fact_invalid_datetime). The duplication means a future divergence would be undetected. This is both a testing gap and a DRY issue.

title: All public consolidation functions lack doc-test examples
description: The four public functions — `consolidate`, `local_dedup`, `cluster_fusion`, `global_integration` — have well-written doc-comments but no `///` code-fence examples. The codebase already has proptest examples in `search/` modules showing a culture of thorough test documentation. Without runnable doc examples, a consumer of this API has no executable demonstration of the primary usage pattern. The `consolidate` function in particular has non-obvious semantics (sentinel return, watermark side-effect, transaction scope) that a doc-test could illustrate.
suggested_fix: Add `/// # Examples` sections with `/// ``` rust` fences to `local_dedup` and `consolidate` at minimum. For `local_dedup`, a minimal runnable example would show: open an in-memory DB, init schema, insert two near-duplicate facts via `FactStore`, call `local_dedup`, and assert the returned count. Use `# use memory_engine::...;` lines to keep the example concise.

title: pub use policy::prune has no doc-test; prune docstring only describes errors
description: The module-level `pub use policy::prune` re-exports `prune` as the sole public symbol of the forgetting module. The doc comment on `prune` (lines 70-81 in policy.rs) describes the algorithm and error conditions but contains no `/// # Examples` block with a runnable doc-test. Since the forgetting module is `pub(crate)` (lib.rs:39), `prune` is not exposed to external consumers, so a missing doc-test has no impact on crate users. However, the two other public-within-crate functions (`ebbinghaus_decay`, `compute_importance`) also lack doc-test examples despite having mathematically precise doc comments. For a library targeting AI agent builders who may inspect source, concrete examples aid understanding.

title: Public API functions lack runnable doc-test examples
description: all_tool_definitions() (tools/mod.rs:30), dispatch() (tools/mod.rs:377), and config::probe_embed_dim (config.rs:88) are the three functions most likely to be called by downstream consumers or integration scripts, yet none has a /// runnable example. The existing doc comments on probe_embed_dim describe error conditions but provide no example illustrating how to call it. Without doc-tests, example code in comments can silently become wrong as the API evolves.
